Short Description: A comforting Filipino stir-fry of ground pork, potatoes, and carrots in a savory-sweet tomato and soy sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g ground pork
- 1 medium potato, diced
- 1 medium carrot, diced
- 1/4 cup green peas
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
3. Add ground pork and cook, breaking it apart, until browned.
4. Pour in soy sauce and water, then simmer for 10 minutes.
5. Add potato and carrot, and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
6. Stir in green peas and cook for 2 more minutes.
7. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A hearty Filipino stew of pork and liver with potatoes, carrots, and bell peppers in a rich tomato sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g pork shoulder, cubed
- 1/4 cup pork liver, cubed
- 1 medium potato, cubed
- 1 medium carrot, cubed
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1/3 cup tomato sauce
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/3 cup water
- 1 1/4 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Bay leaf
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and fry potatoes and carrots until lightly browned; set aside.
2. In the same pot, sauté garlic and onion until soft.
3. Add pork and cook until browned on all sides.
4. Pour in tomato sauce, water, and bay leaf, then simmer for 20 minutes until pork is tender.
5. Add liver and cook for 3 minutes.
6. Return the fried potatoes and carrots to the pot, along with bell pepper.
7. Simmer for another 5 minutes, season with salt and pepper, then serve.

Short Description: Tender braised pork belly simmered in soy sauce, vinegar, and pineapple juice for a sweet-savory glaze.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 240 g pork belly, sliced
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1/4 cup pineapple juice
- 1 clove garlic, crushed
- 1 onion, sliced
- 1 1/4 tbsp brown sugar
- 3/4 tbsp black beans (tausi)
- 1 dried bay leaf
- 1/4 cup water
- 3/4 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Marinate pork belly in soy sauce and vinegar for 15 minutes.
2. Heat oil in a pot and sear pork until lightly browned; set aside marinade.
3. Sauté garlic and onion in the same pot until fragrant.
4. Return pork to the pot along with the reserved marinade, pineapple juice, bay leaves, and water.
5. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 30 minutes until pork is tender.
6. Stir in brown sugar and black beans, then simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to thicken the sauce.
7. Season with salt and pepper, then serve with steamed rice.

Short Description: Thick slices of pork belly marinated in calamansi and soy sauce, then grilled until charred and juicy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Marinating Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 300 g pork belly (liempo), sliced thick
- 1/4 cup calamansi juice
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1/2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Combine calamansi juice, soy sauce, garlic, black pepper, and brown sugar in a bowl.
2. Marinate pork belly in the mixture for at least 20 minutes.
3. Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat and brush with oil.
4. Grill pork slices for 5-7 minutes per side, basting with leftover marinade, until cooked through and charred at the edges.
5. Rest for 2 minutes, then slice and serve with rice and spiced vinegar.

Short Description: A fiery Bicolano dish of pork simmered in coconut milk with shrimp paste and green chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g pork belly, sliced thin
- 1 cups coconut milk
- 1/4 cup bagoong alamang (shrimp paste)
- 2-4 green finger chilies, sliced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb ginger, minced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
2. Add pork belly and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in bagoong and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
5. Cook uncovered for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until pork is tender and sauce thickens.
6. Add chilies and simmer for 5 more minutes.
7. Season with salt if needed, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A quick sauté of canned sardines with bitter melon, garlic, and onion for a budget-friendly breakfast or lunch.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 can (155g) sardines in tomato sauce
- 1 medium ampalaya (bitter gourd), sliced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 2/3 cup water
- 1 1/3 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until softened.
2. Add sardines and simmer for 3 minutes, breaking them up slightly.
3. Pour in water and bring to a boil.
4. Add ampalaya slices and simmer for 8-10 minutes until tender.
5. Season with salt and pepper, then serve with rice.

Short Description: Tilapia gently simmered in creamy coconut milk with ginger, chilies, and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium tilapia, cleaned
- 1 cups coconut milk
- 1 thumb ginger, julienned
- 1 onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 long green chilies
- 1/2 cup spinach or malunggay leaves
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
2. Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
3. Add tilapia and green chilies, and simmer for 10-12 minutes, spooning sauce over the fish occasionally.
4. Add spinach or malunggay leaves and simmer for 2 more minutes.
5. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.

Short Description: Squid cooked adobo-style in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic, often with its own ink for a deeper flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g squid, cleaned and sliced into rings (reserve ink sacs)
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1/2 tbsp cooking oil
- 1/2 tsp sugar (optional)
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add squid and cook briefly for 1-2 minutes.
3. Pour in vinegar and let it boil uncovered for 2 minutes without stirring.
4. Add soy sauce, bay leaf, and black pepper, then stir gently.
5. Mix in the reserved squid ink and simmer for 8-10 minutes until squid is tender and sauce darkens.
6. Add sugar if using, adjust seasoning, then serve with rice.

Short Description: Thin slices of beef marinated in soy sauce and calamansi, pan-seared and topped with sweet caramelized onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g beef sirloin, thinly sliced
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup calamansi juice
- 1 large onion, sliced into rings
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 1/2 tbsp cooking oil
- 1/2 cup water
Steps:
1. Marinate beef slices in soy sauce, calamansi juice, and black pepper for 15 minutes.
2. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic until golden.
3. Sear marinated beef in batches until browned; set aside marinade.
4. Add the reserved marinade and water to the pan, and simmer for 10 minutes until beef is tender.
5. Return beef to the pan and top with onion rings.
6. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until onions soften slightly, then serve hot.

Short Description: A rich Filipino beef stew simmered with vegetables in a savory-sweet, slightly tangy sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g beef chuck, cubed
- 1 cups coconut milk
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb ginger, minced
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
2. Add beef and cook until browned on all sides.
3. Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
4. Pour in water and lemongrass, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 30 minutes until beef is tender.
5. Add coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
6. Season with salt, remove lemongrass, then serve with rice.

Short Description: A Filipino rice plate topped with sautéed ground meat, fried banana, and a sunny-side-up egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g ground beef
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1/4 cup raisins
- 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 eggs, fried sunny-side up
- 1 ripe saba bananas, sliced and fried
- 2 cups cooked rice
- 1 1/2 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
3. Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart.
4. Stir in soy sauce and raisins, then simmer for 8-10 minutes.
5. Season with salt and pepper.
6. Plate rice with the beef mixture, a fried egg, and fried banana slices on the side.

Short Description: A rich and savory Filipino favorite with tender chicken in a soy-vinegar sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 400 g chicken thighs and legs
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 1/4 cup water
- 1/2 tbsp cooking oil
- 1/2 tsp sugar (optional)
Steps:
1. Combine chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot and let marinate for 10 minutes.
2. Place the pot over medium heat and bring to a boil without stirring.
3. Reduce heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
4. Remove chicken and set aside; reduce the sauce for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
5. Heat oil in a separate pan and pan-fry chicken pieces until lightly browned.
6. Return chicken to the sauce, add sugar if using, and simmer for 2 minutes before serving.

Short Description: A light, comforting chicken soup with ginger, green papaya, and leafy greens.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 400 g chicken, cut into pieces
- 1 chayote (sayote), sliced
- 1 cups malunggay or spinach leaves
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 1/2 cups water or rice washing (hugas bigas)
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
2. Add chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned.
3. Pour in fish sauce and water, then bring to a boil.
4. Simmer covered for 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
5. Add chayote and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
6. Stir in malunggay or spinach leaves and simmer for 2 minutes before serving hot.

Short Description: A classic Ilocano vegetable stew of squash, eggplant, and string beans seasoned with shrimp paste.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small squash (kalabasa), cubed
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 1 bundle string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1 bitter gourd (ampalaya), sliced
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp bagoong alamang (shrimp paste)
- 1/4 cup water
- 50 g pork belly, sliced thin (optional)
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
2. If using pork, add it now and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in bagoong and cook for 1 minute.
4. Add squash and water, cover, and cook for 8 minutes until squash starts to soften.
5. Add string beans, eggplant, and bitter gourd, then cook covered for 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender but not mushy.
6. Adjust seasoning if needed, then serve with rice.

Short Description: Chicken pieces marinated in a sweet and savory sauce, grilled and brushed with a sticky glaze.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 400 g chicken thighs, cut into serving pieces
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup calamansi juice
- 1/4 cup banana ketchup
- 1 1/2 tbsp brown sugar
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- Bamboo skewers
- 1 tbsp cooking oil for basting
Steps:
1. Combine soy sauce, calamansi juice, banana ketchup, brown sugar, garlic, and black pepper in a bowl.
2. Marinate chicken pieces in the mixture for at least 30 minutes, reserving some marinade for basting.
3. Thread chicken onto skewers.
4. Grill over medium heat for 8-10 minutes per side, basting with reserved marinade and oil, until cooked through and lightly charred.
5. Serve hot with steamed or java rice.

Short Description: Soft, tender eggplant cooked in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic for a simple vegetable adobo.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 Chinese eggplants (long, thin variety), cut into 3-inch pieces and halved lengthwise
- 3 tbsp cooking oil
- 3 cloves garlic, chopped
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp vinegar
- 2 tbsp water
- 1/2 tsp brown sugar
- 1 dried bay leaf
- 1/4 tsp cracked black pepper
Steps:
1. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the eggplant pieces in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly browned and tender. Set aside.
2. In the same pan, heat the remaining oil and sauté garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Pour in soy sauce and water, then add black pepper and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
4. Add vinegar and let it boil undisturbed for 1 minute without stirring.
5. Stir in brown sugar and simmer for 2 minutes.
6. Return the fried eggplant to the pan and gently toss to coat with the sauce.
7. Simmer for 2 minutes until the eggplant absorbs the sauce, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A cool, refreshing salad of juicy cucumbers, tomatoes, and onions in a light vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cucumber, diced
- 6 grape or cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/2 small red onion, chopped
- 1 stalk green onion, chopped
- 1 tbsp vinegar
- 1/2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/4 tsp sugar
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Pinch of ground black pepper
Steps:
1. In a bowl, combine salt, sugar, and black pepper, then mix well.
2. Add vinegar and olive oil, and stir until the dressing is well combined.
3. Add cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and green onion to the bowl.
4. Toss until the vegetables are evenly coated with the dressing.
5. Serve immediately alongside grilled or fried dishes.

Short Description: A creamy chicken and macaroni soup with vegetables, perfect for rainy days and merienda.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/3 medium onion, diced
- 170g boneless, skinless chicken breast, diced
- 1 1/3 cups chicken broth
- 2/3 cup elbow macaroni
- 1/4 cup celery, chopped
- 1/4 cup carrots, diced
- 1/4 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup fresh or evaporated milk
- 1/3 cup water
- Salt and ground black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Melt butter in a pot over medium heat.
2. Add onion and cook until softened.
3. Add chicken and cook for 3-5 minutes until no longer pink. Season with salt and pepper.
4. Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
5. Add water and milk, bring back to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
6. Add elbow macaroni and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
7. Add carrots and celery, and simmer for 3 minutes.
8. Stir in cabbage and cook for 2 more minutes.
9. Turn off heat and serve hot.

Short Description: A golden, flaky pastry filled with seasoned chicken and vegetables, baked or fried until crisp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 6 empanada wrappers (store-bought or homemade)
- 150g ground chicken
- 1 small potato, diced small
- 1/4 cup carrots, diced small
- 1/4 cup raisins
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp tomato sauce
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 egg, beaten (for sealing and egg wash)
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Oil for frying
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add ground chicken and cook until browned.
3. Stir in potato and carrots, then add tomato sauce and soy sauce.
4. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender and mixture thickens.
5. Add raisins, season with salt and pepper, then let the filling cool.
6. Spoon filling onto each wrapper, brush edges with beaten egg, fold over, and crimp to seal.
7. Fry empanadas in hot oil until golden brown on both sides, then drain and serve.

Short Description: Soft, fluffy steamed buns filled with sweet-savory braised pork in a thick asado sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Resting Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 tsp instant yeast
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 cup warm water
- 1/2 tbsp cooking oil
- 150g pork shoulder, cubed
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Simmer pork in soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, onion, garlic, and water for 30 minutes until tender.
2. Shred or dice the pork finely and thicken the sauce with the cornstarch mixture, then set the filling aside to cool.
3. Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and warm water to form a dough; knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
4. Cover and let the dough rise for 45 minutes until doubled in size.
5. Punch down the dough, divide into small rounds, and flatten each into a circle.
6. Place filling in the center of each round, gather the edges, and twist to seal.
7. Steam the buns for 15-18 minutes over simmering water until puffed and cooked through.

Short Description: Soft, lightly sweet Filipino bread rolls coated in fine breadcrumbs, best eaten fresh and warm.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Rising and Resting Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 3/4 cup warm milk
- 2 tbsp butter, softened
- 1 egg
- 1/2 cup fine breadcrumbs (for coating)
Steps:
1. Combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt in a bowl.
2. Add warm milk, egg, and butter, then mix and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
3. Cover and let the dough rise for 1 hour until doubled in size.
4. Punch down the dough and shape into a log, then cut into small equal pieces.
5. Roll each piece in breadcrumbs and place on a baking tray, leaving space between pieces.
6. Let rest for 20 minutes, then bake at 190°C (375°F) for 15-18 minutes until golden brown.

Short Description: A creamy baked pasta layered with sweet meat sauce and melted cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150g elbow macaroni
- 150g ground beef or ground pork
- 1/2 cup tomato sauce
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 2 tbsp butter
- 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 1/4 cup grated parmesan cheese (for topping)
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Cook macaroni according to package instructions, then drain and set aside.
2. Sauté garlic and onion in a pan, then add ground meat and cook until browned.
3. Stir in tomato sauce and simmer for 10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
4. In a separate pot, melt butter, whisk in flour, then gradually add evaporated milk to make a white sauce.
5. Combine the meat sauce, white sauce, and cooked macaroni in a baking dish, then top with cheddar and parmesan cheese.
6. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

Short Description: A Filipino meatloaf with ground pork, raisins, and vegetables, steamed or baked and sliced.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 250g ground pork
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
- 2 tbsp raisins
- 2 tbsp diced carrots
- 2 tbsp diced pickle relish
- 1 hard-boiled egg, sliced
- 1 hotdog or Vienna sausage, sliced lengthwise
- 2 tbsp evaporated milk
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Aluminum foil
Steps:
1. Combine ground pork, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, raisins, carrots, and pickle relish in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
2. Lay out a sheet of foil and spread half of the mixture into a rectangle.
3. Arrange hard-boiled egg slices and hotdog down the center, then top with the remaining mixture, shaping it into a log.
4. Roll tightly in foil, twisting the ends to seal.
5. Steam the log for 40-45 minutes until firm and cooked through.
6. Let cool slightly, then unwrap, slice, and serve.

Short Description: A creamy custard pie with a golden, flaky crust and a silky egg-and-milk filling.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Chilling Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 1 pre-made pie crust (or 3/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup butter, pinch of salt, 2 tbsp cold water for homemade)
- 2 eggs
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 1/4 cup condensed milk
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
Steps:
1. If making the crust from scratch, combine flour, butter, and salt until crumbly, then add cold water and form into a dough. Chill for 15 minutes.
2. Roll out the dough and press into a small pie pan, trimming the edges.
3. Whisk together eggs, evaporated milk, condensed milk, sugar, and vanilla until smooth.
4. Pour the filling into the pie crust.
5. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30-35 minutes until the filling is set and the top is lightly golden.
6. Let cool before slicing and serving.

Short Description: Soft crepe-style wrappers filled with fresh vegetables and topped with a sweet garlic peanut sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4 fresh lumpia wrappers or crepes
- 100g pork, thinly sliced (optional)
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 cup carrots, julienned
- 1/4 cup green beans, sliced thin
- 1/4 cup tofu, cubed and fried (optional)
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
- 1/4 cup crushed peanuts (for garnish)
- 1/2 cup water
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, then add pork if using and cook until lightly browned.
2. Add cabbage, carrots, and green beans, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
3. Season with soy sauce, then add tofu if using and set the vegetable filling aside.
4. In a separate small pot, combine water, brown sugar, and a splash of soy sauce, then thicken with the cornstarch slurry to make the sauce.
5. Lay a wrapper flat, place a portion of the vegetable filling near one edge, then roll tightly.
6. Drizzle the sauce over the rolls and top with crushed peanuts before serving.

Short Description: A Filipino ground meat dish sautéed with potatoes, tomatoes, and raisins for a sweet-savory finish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250g ground beef or ground pork
- 1 small potato, diced small
- 1 small carrot, diced small
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1 cup water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and tomato until softened.
2. Add ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it apart.
3. Add potato and carrot, then pour in water.
4. Simmer for 12-15 minutes until vegetables are tender and the mixture thickens slightly.
5. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Tender marinated beef skewers grilled until smoky, juicy, and full of flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 300g beef sirloin, cubed
- 1/2 red bell pepper, cut into chunks
- 1/2 green bell pepper, cut into chunks
- 1/2 onion, cut into chunks
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice or lemon juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- Bamboo skewers, soaked in water
Steps:
1. Combine soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic, oil, and black pepper in a bowl, then marinate beef for at least 15 minutes.
2. Thread beef, bell peppers, and onion alternately onto skewers.
3. Grill or pan-sear the skewers over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until beef reaches desired doneness.
4. Baste with leftover marinade while cooking.
5. Serve hot with rice or as an appetizer.

Short Description: A mild, creamy Filipino-style chicken curry with potatoes and carrots in a spiced coconut sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 400g chicken, cut into pieces
- 1 small potato, cubed
- 1/2 carrot, sliced
- 1/4 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb ginger, minced
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
2. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
4. Add potato, water, and fish sauce, then simmer for 15 minutes until chicken is nearly cooked.
5. Pour in coconut milk and add carrot and bell pepper, then simmer for 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
6. Season with salt, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A colorful Filipino stir-fry of mixed vegetables and meat in a light, savory sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 100g pork or chicken, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup cauliflower florets
- 1/2 cup carrots, sliced
- 1/2 cup cabbage, chopped
- 1/4 cup snow peas
- 1/4 cup baby corn
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 onion, sliced
- 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add pork or chicken and cook until lightly browned.
3. Pour in chicken broth and oyster sauce, then bring to a simmer.
4. Add carrots and cauliflower first, cooking for 3 minutes, then add cabbage, snow peas, and baby corn.
5. Cook for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
6. Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce, season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately.

Short Description: Pan-fried pork chops marinated in soy sauce and calamansi, topped with sautéed onion rings.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pork chops, sliced thin
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 onion, sliced into rings
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Marinate pork chops in soy sauce, calamansi juice, and black pepper for 15 minutes.
2. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic until golden.
3. Sear the marinated pork chops until browned on both sides; set aside the marinade.
4. Pour the reserved marinade and water into the pan, and simmer for 8-10 minutes until pork is tender.
5. Return pork to the pan, top with onion rings, and simmer for 3 minutes until onions soften.
6. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A flavorful Chinese-Filipino fried rice with shrimp, pork, egg, and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked rice, preferably day-old
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1/4 cup Chinese sausage (lap cheong) or ham, diced
- 1/4 cup shrimp, chopped (optional)
- 1/4 cup green peas
- 1/4 cup carrots, diced small
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 stalk green onion, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok and scramble the eggs until just set, then set aside.
2. Heat the remaining oil and sauté garlic until fragrant.
3. Add Chinese sausage or ham, and shrimp if using, and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Add carrots and green peas, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
5. Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
6. Return the scrambled egg to the wok, season with soy sauce, salt, and pepper, and toss well.
7. Garnish with green onion and serve hot.

Short Description: A smooth, silky caramel custard made with egg yolks and milk, a Filipino party staple.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 50 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: At least 2 hours
Ingredients:
- 4 egg yolks
- 1/2 cup condensed milk
- 1/4 cup evaporated milk
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar (for caramel)
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. In a small pan, melt sugar with water over low heat until it turns amber-colored caramel, then pour into a llanera or small heatproof mold.
2. Whisk together egg yolks, condensed milk, evaporated milk, and vanilla until smooth, straining to remove bubbles.
3. Pour the egg mixture gently over the caramel in the mold.
4. Cover the mold with foil and steam over simmering water for 30-35 minutes until set.
5. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
6. Run a knife around the edges and invert onto a plate to serve, letting the caramel sauce flow over the flan.

Short Description: A rich Filipino stew in a thick peanut sauce, served with sautéed vegetables and shrimp paste.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 300g beef (oxtail or tripe), cut into chunks
- 1/4 cup ground peanuts or peanut butter
- 2 tbsp ground toasted rice
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 1/2 bundle string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/4 banana heart, sliced (optional)
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups water or beef broth
- 2 tbsp annatto (achuete) water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Bagoong alamang (shrimp paste), for serving
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Boil beef in water until very tender, about 45-60 minutes, reserving the broth.
2. In a pot, heat oil and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
3. Add the cooked beef and annatto water, then pour in the reserved broth.
4. Stir in ground peanuts and toasted rice powder, and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
5. Add eggplant, string beans, and banana heart, and cook for 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
6. Season with salt, then serve hot with bagoong on the side.

Short Description: Pork ribs and vegetables in a sour, tamarind-flavored broth, a Filipino comfort-food favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 300g pork ribs or pork belly, cubed
- 1 packet (20g) sinigang sa sampalok mix, or 1/4 cup tamarind pulp
- 1 small radish, sliced
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 1 tomato, quartered
- 1/2 bundle string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1 cup kangkong (water spinach) leaves
- 1/4 onion, quartered
- 3 cups water
- Fish sauce to taste
- 1-2 green finger chilies (optional)
Steps:
1. Boil pork with onion and tomato in water for 30 minutes until tender, skimming off scum as needed.
2. Add radish and simmer for 5 minutes.
3. Stir in the sinigang mix or tamarind pulp, then add eggplant and string beans.
4. Simmer for 8 minutes until vegetables are tender.
5. Add kangkong leaves and chilies, and cook for 2 minutes.
6. Season with fish sauce to taste, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A festive beef roll stuffed with sausage, cheese, and egg, simmered in a savory tomato sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 300g beef flank steak, pounded thin
- 1 hotdog or sausage, halved lengthwise
- 2 hard-boiled eggs, halved
- 1/4 cup carrots, cut into strips
- 1/4 cup pickle relish or sliced pickles
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup tomato sauce
- 1 cup water or beef broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Kitchen twine
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Marinate the flattened beef in soy sauce and calamansi juice for 15 minutes.
2. Lay the beef flat and arrange hotdog, egg, carrot strips, and pickles along the center.
3. Roll the beef tightly around the filling and tie with kitchen twine to secure.
4. Heat oil in a pot and sear the beef roll on all sides until browned.
5. Sauté garlic and onion in the same pot, then add tomato sauce and broth.
6. Return the beef roll to the pot, cover, and simmer for 50-60 minutes until tender, turning occasionally.
7. Remove twine, slice into rounds, and serve with the sauce spooned over.

Short Description: A festive, savory-sweet Filipino rice dish cooked with meat, vegetables, and turmeric.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice (malagkit), rinsed
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 100g chicken, diced
- 50g Chinese sausage or chorizo, sliced
- 1/4 cup raisins
- 1/4 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp annatto (achuete) water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add chicken and sausage, and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in annatto water, then add the rinsed glutinous rice and mix to coat.
4. Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth, and bring to a boil.
5. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is tender.
6. Stir in raisins and bell pepper, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 3 more minutes before serving.

Short Description: A rolled and roasted pork belly stuffed with herbs, with crackling skin and juicy, flavorful meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours
Ingredients:
- 600g pork belly, butterflied
- 4 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Kitchen twine
Steps:
1. Season the inside of the pork belly with garlic, lemongrass, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
2. Roll the pork belly tightly and tie with kitchen twine at even intervals.
3. Rub the outside of the roll with oil and additional salt.
4. Roast in an oven at 160°C (320°F) for 1 hour 30 minutes, then increase temperature to 220°C (425°F) for a final 15-20 minutes to crisp the skin.
5. Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
6. Serve with lechon sauce or spiced vinegar on the side.

Short Description: A creamy, sweet macaroni salad with fruit, ham, and cheese, a must-have on the holiday table.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150g elbow macaroni
- 1/4 cup ham, diced
- 1/4 cup cheddar cheese, diced
- 1/4 cup pineapple tidbits, drained
- 1/4 cup raisins
- 1/3 cup mayonnaise
- 2 tbsp condensed milk
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Cook macaroni according to package instructions, then drain and let cool completely.
2. In a large bowl, combine ham, cheese, pineapple, and raisins.
3. Add the cooled macaroni to the bowl.
4. Stir in mayonnaise and condensed milk until well combined.
5. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
6. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.

Short Description: Deep-fried pork belly with crackling skin and juicy meat, served with liver sauce or vinegar dip.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Chilling Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 500g pork belly, whole slab
- 4 cups water
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- Cooking oil for deep frying
Steps:
1. Boil pork belly with water, garlic, bay leaf, salt, and peppercorns for 45 minutes until tender.
2. Remove the pork and let it air-dry, uncovered, in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to dry the skin.
3. Heat oil in a deep pan or pot until very hot.
4. Carefully deep-fry the pork belly until the skin is golden, crisp, and blistered, about 8-10 minutes, turning as needed.
5. Drain on paper towels, then chop into serving pieces.
6. Serve with spiced vinegar or lechon sauce.

Short Description: Tilapia cooked with wine and aromatics for a savory dish with a gentle tipsy kick.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 medium tilapia, cleaned and scored
- 1/4 cup white wine or gin
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 tomato, sliced
- 1 onion, sliced
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup cornstarch (for dusting)
- Cooking oil for frying
Steps:
1. Marinate tilapia in wine, garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper for 15 minutes.
2. Stuff the cavity of each fish with tomato and onion slices.
3. Dust the fish lightly with cornstarch.
4. Heat oil in a pan and fry the fish for 4-5 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
5. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with rice.

Recipe Name: Ensaladang Dilis (Tomato and Onion Salad with Dried Anchovies)
Short Description: A simple tomato and onion salad topped with crunchy dried anchovies for a salty, tangy bite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup dried anchovies (dilis)
- 2 medium tomatoes, chopped
- 1/2 red onion, chopped
- 1 tbsp vinegar
- 1/2 tbsp cooking oil (for frying anchovies)
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Fry the dried anchovies in a small amount of oil until crisp, then drain and let cool.
2. In a bowl, combine tomatoes and red onion.
3. Add vinegar, salt, and pepper, then toss gently.
4. Top the salad with the fried anchovies just before serving.

Short Description: A bold bitter melon salad with tomatoes, onions, and egg in a tangy vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium ampalaya (bitter gourd), thinly sliced
- 1 tsp salt (for rubbing)
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1/4 red onion, chopped
- 1 tbsp vinegar
- 1/2 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 hard-boiled egg, sliced (optional)
Steps:
1. Rub the sliced ampalaya with salt and let sit for 10 minutes to reduce bitterness, then rinse and squeeze out excess liquid.
2. In a bowl, combine ampalaya, tomato, and red onion.
3. Add vinegar and fish sauce, then toss well.
4. Top with sliced hard-boiled egg if using, and serve chilled or at room temperature.

Short Description: A sweet and tangy pickle of shredded green papaya, carrots, and bell peppers.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Pickling Time: 1 day
Overall Time: 1 day and 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small green papaya, julienned
- 1/4 carrot, julienned
- 1 tbsp salt (for salting papaya)
- 1/2 cup white vinegar
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 red bell pepper, julienned
- 1 small piece ginger, julienned
- 2 cloves garlic, sliced
- 1/4 tsp whole peppercorns
Steps:
1. Sprinkle papaya and carrot with salt and let sit for 20 minutes, then rinse and squeeze out excess water.
2. In a saucepan, combine vinegar and sugar and heat gently until sugar dissolves; let cool.
3. Pack papaya, carrot, bell pepper, ginger, garlic, and peppercorns into a clean jar.
4. Pour the cooled vinegar mixture over the vegetables until fully submerged.
5. Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 1 day before serving to let the flavors develop.

Recipe Name: Ginataang Talong with Malunggay and Tofu
Short Description: Eggplant, moringa leaves, and tofu simmered in creamy coconut milk for a mild vegetable dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium eggplant, sliced
- 1/2 cup tofu, cubed and fried
- 1 cup malunggay leaves
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
2. Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
3. Add eggplant and fried tofu, then simmer for 8-10 minutes until eggplant is tender.
4. Stir in malunggay leaves and cook for 2 more minutes.
5. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A simple Filipino breakfast staple of rice fried with plenty of crispy golden garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked rice, preferably day-old
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and add garlic.
2. Fry garlic slowly until golden and crisp, then remove half for garnish, leaving the rest and the oil in the pan.
3. Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until heated through and lightly toasted.
4. Season with salt, then top with the reserved crispy garlic before serving.

Short Description: A rich, savory pork stew cooked in blood with a tangy hint of vinegar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 300g pork belly or pork ears, cubed
- 1 cup pork blood
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1/4 onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1-2 green finger chilies
- 1 cup water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
3. Pour in water and simmer for 20 minutes until pork is tender.
4. Stir in pork blood and cook, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens, about 8-10 minutes.
5. Add vinegar and chilies, and simmer for 5 minutes without stirring too much at first to let the sourness cook off.
6. Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with rice or puto.

Short Description: Pork trotters slow-cooked in vinegar, soy sauce, and spices until fork-tender.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 pork hock (pata), cut into chunks
- 1/3 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 2 bay leaves
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 2 cups water
- 1/4 cup banana blossom or dried banana peel (panutsa alternative, optional)
- 1 tsp whole peppercorns
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Combine pork hock, water, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot and bring to a boil.
2. Simmer covered for 1 hour until the pork is tender, adding more water if needed.
3. Add soy sauce and vinegar, and simmer for 10 minutes without stirring.
4. Stir in brown sugar and continue simmering for 10-15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
5. Adjust seasoning with salt if needed, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Crispy fried fish topped with a sweet and sour sauce of ginger, carrots, and bell peppers.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 whole Lapu-Lapu (2–3 pounds)
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Oil, for frying
- 1 onion, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb-sized piece of ginger, julienned
- 1/2 small green papaya, peeled and grated
- 1 small red bell pepper, cut into strips
- 1 small green bell pepper, cut into strips
- 1 cup vinegar
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp ketchup
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
Steps:
1. Clean and gut the fish. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
2. In a wide pan over medium heat, heat about 2 inches of oil. Add the fish and cook, turning once or twice, until golden, crisp, and cooked through. Remove from the heat, drain on paper towels, and keep warm.
3. In a pan over medium heat, heat about 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the onions, garlic, and ginger and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened.
4. Add the grated papaya and bell peppers and cook, stirring regularly, until tender yet crisp. Remove from the pan and keep warm.
5. In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the vinegar, sugar, and ketchup.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil.
7. In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch and water. Stir until smooth. Add to the pan and continue to cook, whisking continuously, for about 1 to 2 minutes or until the sauce thickens.
8. Place the fried fish on a serving platter and garnish with the vegetable mixture. When ready to serve, pour the sweet and sour sauce on top.

Short Description: Tilapia stuffed with tomatoes and onions, then deep-fried until the skin is crisp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 whole tilapia, scaled and gutted
- 1 1/2 tbsp tamarind base powder
- 1 large Roma tomato, diced
- 1/2 medium onion, peeled and chopped
- 1/2 thumb-size ginger, peeled and minced
- 1 clove garlic, peeled and minced
- 1 tbsp butter, melted
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Calamansi juice, to taste
- Soy sauce, to taste
Steps:
1. Preheat the oven to 375°F.
2. Rinse the tilapia well, including the cavities, and pat dry. Make two or three slits across the body of each fish on both sides.
3. Rub the fish all over, including the cavity, with 1 tablespoon of the tamarind base powder. Let stand for about 10 minutes.
4. In a bowl, combine the tomato, onion, ginger, garlic, the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of tamarind powder, and salt and pepper to taste. Stir to distribute.
5. Stuff the cavity of the fish with the tomato-onion mixture.
6. Liberally brush the outside of the fish with the melted butter. Wrap the fish individually in aluminum foil, then double-wrap to prevent the juices from leaking.
7. Place the fish packet on a baking sheet. Bake in the oven for about 20–25 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through.
8. Combine calamansi juice and soy sauce to taste to make the dipping sauce.
9. Serve the baked fish hot with the dipping sauce.

Short Description: Mussels folded into a fluffy egg omelet with onions, a quick and affordable favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 eggs
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp oil
- 1 shallot, peeled and chopped
- 1 clove garlic, peeled and minced
- 1 large Roma tomato, chopped
- 1/2 cup mussel meat, cooked and removed from shell
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 2 tbsp green onions, chopped
Steps:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. In a bowl, combine the eggs and salt and pepper to taste. Beat the eggs until frothy, then set aside.
3. In a skillet over medium heat, heat the oil. Add the shallot and garlic and cook until softened.
4. Add the tomatoes and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until softened.
5. Add the mussels and cook for about 1 to 2 minutes.
6. Add the oyster sauce and stir to combine.
7. Add the beaten eggs, swirling the pan to fully disperse the eggs over the mussels.
8. Sprinkle the green onions on top.
9. Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes, or until the eggs begin to set at the edges but are still wet in the middle.
10. Transfer the pan to the oven. Continue to cook for about 8 to 10 minutes, or until the eggs are completely set.
11. Remove from the heat and cut into wedges to serve.

Short Description: A hearty boiled soup of meat, corn, and vegetables in a clear, savory broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours 40 minutes
Overall Time: 3 hours
Ingredients:
- 1/4 pound beef shanks
- 1/4 pound pork belly
- 1/4 pound chicken legs and thighs
- 1/4 pound ham
- 1/2 chorizo de Bilbao
- 1/4 large onion, peeled and quartered
- 1/4 teaspoon peppercorns
- 1/2 tablespoon fish sauce
- 1/2 ear corn on the cob, shucked and cut into thirds
- 1/2 large potato, peeled and quartered
- 2 1/2 pieces green beans, ends trimmed
- 1/2 Maggi chicken cube
- Green onions, ends trimmed and cut into 4-inch lengths
- 1/4 medium cabbage, quartered
- Salt and pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. In a large pot, combine beef shanks and water. Bring to a boil for about 10 minutes, skimming scum that floats. Drain and rinse the beef and the pot well.
2. Place blanched beef and enough cold water to cover it about 2 inches in the pot. Bring to a boil, skimming any foam that arises. Cover, lower heat, and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes or until the beef is half done.
3. Add pork belly and continue to simmer for about 15 to 20 minutes.
4. Add chicken, ham, and chorizo. Add white onions, peppercorns, and fish sauce. Continue to simmer, occasionally skimming the froth that floats, for about 30 to 40 minutes or until beef, pork, and chicken are cooked and fork-tender.
5. Add green onions. Add corn and cook for about 5 minutes.
6. Add potatoes. Cook until half tender.
7. Add cabbage and green beans and cook until tender.
8. Sprinkle Maggi chicken cubes. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Cook for another 5 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.

Short Description: A creamy Filipino-style macaroni salad with chicken, pineapple, raisins, and cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3/4 cup uncooked elbow macaroni
- 75 g boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh meat
- 1 small carrot, peeled and diced (use about 1/4 of it)
- 2 tablespoons ham, cubed
- 1 hard-boiled egg, peeled and coarsely chopped
- 1/4 cup crushed pineapple, including a little packing juice
- 2 tablespoons cheese, cubed
- 1 tablespoon sweet pickle relish (or atchara)
- 2 tablespoons raisins
- 2 tablespoons onion, peeled and diced
- 1/4 cup mayonnaise
- 1 tablespoon sweetened condensed milk
- Salt and pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. In a pot over medium heat, bring about 4 quarts salted water to a boil. Add macaroni and cook according to package directions for about 8 to 9 minutes or until firm to bite. Drain well and allow to cool completely.
2. In a pot, add chicken meat and enough water to cover. Bring the water to a boil, skimming scum that floats on top. Lower heat, cover, and simmer for about 15 to 20 minutes or until cooked through. Drain from the liquid, allow to completely cool and shred. Set aside.
3. In a pot, bring water to a boil. Add diced carrots and cook for about 30 seconds. With a slotted spoon, remove from water and plunge into an ice bath until completely cool. Drain and set aside.
4. In a large bowl, combine macaroni, chicken, carrots, ham, eggs, crushed pineapple including packing juice, cheese, sweet pickle relish, raisins, onions, mayonnaise, and sweetened condensed milk. Gently stir together until evenly distributed.
5. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Refrigerate for about 1 hour to cool completely and to allow flavors to meld.

Short Description: Taro leaves slowly simmered in rich coconut milk with chilies and savory shrimp paste.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2/3 ounce dried gabi leaves
- 2/3 lemongrass stalk
- 1 teaspoon oil
- 1/3 onion, peeled and chopped
- 1 1/3 cloves garlic, peeled and minced
- 1/3 thumb-size ginger, peeled and minced
- 1/3 pound pork belly, diced
- Pepper, to taste
- 1 teaspoon shrimp paste
- 1 1/3 cups coconut milk
- 2 2/3 chili peppers, chopped
- 1/3 cup coconut cream
- Salt, to taste
Steps:
1. Go through the dried leaves, and shred into pieces. Inspect for any other stray leaves accidentally mixed in during the drying process and discard.
2. Remove and discard the dark green layers of the lemongrass until you get to the lighter green part. Using the back of a knife, pound ends of stalks to release flavor and then chop.
3. In a wide pan over medium heat, heat oil. Add onions, garlic, and ginger and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and aromatic.
4. Add pork and cook until lightly browned. Season with pepper to taste.
5. Add shrimp paste and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 1 to 2 minutes.
6. Add coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
7. Add lemongrass and chili peppers.
8. Add gabi leaves and with the spoon, push down into the liquid until moistened. Do not stir for the first 15 to 20 minutes.
9. Lower heat, cover, and cook for about 25 to 30 minutes or until pork is fully cooked and leaves have softened.
10. Add coconut cream and continue to cook for about 10 to 15 minutes or until almost dry and begins to render fat.
11. Season with salt to taste. Serve hot.

Short Description: A quick breakfast or lunch of corned beef sautéed with garlic, onion, and potatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 1/2 large potato, peeled and diced
- 1/2 onion, peeled and chopped
- 1 clove garlic, peeled and minced
- 1/2 can (5.75 ounces) chunky-style corned beef
- 1/4 cup water
- Salt and pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. In a skillet over medium heat, heat about 1 tablespoon of oil.
2. Add potatoes and cook until lightly browned.
3. Add onions and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened.
4. Add corned beef and water and bring to a boil, breaking meat into smaller pieces.
5. Cover, lower heat, and cook for about 3 to 5 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

Short Description: A comforting mung bean stew simmered in coconut milk, often served for breakfast or merienda.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/3 cup green mung beans
- 1/3 cup glutinous rice
- 2/3 cup coconut milk
- 1/3 cup coconut cream
- 2/3 cup water, or more as needed
- 1/4 cup sugar, adjusted to taste
Steps:
1. Wash and rinse glutinous rice. Set aside.
2. In a skillet over medium heat, toast the mung beans until they turn brown and produce a nutty roasted aroma.
3. Transfer the roasted mung beans to a tray or any flat surface and roll a rolling pin through the beans to crack them open. You can also use a food processor to pulse them just several times to crack, but do not pulverize them. Run the cracked mung beans through a coarse sieve to remove some of the pulverized skins.
4. In a pot over medium heat, bring coconut milk and 1/3 cup of water to a simmer. Add the glutinous rice and roasted mung beans. Cover the pot and lower the heat to low once it starts to simmer again. Cook for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until the rice and mung beans have expanded and softened. You may need to add more water until this is achieved, but not so much as we want all liquids to be almost absorbed once it is cooked.
5. Add the sugar and half of the coconut cream. Stir and cook for another 5 minutes.
6. Turn off the heat and transfer to individual bowls. Top with some of the remaining coconut cream. Can be served warm or cold.

Short Description: A light, comforting corn soup with shrimp or fish and leafy greens.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces white young corn
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 1/2 medium onion, sliced
- 1 1/2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 1/2 cups water
- 1 tablespoon fish sauce
- 1/4 pound shrimp, peeled and deveined
- Salt, to taste
- 1/2 bunch chili leaves, about 1/4 cup
Steps:
1. Slice off the kernels on one of the corn cobs, then grate the remaining corn. Set aside.
2. In a pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Sauté the garlic and onion until limp and aromatic.
3. Add the fish sauce and shrimp. Cook until the shrimp changes color.
4. Add the water and bring to a boil.
5. Add the corn kernels and grated corn. Stir until well dispersed. Cook until the soup is thick and the corn is cooked through. Season with salt if needed.
6. Add the chili leaves and let simmer for 1 minute.
7. Serve while still hot.

Short Description: String beans cooked adobo-style in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 2 tablespoons garlic, minced coarsely
- 1/2 medium onion, chopped
- 1/4 pound pork belly, cut into thin strips
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/8 teaspoon coarse ground pepper
- 1/2 cup water
- 3 cups yardlong beans (sitaw), ends trimmed and cut into 3-inch pieces
Steps:
1. In a deep pan or wok over medium heat, add oil and 1 1/2 tablespoons minced garlic. Cook, stirring from time to time, until the garlic turns golden. Remove from oil and set aside.
2. In the same oil, add the pork belly strips and sear for several minutes until fat is rendered and the meat turns golden brown.
3. Push the pork strips to the sides and add the onion and remaining 1/2 tablespoon minced garlic. Cook until limp and aromatic.
4. Add the soy sauce, vinegar, pepper, and water and bring to a boil. Cover the pan or wok and let it cook for 15–20 minutes or until the pork belly strips are tender and the liquid has been reduced a bit.
5. Add the yardlong beans and cook for another 3 minutes or until the desired tenderness is achieved. Remove from heat and transfer to a serving plate.
6. Top with the roasted garlic and serve as a side dish with your favorite fried meat or on its own with steamed rice.

Short Description: Unripe mango pickled in a sweet and sour brine, a perfect tangy side or snack.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 almost ripe mango, Carabao/Manila
- 3 tablespoons distilled white vinegar
- 3 tablespoons water
- 3 tablespoons sugar
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 2 1/2 pieces whole peppercorns
- 1/4 piece hot chili, chopped, optional
Steps:
1. Sterilize glass jars for storing: Place the jars in a pot with water enough to cover them. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and let it gently boil for 10 minutes. Remove the jars from the hot water using tongs and then dip the lids for 10 seconds. Tip the jars and lids over a cooling rack and allow to air dry.
2. In a non-reactive pan or pot, combine the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and cloves, if using. Bring to a boil over high heat. Lower the heat and let it simmer for 3 minutes, making sure the sugar and salt are completely dissolved. Remove from heat and let it cool down.
3. While waiting, prepare the mango. Wash and peel the mango. Hold the mango stem-side up, then cut vertically on both sides along the wide side of the seed to separate the cheeks. Then do the short sides as well to leave just the seed.
4. Cut the cheeks into slices about 1-cm thick. Rinse and drain the mango slices. Arrange the slices inside the sterilized jar, filling it with mangoes as much as you can. If you prefer it spicy, add the chili to the jar with the mangoes.
5. Pour enough of the pickling liquid to cover the mangoes. Close the jar with the lid.
6. Let them sit in a cool place for a minimum of 1–2 days. You can also refrigerate them. Longer pickling time will let the flavor seep in better, although the mango will stay crisp and crunchy for several weeks only.
7. Serve to accompany fried dishes or enjoy as a snack.

Short Description: Crispy fried dried danggit, salty and crunchy, usually served with garlic rice and vinegar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 package dried danggit
- 2 tablespoons oil
Steps:
1. Transfer package from freezer to fridge to thaw. It doesn’t take long. I don’t normally thaw them, as long as I am able to separate them apart then I’m ready to fry.
2. Heat oil over medium or medium to low heat.
3. Fry each side for about 2 minutes. Then raise heat to crisp danggit. This is quick, maybe a few seconds.
4. Remove from heat.

Short Description: Pork simmered in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- ½ kilo pork belly, cut into pieces
- 4 cloves garlic, crushed
- 2–3 dried bay leaves
- ¼ cup soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons vinegar
- 1½ teaspoons whole peppercorns
- 1 cup water (240 ml)
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Combine the pork belly, soy sauce, and crushed garlic in a bowl. Mix well and marinate for at least 1 hour.
2. Heat a pot over medium heat. Add the marinated pork and cook for a few minutes until lightly browned.
3. Pour the remaining marinade, including the garlic, into the pot.
4. Add the water, whole peppercorns, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the pork is tender.
5. Add the vinegar and simmer for another 12–15 minutes.
6. Add salt to taste, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Chicken adobo simmered in creamy coconut milk for a rich, savory, and mildly tangy sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 pieces chicken, cut into serving pieces
- 1 cup coconut milk
- half piece Chicken Cube
- 1/4 cup white vinegar
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 3 cloves garlic
- 2.5 pieces dried bay leaves
- 1 teaspoon whole peppercorn
- 1.5 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
Heat oil in a pan.
Crush the garlic, and then saute until it starts to brown.
Fry the chicken for 1 to 1 ½ minutes per side.
Pour soy sauce and vinegar. Cover the pan. Let boil. Flip the chicken pieces afterwards. Continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Add whole peppercorn and bay leaves. Pour coconut milk. Stir and then let the mixture boil.
Add Knorr Chicken Cube. Stir and cover the pan. Adjust heat to low. Cook for 20 minutes.
Remove the cover and continue to cook until sauce reduces to desired amount.
Serve with warm rice. Share and enjoy!

Short Description: A white-style pork adobo cooked in vinegar, garlic, and salt for a clean, sharp flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small slab pork belly, cut into serving pieces
- 2 teaspoons oil
- 1/3 onion, peeled and sliced thinly
- 1/3 head garlic, peeled and minced
- 1/3 cup vinegar
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/3 teaspoon cracked peppercorns
- 1/3 teaspoon sugar
- Fried garlic bits (optional)
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
2. Add onions and garlic and cook until softened and aromatic.
3. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
4. Add vinegar and bring to a boil, uncovered and without stirring, for about 3 to 5 minutes.
5. Add water, salt, bay leaf, and peppercorns. Stir and boil for another 3 to 5 minutes.
6. Lower the heat, cover, and cook for about 40 to 50 minutes or until the pork is fork-tender and the liquid is reduced.
7. Add sugar and stir. Continue cooking uncovered until the mixture begins to render fat.
8. Sprinkle with fried garlic bits if desired and serve hot.

Short Description: A golden pork adobo colored with turmeric for a fragrant, mildly spiced variation.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3–4 pieces pork, sliced
- 1/4 cup white vinegar
- 1/2 small yellow onion, minced
- 1/2 knob turmeric, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 2 dried bay leaves
- 1/2 piece pork or beef cube or 1 teaspoon beef powder
- 1/4 teaspoon granulated white sugar
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 teaspoon peppercorn
- 1.5 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat the cooking oil in a cooking pot.
2. Put in the garlic and cook until the color turns light brown.
3. Add the onion. Cook for 1 minute.
4. Put in the sliced turmeric, peppercorn, and bay leaves. Cook for 10 to 15 seconds.
5. Add the pork slices. Cook while stirring once in a while until the pork turns light brown, about 5 minutes.
6. Put in the pork or beef cube (or powder) and pour in the water. Let boil.
7. Cover the pot and simmer for 30 to 45 minutes. Add additional water as necessary.
8. Pour in the vinegar. Allow the liquid to re-boil.
9. Stir and then add the sugar. Cook for 1 minute more.
10. Transfer to a serving plate.
11. Serve and enjoy.

Short Description: Beef braised in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic until fork-tender in a rich adobo sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 35 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons vinegar
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- A pinch of salt
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 small bay leaf
- 3–4 whole peppercorns
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- 1 small tomato, for garnish
Steps:
1. Combine the beef, vinegar, soy sauce, minced garlic, salt, sugar, ground black pepper, bay leaf, and whole peppercorns in a saucepan. Marinate for 30 minutes.
2. Cover the saucepan and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour, or until the beef is tender.
3. Drain the beef, reserving the sauce. Set the beef aside.
4. Heat the cooking oil in a skillet and brown the beef on all sides.
5. Transfer the beef to a serving dish and pour off the excess oil from the skillet.
6. Return the reserved sauce to the skillet and cook for a few minutes.
7. Pour the sauce over the beef.
8. Garnish with tomato and parsley, if desired. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Pork trotters braised in adobo sauce until the skin is soft and sticky.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces ham hock/pata, sliced into individual servings
- 2 pieces dried bay leaves
- 1 teaspoon whole peppercorn
- 2 1/2 cups water
- 2 1/2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 2 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar
- 1/5 piece beef or pork cube
- 1/2 head garlic, crushed
- 1/2 teaspoon onion powder
- 1/2 tablespoon granulated white sugar
- Salt to taste (optional)
- 1 tablespoon + 1/2 teaspoon cooking oil
Steps:
1. Boil 8 cups of water in a large cooking pot. Add the ham hock (pata). Continue to boil for 60 minutes. Discard the water and set the ham hock aside.
2. Heat the oil in a large cooking pot. You may use the same pot that you used for the pata.
3. Add the crushed garlic and cook until brown. Add the peppercorn and bay leaves and cook for 30 seconds.
4. Put the boiled ham hock in the cooking pot and pour in the water. Let boil. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
5. Add the beef cube and soy sauce. Cook for 40 minutes on low heat. Add more water if needed.
6. Add the onion powder, vinegar, and sugar. Let the mixture boil. Stir and cover the cooking pot. Continue to simmer for 20 minutes. Add more water if necessary. Make sure that there is enough sauce left.
7. Add salt, if desired. Serve.
8. Share and serve it

Short Description: Chicken liver and gizzard simmered in a savory soy-vinegar adobo sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 2–3 pieces chicken gizzard
- 2–3 pieces chicken liver
- 2 tablespoons + 1 teaspoon all-purpose flour
- 2 tablespoons + 1 teaspoon soy sauce
- 1 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar
- 1/3 teaspoon garlic powder
- 1–2 pieces dried bay leaves
- 1/3 teaspoon whole peppercorn
- 2–3 cloves crushed garlic
- 1/4 cup water
- Salt to taste
- 2 teaspoons green onion, chopped
- 1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon cooking oil
Steps:
1. Boil the chicken gizzard in 4 cups of water, covered, for 60 to 90 minutes. Drain the water and set aside.
2. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/4 teaspoon salt all over the chicken liver. Let it stay for 10 minutes.
3. Heat the cooking oil in a frying pan.
4. Dredge the chicken liver in all-purpose flour. Pan-fry for 2 minutes per side. Remove the pan-fried chicken liver and set aside.
5. On the same pan using the remaining oil, add the garlic. Cook until the color turns light brown.
6. Put in the gizzard and pan-fried liver. Stir.
7. Add the soy sauce and water. Let boil.
8. Add the bay leaves and whole peppercorn. Cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
9. Add the vinegar. Let the liquid re-boil. Stir and cook for 5 minutes.
10. Turn the heat off. Transfer to a serving plate.
11. Top with chopped green onions. Serve and enjoy!

Short Description: Grilled or boiled chicken intestines cooked adobo-style in a savory, tangy sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4–6 medium-sized squid
- 1 piece onion
- 2 pieces tomatoes
- 1/2 cup soy sauce
- 1/2 cup vinegar
- 1 cup water
- 5 cloves crushed garlic
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat a wok or cooking pot then pour in soy sauce, vinegar, and water then bring to a boil.
2. Add the squid and wait for the liquid to re-boil. Simmer for 5 minutes.
3. Turn off the heat then separate the squid from the liquid. Set aside.
4. Pour cooking oil in a separate wok or cooking pot then apply heat.
5. When the oil is hot enough, sauté the garlic, onions, and tomatoes.
6. Put in the squid then cook for a few seconds.
7. Pour in the soy sauce-vinegar-water mixture that was used to cook the squid while black. Bring to a boil and simmer for 3 minutes.
8. Add the ink, salt, ground black pepper, and sugar then stir. Simmer for 3 minutes.
9. Transfer to a serving bowl then serve.
10. For a thicker sauce, remove the squid from the wok or cooking pot and let the sauce boil until enough liquid evaporates. Once done, top the squid with the sauce.

Short Description: Shrimp sautéed in a quick soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic adobo sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram large shrimp, head-on and shell-on
- 1/2 teaspoon ginger, minced or grated
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small shallot, minced
- 1 1/2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon oyster sauce
- 1/2 teaspoon sugar
- 2 tablespoons water
- 1/2 lemon or 2–3 calamansi, juiced
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Oil, for searing and sautéing
Steps:
1. Trim the sharp tip and whiskers of the shrimp. Cut along the back to devein, then rinse and pat dry. Lightly season with salt and pepper.
2. Heat oil over high heat. Sear the shrimp in a single layer for about 1 minute. Flip and cook for 30 seconds more. Do not cook through. Transfer to a plate and cook in batches if needed.
3. Lower the heat to medium. Wipe out any burnt bits and add more oil if needed. Add the ginger, garlic, and shallots. Cook until lightly golden and fragrant.
4. Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and water. Simmer for about 1 minute. Taste and adjust. Add more water if you want more sauce.
5. Return the shrimp to the pan with any juices. Toss and cook for about 2 minutes, until just cooked through and coated in the sauce.
6. Turn off the heat and squeeze in the lemon or calamansi juice.
7. Serve with hot steamed rice.

Short Description: Octopus cooked in vinegar, oyster sauce, garlic, and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 55 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 5 minutes
Ingredients:
- ½ kilo octopus, cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces
- 1 pack (30 g) SARSAYA® Oyster Sauce
- ¼ cup vinegar (60 ml)
- ¼ cup water (60 ml), for the marinade
- 2 cups water (475 ml), for blanching
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- ¼ cup chopped onion
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- A pinch of salt
- A pinch of ground black pepper
- ½ lemon
- A little chopped parsley, for garnish
Steps:
1. Combine the octopus, oyster sauce, vinegar, ¼ cup water, salt, and ground pepper in a bowl. Marinate for 45 minutes.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
3. Pour the marinade into the pan and add the bay leaf. Let it simmer briefly, then turn off the heat.
4. In a separate pot, bring 2 cups of water and the lemon to a rolling boil.
5. Add the octopus and blanch for 2 minutes. Remove it immediately and transfer it to the adobo sauce.
6. Cook the octopus in the sauce for another 2 minutes, following the source's instructions to avoid overcooking.
7. Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with chopped parsley. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Mussels cooked in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic for a quick, savory seafood adobo.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 pound mussels (tahong), cleaned and shelled
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 3 tablespoons soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons white vinegar
- 4 dried bay leaves
- 1/2 tablespoon whole peppercorns
- 2 tablespoons toasted garlic
- 2 tablespoons oil
- Salt, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat the oil in a cooking pot.
2. Add the crushed garlic and whole peppercorns. Cook until the garlic turns light brown.
3. Add the mussels. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Add the bay leaves, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon of toasted garlic. Let it boil, then simmer for 5 to 7 minutes.
5. Pour in the vinegar. Let the liquid reboil, then stir and cook for 3 minutes.
6. Add salt to taste and transfer to a serving plate.
7. Top with the remaining toasted garlic and serve.

Short Description: Crispy fried tofu tossed in a savory soy-vinegar adobo sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup oil
- 1/2 kilogram tokwa, sliced 1-inch thick
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 1 1/2 tablespoons vinegar
- 1/2 Oyster Sauce 30g
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 sachet Magic Sarap 8g
- 1/2 tablespoon brown sugar
- 1/2 cup water
- 1/2 tablespoon toasted garlic
- 1 tablespoon sliced spring onion
Steps:
1. Fry tokwa in oil until golden brown. Remove and set aside. Cut into serving pieces.
2. In the same oil, sauté garlic and onion. Add vinegar, MAGGI® Oyster Sauce, and bay leaves. Cook for 2 minutes.
3. Cut tokwa into 3/4-inch pieces and add to the pan. Season with MAGGI® Magic Sarap® and sugar. Pour water and simmer for 2 minutes.
4. Transfer to a serving plate, top with spring onion and toasted garlic, and serve.

Short Description: Water spinach quickly cooked adobo-style for a simple, garlicky vegetable dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 bunch kangkong
- 1/2 tablespoon oil
- 1/2 onion, peeled and sliced thinly
- 3 cloves garlic, peeled and minced
- 1/4 pound pork belly, cut into 1/2-inch thick strips
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1/4 cup water
- Pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Trim about 2 inches from the kangkong stalks and discard. Cut kangkong into 3-inch lengths, separating the sturdier stalks from the leaves. Wash thoroughly and drain well.
2. In a wide skillet over high heat, heat oil. Add onions and garlic and cook, stirring regularly, until softened.
3. Add pork and cook, stirring regularly, until lightly browned.
4. Add vinegar and bring to a boil. Continue to cook, without stirring, for about 2 to 3 minutes.
5. Add soy sauce and water. Bring to a boil for about 1 to 2 minutes.
6. Lower heat, cover, and cook for about 8 to 10 minutes or until pork is tender and sauce is reduced. Season with pepper to taste.
7. Increase heat to high. Add kangkong stalks and cook for about 1 to 2 minutes.
8. Add kangkong leaves and cook, stirring regularly, for another minute or until just wilted and covered with sauce.
9. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
10. Garnish with fried garlic bits, if desired. Serve hot.

Short Description: Okra cooked in a tangy soy-vinegar adobo sauce with garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 10 pieces okra
- 2 tablespoons water
- 2 tablespoons vinegar
- 1/4 cup pork, diced
- 1 1/2 tablespoons fish sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon pepper
Steps:
1. Wash and parboil the okra in water. Set aside.
2. Fry the pork. Push to one side of the pan.
3. Sauté garlic, onion, and okra.
4. Season with vinegar, fish sauce, and pepper.
5. Cook until the okra is tender crisp.

Short Description: Sponge gourd sautéed with garlic, onion, and tomatoes in a light, savory broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram labanos (daikon/white radish), sliced into thick strips
- 1 carrot, sliced into thick strips
- 1 tomato, cubed
- 1/2 cup pork, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup small dried shrimp (hibe)
- 1/2 medium onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 1/2 teaspoons patis (fish sauce)
- 1/3 cup water
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 1/2 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat the oil in a pan.
2. Sauté the garlic and onion.
3. Once the onion becomes soft, add the tomato. Cook for 3 minutes.
4. Add the pork. Cook for 5 minutes.
5. Pour in the water and let it boil. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
6. Add the labanos and carrot. Stir, then cover and cook for 5 minutes.
7. Add the dried shrimp, patis, and ground black pepper. Stir and cook for 10 minutes more.
8. Transfer to a serving plate.
9. Serve with hot rice.

Short Description: Crispy dried anchovies coated in a sweet and spicy syrup.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- ¼ kilo dried dilis (dried anchovies)
- ½ cup water (120 ml)
- ½ cup white sugar
- ¼ teaspoon chili powder
- ¼ teaspoon red or orange food coloring
- ½ cup cooking oil, for frying
- 1–2 tablespoons sugar, for sprinkling
Steps:
1. Place the dried dilis in a stainless steel mixing bowl and set aside.
2. In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the water, white sugar, chili powder, and food coloring. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
3. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until it thickens into a syrup.
4. Pour the syrup over the dried dilis and gently toss until they are evenly coated.
5. Heat the cooking oil in a wok or wide pan over medium heat. Fry the coated dilis in batches, stirring regularly, until crispy. Avoid overcooking to prevent bitterness.
6. Using a slotted spoon, remove the dilis and transfer them to a mixing bowl.
7. Sprinkle the sugar over the dilis while they are still hot and toss gently.
8. Spread the dilis on a tray and allow them to cool and dry before serving.

Short Description: Snails simmered in vinegar, soy sauce, and garlic for a rich, tangy adobo.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours 15 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 kilogram snails (kuhol)
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium-sized onion, chopped
- 2 tablespoons oil
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons vinegar
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 red or green chili pepper (siling labuyo), chopped
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Water, for boiling and rinsing
Steps:
1. If using live snails, clean and purify them. Place them in a container, cover with water, add salt, and leave them for a few hours to allow the snails to expel any impurities. Rinse them thoroughly under running water.
