4. Add green papaya and cook for 10 minutes.
5. Add chili leaves and pepper, cook for 1 minute and serve.

Short Description: Chicken slow-roasted in a pot with salt for tender, flavorful meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken (leg quarters)
- 2 cups rock salt
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 2 stalks lemongrass, crushed
- 1 medium onion, quartered
- 1 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 pieces bay leaves
- 2 pieces banana leaf (optional)
- 2 tbsp calamansi juice
- 2 tbsp fish sauce (for dip)
Steps:
1. Rub chicken with garlic, pepper and a little salt. Tuck lemongrass, onion and bay leaves around the pieces.
2. Spread the rock salt in a heavy pot and lay banana leaf on top, if using.
3. Place the chicken on the salt bed, cover tightly with a lid.
4. Cook on medium-low heat for 1 hr until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
5. Brush off the loose salt and serve with fish sauce and calamansi.

Short Description: Chicken braised in a sweet-savory red sauce with tomatoes and soy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken (leg quarters), cut up
- 2 tbsp annatto (atsuete) seeds
- 1/4 cup cooking oil
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 2 pieces bay leaves
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 1 tsp brown sugar
- 1 cup water
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan, add annatto seeds, and stir for 1 minute until the oil turns bright red. Strain and discard the seeds.
2. Saute garlic in the annatto oil. Add chicken and brown lightly.
3. Add soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, peppercorns and water.
4. Simmer covered for 25 minutes.
5. Add sugar and simmer uncovered until the sauce reduces and the chicken turns deep red. Serve with rice.

Short Description: Chicken braised in a sweet-savory soy and vinegar sauce until tender.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken (leg quarters), cut up
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 3 tbsp vinegar
- 3 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 2 pieces bay leaves
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 2 pieces saba bananas, sliced
- 1 piece carrot, sliced
- 1 cup water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Brown the chicken in oil with garlic.
2. Add soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, bay leaves, peppercorns and water.
3. Simmer covered for 25 minutes.
4. Add saba and carrot and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
5. Serve hot.

Short Description: A Filipino stew of chicken, liver, potatoes, and carrots in tomato sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken breast, cubed
- 1 piece chicken liver, cubed
- 1 cup tomato sauce
- 1 piece potato, cubed
- 1 piece carrot, cubed
- 1/4 cup raisins
- 1/2 piece red bell pepper, diced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Saute garlic and onion in oil. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
2. Add soy sauce, fish sauce, tomato sauce and water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
3. Add potato and carrot and cook for 10 minutes.
4. Add liver, raisins and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
5. Season to taste and serve.

Short Description: Whole chicken marinated in lemongrass, soy, and calamansi, then roasted until golden.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Marinating Time: 4 hours
Overall Time: 5 hours 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small whole chicken
- 3 stalks lemongrass, crushed
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 3 stalks scallions
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 pieces bay leaves
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Mix soy sauce, fish sauce, calamansi juice, sugar and pepper. Rub it all over and inside the chicken.
2. Stuff the cavity with lemongrass, garlic, scallions and bay leaves. Marinate for at least 4 hours.
3. Tie the legs together and place the chicken on a rack.
4. Roast at 190 C for 1 hr 15 mins, brushing with oil and marinade every 20 minutes.
5. Rest for 10 minutes, then carve and serve with liver sauce or soy-calamansi dip.

Short Description: Crispy fried chicken skin, crunchy and salty, perfect with vinegar dip.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 5 minutes
Drying Time: 3 hours
Overall Time: 4 hours 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- skin from 4 pieces chicken
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- 3 cups water
- 2 cups cooking oil for frying
- 3 tbsp spiced vinegar for dipping
Steps:
1. Boil the chicken skin in salted water for 10 minutes. Drain and scrape off extra fat.
2. Pat the skin dry and spread out flat on a rack. Air-dry for 3 hours or dry in a 100 C oven for 1 hr.
3. Season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
4. Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 3 to 5 minutes until golden and crunchy.
5. Drain on paper towels and serve with spiced vinegar.

Short Description: A smoky Tausug chicken dish grilled and simmered in a savory coconut sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken (leg quarters)
- 1/4 cup grated coconut, for burning
- 1 tbsp turmeric powder
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, julienned
- 2 stalks lemongrass, minced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup coconut cream
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Toast the grated coconut in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until completely blackened and smoky (not ashy). Grind it into a paste with a little water.
2. Mix the black coconut paste with turmeric, ginger, half the lemongrass and salt. Rub it on the chicken and marinate for 30 minutes.
3. Saute onion and garlic in oil. Add the chicken with the marinade, siling haba and remaining lemongrass.
4. Pour in coconut milk and simmer covered for 25 minutes, then stir in the coconut cream and simmer until thick.
5. Grill the chicken for 1 to 2 minutes per side. Spoon the black sauce over and serve with rice.

Short Description: A Maranao chicken stew with turmeric, coconut, and spicy vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken (leg quarters), cut up
- 1/2 cup freshly grated coconut
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp turmeric powder
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 stalks scallions (or sakurab), chopped
- 1/2 piece red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 tbsp coconut oil
- 2 cups water
- 4 tbsp sakurab (or scallions), minced (for the palapa)
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, minced
- 5 pieces red chili (siling labuyo), minced
Steps:
1. Pound the sakurab (or scallions), ginger and chili together to make the palapa.
2. Saute garlic and onion with 2 tbsp of the palapa. Add chicken and water, bring to a boil and add 1 tsp turmeric and salt.
3. Simmer for 20 minutes, remove the chicken, and pour in the coconut milk. Cook the broth for 5 minutes.
4. Mix the grated coconut with the remaining turmeric and 2 tbsp palapa.
5. Heat coconut oil and saute bell pepper, then add the coconut mixture and cook until fragrant.
6. Return the chicken and cook on low heat for 10 minutes. Serve with rice and the remaining broth.

Short Description: A black, savory Tausug beef soup flavored with burnt coconut and spices.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 6-8 pieces beef (shank or brisket) cubes
- 1/4 cup grated coconut, for burning
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 thumb-sized lengkuas (galangal), sliced
- 1 tbsp turmeric powder
- 2 stalks lemongrass, crushed
- 1 medium onion, sliced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tsp salt
- 5 cups water
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Toast the grated coconut in a dry pan until completely black and smoky. Grind it into a paste with a little water.
2. Rub the beef with the black coconut paste, turmeric, ginger, lengkuas and salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
3. Saute garlic and onion in oil. Add the beef and its marinade and fry for 5 minutes.
4. Add water, lemongrass, pepper and siling haba.
5. Simmer on low heat for 1 hr 45 mins until the beef is tender and the broth is black.
6. Adjust the salt and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Grilled chicken skewers served with a sweet, spicy sauce and sticky rice.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Marinating Time: 2 hours
Overall Time: 3 hours
Ingredients:
- 1 small slab beef sirloin, cut into small cubes
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp turmeric powder
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, minced
- 8-10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water
- 1 tbsp curry powder (for the sauce)
- 2 tbsp dried chili flakes
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, minced
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp tomato sauce
- 1 cup water
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
- 3 tbsp cooking oil
- 2 cups cooked rice (puso or plain)
Steps:
1. Marinate the beef in soy sauce, turmeric, garlic and ginger for at least 2 hours.
2. Thread the beef tightly onto the soaked skewers.
3. Make the sauce: saute garlic, ginger, curry powder and chili flakes in oil until fragrant. Add tomato sauce, sugar and water and simmer for 10 minutes.
4. Stir in the cornstarch mixture until the sauce is slightly thick and orange.
5. Grill the skewers over hot coals for 3 to 4 minutes per side, basting with the sauce.
6. Place skewers in a bowl, ladle the hot sauce over, and serve with rice.

Short Description: Boneless milkfish marinated in vinegar and garlic, then fried until golden and crisp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Marinating Time: 3 hours
Overall Time: 3 hours 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces boneless bangus (butterflied)
- 1/3 cup vinegar
- 1 head garlic, minced
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
- 3 tbsp spiced vinegar for dipping
Steps:
1. Combine vinegar, garlic, salt and pepper in a shallow dish.
2. Marinate the bangus in the mixture for at least 3 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
3. Drain and pat dry.
4. Fry in hot oil for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
5. Serve with garlic rice and spiced vinegar.

Short Description: Stuffed milkfish with sautéed vegetables and ground fish meat, fried until golden.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium bangus (milkfish)
- 1 piece carrot, minced
- 1 piece potato, minced
- 1/4 cup green peas
- 2 tbsp raisins
- 1 medium onion, minced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 piece egg, beaten
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
Steps:
1. Debone the bangus, keeping the skin intact (or ask the market to do it). Season with soy sauce and pepper.
2. Steam or boil the fish meat, flake it, and set aside.
3. Saute garlic and onion in a little oil. Add carrot, potato, flaked fish, peas, raisins, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes. Let cool.
4. Mix in the beaten egg.
5. Stuff the mixture back into the skin and sew or secure the opening with toothpicks.
6. Fry in hot oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden. Slice and serve.

Short Description: Crunchy, sizzling milkfish sisig with onions, chilies, and calamansi.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces boneless bangus
- 1 medium red onion, chopped
- 2 pieces siling haba, chopped
- 1 piece siling labuyo, chopped
- 3 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp mayonnaise
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 pieces eggs
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
Steps:
1. Fry or grill the bangus until cooked and crisp. Flake the meat and chop the crispy skin.
2. Saute onion and chilies in a little oil for 2 minutes.
3. Add the fish, soy sauce, calamansi juice and pepper. Toss over high heat.
4. Stir in mayonnaise.
5. Serve on a hot plate topped with a raw or fried egg.

Short Description: Milkfish simmered in sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces bangus belly, cut in half
- 1/4 cup tamarind pulp (or 1 pack sinigang mix)
- 1 piece tomato, quartered
- 1 medium onion, quartered
- 1/2 small radish (labanos), sliced
- 1/2 cup string beans, cut
- 1 piece eggplant, sliced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 bunch kangkong leaves
- 2 tbsp fish sauce
- 4 cups water
Steps:
1. Boil water with tamarind pulp, onion and tomato for 10 minutes.
2. Add radish and cook for 5 minutes.
3. Add the bangus and simmer for 8 minutes.
4. Add string beans, eggplant and siling haba and cook for 4 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce, add kangkong, and serve hot.

Short Description: Milkfish simmered in vinegar, ginger, and peppercorns for a tangy, savory dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces bangus, cut into pieces
- 1/3 cup vinegar
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 1 small ampalaya (bitter melon), sliced
- 1 piece eggplant, sliced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup water
Steps:
1. Arrange ginger, garlic and peppercorns at the bottom of a pot. Layer the eggplant and ampalaya, then the bangus.
2. Pour vinegar and water over; do not stir. Add siling haba.
3. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 15 minutes.
4. Season with salt and simmer for 5 more minutes. Serve hot.

Short Description: Grilled milkfish stuffed with tomato, onion, and ginger, served with soy-calamansi dip.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 whole bangus (milkfish), about 450-600 g, cleaned and slit along the belly
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 1/2 medium red onion, diced
- 1 tbsp minced ginger
- 1 tbsp calamansi or lemon juice
- 1 tsp salt, divided
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 tbsp oil, for brushing banana leaf or fish if needed
- Banana leaf or foil, optional
- 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp calamansi juice, for dipping sauce
Steps:
1. Rinse the cleaned milkfish and pat it dry. Rub about half the salt inside the cavity and lightly over the skin.
2. Mix tomato, onion, ginger, calamansi juice, remaining salt, and black pepper. Stuff the mixture into the fish cavity without packing it too tightly.
3. Lightly oil the grill grate. Wrap the fish in banana leaf if desired, or grill it directly in a fish basket so it holds together.
4. Grill over medium heat for about 10-12 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily near the backbone. Turn with a spatula and tongs together to avoid tearing the fish.
5. Mix soy sauce and calamansi juice for dipping. Rest the fish briefly, then serve with rice and the dip.

Short Description: Crispy fried galunggong, simple, salty, and perfect with rice.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3-4 pieces galunggong, cleaned
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
- 2 pieces calamansi
- 2 tbsp spiced vinegar
Steps:
1. Rinse the galunggong and pat dry very well.
2. Season inside and out with salt.
3. Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
4. Fry the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
5. Drain and serve with calamansi and spiced vinegar.

Short Description: Galunggong simmered in vinegar, ginger, and chilies for a tangy, savory dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3-4 pieces galunggong, cleaned
- 1/3 cup vinegar
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup water
Steps:
1. Arrange ginger, garlic and peppercorns at the bottom of a pot. Place the fish on top.
2. Pour in vinegar and water; do not stir. Add siling haba.
3. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 15 minutes.
4. Season with salt and simmer for 3 minutes. Serve hot.

Short Description: Fish simmered in vinegar, ginger, and garlic, a classic tangy Filipino dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces whole fish (such as tambakol or lapu-lapu steaks)
- 1/3 cup vinegar
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 head garlic, crushed
- 1 small ampalaya (bitter melon), sliced
- 1 piece eggplant, sliced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 1/2 cup water
Steps:
1. Layer ginger, garlic, ampalaya and eggplant in a pot. Place the fish on top.
2. Add vinegar, water, peppercorns and siling haba without stirring.
3. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 15 minutes.
4. Season with fish sauce and simmer for 5 more minutes. Serve hot.

Short Description: Golden fried tilapia with crisp skin and tender, flaky meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces tilapia, cleaned and scaled
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
- 2 pieces calamansi
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
Steps:
1. Pat the tilapia dry. Season with salt and pepper inside and out.
2. Dust lightly with cornstarch for extra crispness.
3. Fry in hot oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden brown.
4. Drain and serve with calamansi and soy sauce.

Short Description: Fried tilapia in a sweet and sour sauce with ginger and bell peppers.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces tilapia, cleaned
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
- 1 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 piece red bell pepper, sliced
- 1/2 piece green bell pepper, sliced
- 1 small onion, sliced
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, julienned
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp tomato ketchup
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Season the tilapia with salt and dust with cornstarch. Fry until golden and crisp. Drain and place on a plate.
2. In a pan, saute ginger and onion in a little oil.
3. Add vinegar, sugar, ketchup and water. Simmer for 3 minutes.
4. Add carrot and bell peppers and cook for 2 minutes.
5. Stir in the cornstarch mixture until thick.
6. Pour the sauce over the fried tilapia and serve.

Short Description: Fish in a savory tomato-onion sauce thickened with egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces tilapia, cleaned
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
- 2 pieces tomatoes, chopped
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, minced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 piece egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 stalk scallion, chopped
Steps:
1. Season the fish with salt. Fry until golden. Drain.
2. In another pan, saute garlic, ginger, onion and tomatoes until soft.
3. Add fish sauce, pepper and water. Simmer for 3 minutes.
4. Place the fried fish in the sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
5. Pour the beaten egg around the fish and let it set. Top with scallions and serve.

Short Description: A light, ginger-flavored fish soup with tomatoes and leafy vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces dalag (mudfish), cut into pieces
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 piece tomato, quartered
- 1 medium onion, quartered
- 1/4 head napa cabbage, chopped
- 1 bunch pechay
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 2 tbsp fish sauce
- 4 cups water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Saute ginger, onion and tomato in oil.
2. Add water and peppercorns and bring to a boil.
3. Add the dalag and simmer for 10 minutes.
4. Season with fish sauce.
5. Add cabbage and cook for 3 minutes, then add pechay for 1 minute. Serve hot.

Short Description: Crispy fried catfish with a golden crust and tender, flaky meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium hito (catfish), cleaned and cut into pieces
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp calamansi juice
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 cup cooking oil for frying
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 pieces calamansi
Steps:
1. Season the catfish with salt, pepper and calamansi juice. Rest for 10 minutes.
2. Pat dry and dust with cornstarch.
3. Fry in hot oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
4. Drain and serve with soy sauce and calamansi.

Short Description: Whole catfish grilled over charcoal after a calamansi-garlic marinade; served with a fresh tomato-onion relish or sawsawan.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium hito (catfish), about 400-500 g, cleaned and slit on both sides
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 tbsp soy sauce (optional)
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 small tomato, finely chopped, for relish
- 1/4 small onion, finely chopped, for relish
- 1 tbsp vinegar or calamansi juice, for relish
- Oil for brushing the grill
Steps:
1. Clean the catfish thoroughly and pat dry. Score each side with two or three shallow slashes so the marinade reaches the flesh.
2. Mix calamansi juice, optional soy sauce, crushed garlic, salt, and pepper. Rub over the fish and inside the cavity; marinate for 10-15 minutes.
3. Heat and lightly oil a grill. Grill over medium coals, turning carefully every 5-7 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. Thick catfish may need 15-20 minutes total depending on heat.
4. Mix the chopped tomato and onion with vinegar or calamansi for a fresh relish.
5. Transfer the fish carefully to a plate and serve with the relish or dipping sauce. Avoid repeatedly turning the fish; the skin can stick if the grill is not hot and oiled.

Short Description: Grilled tilapia stuffed with tomato, onion, garlic, and ginger, then wrapped in banana leaf to keep the flesh moist.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 large tilapia (about 400-500 g), scaled, gutted, and cleaned
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 1/2 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp minced ginger
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- Banana leaf or foil, for wrapping
- 1 tsp oil, for brushing
Steps:
1. Pat the cleaned tilapia dry and make two or three shallow slashes on each side. Rub with salt and pepper.
2. Mix tomato, onion, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, and calamansi juice. Spoon the mixture into the fish cavity.
3. Brush the banana leaf lightly with oil, place the fish on it, and wrap securely. If using foil, leave a little space around the fish so steam can circulate.
4. Grill over medium heat for about 8-10 minutes per side, depending on size, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. Open the packet carefully because steam will escape.
5. Serve hot with the cooked stuffing and any soy-calamansi juices from the packet.

Short Description: Smoky grilled squid stuffed with tomatoes and onions, with a tangy dipping sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4-6 medium-sized squid, cleaned
- 2 pieces tomatoes, chopped
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 3 tbsp soy sauce (for the dip)
- 2 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 piece siling labuyo, chopped
Steps:
1. Mix tomatoes, onion, salt and pepper.
2. Stuff each squid with the mixture and secure the opening with a toothpick.
3. Grill over hot coals for 3 to 4 minutes per side. Do not overcook.
4. Mix soy sauce, calamansi juice and chili for the dip and serve.

Short Description: Plump shrimp marinated in a buttery garlic sauce and grilled until pink.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 8-10 pieces shrimp (shell on)
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp melted butter
- 2 pieces calamansi
Steps:
1. Rinse the shrimp and trim the whiskers and legs.
2. Mix garlic, calamansi juice, salt, pepper and butter. Marinate the shrimp for 15 minutes.
3. Grill over hot coals for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and curled.
4. Serve with calamansi wedges.

Short Description: Shrimp steamed in their own juices with a simple salt seasoning.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 8-10 pieces shrimp (shell on)
- 1/2 cup lemon-lime soda
- 4 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 stalk scallion, chopped
Steps:
1. Rinse the shrimp and trim the whiskers.
2. Heat oil in a pan and saute the garlic for 30 seconds.
3. Add the shrimp, salt, pepper and lemon-lime soda.
4. Cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the shrimp turn red and the liquid has reduced.
5. Top with scallions and serve.

Short Description: Shrimp sautéed with garlic, onions, and tomatoes in a savory sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 8-10 pieces shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 piece tomato, chopped
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp calamansi juice
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 stalk scallion, chopped
Steps:
1. Saute garlic, onion and tomato in oil until soft.
2. Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink.
3. Add fish sauce, pepper and calamansi juice. Toss for 1 minute.
4. Top with scallions and serve with rice.

Short Description: Crispy battered shrimp, golden and crunchy, with a sweet-sour dipping sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 8-10 pieces shrimp, peeled with tails on
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 piece egg
- 1/2 cup cold water
- 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 cups cooking oil for frying
- 1/4 cup tomato ketchup (for the sauce)
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp vinegar
- 2 tbsp pineapple juice
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Season the shrimp with salt and pepper.
2. Whisk flour, cornstarch, egg, water, baking powder and salt into a smooth batter.
3. Make the sauce: simmer ketchup, sugar, vinegar and pineapple juice for 2 minutes, then stir in the cornstarch mixture until thick.
4. Dip the shrimp in the batter and deep fry for 2 to 3 minutes until golden.
5. Drain and serve with the sauce.

Short Description: Shrimp simmered in rich coconut milk with ginger and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 8-10 pieces shrimp (shell on)
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup coconut cream
- 1 cup kalabasa (squash), cubed
- 1/2 cup string beans, cut
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Saute garlic, onion and ginger in oil.
2. Add coconut milk and kalabasa. Simmer for 8 minutes.
3. Add string beans and siling haba and cook for 3 minutes.
4. Add the shrimp and cook for 3 minutes until pink.
5. Stir in coconut cream and fish sauce and simmer for 2 minutes. Serve hot.

Short Description: Crab simmered in creamy coconut milk with ginger and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces medium alimasag (blue crab), cleaned and halved
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup coconut cream
- 1 piece sayote, wedged
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 handful malunggay leaves
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Saute garlic, onion and ginger in oil.
2. Add coconut milk and sayote and simmer for 8 minutes.
3. Add the crab and siling haba and cook covered for 10 minutes until the shells turn red.
4. Stir in the coconut cream and fish sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
5. Add malunggay leaves and serve.

Short Description: Mud crab cooked in coconut milk with ginger, garlic, and chili.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 large alimango (mud crab), cleaned and cut up
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup coconut cream
- 1 cup kalabasa (squash), cubed
- 1/2 cup sitaw (string beans), cut
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/2 tsp ground black pepper
Steps:
1. Place coconut milk, ginger, garlic and kalabasa in a pot and simmer for 8 minutes.
2. Add the crab and cook covered for 12 minutes until the shells turn red.
3. Add sitaw and siling haba and cook for 3 minutes.
4. Stir in coconut cream, fish sauce and pepper. Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly. Serve.

Short Description: Crab in a rich tomato-egg sauce with garlic and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces medium alimasag (blue crab), cleaned and halved
- 2 pieces tomatoes, chopped
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, minced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 piece egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 stalk scallion, chopped
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Saute garlic, ginger, onion and tomatoes in oil until soft.
2. Add the crab, fish sauce, pepper and water. Cover and cook for 12 minutes until the shells turn red.
3. Pour the beaten egg around the crab and let it set without stirring for 2 minutes.
4. Top with scallions and serve.

Short Description: A fluffy egg omelet filled with sweet crab meat and aromatics.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces medium alimasag (blue crab), steamed
- 3 pieces eggs, beaten
- 1/2 piece tomato, diced
- 1/2 medium onion, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 3 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Steam the crab for 12 minutes, cool and pick out all the meat.
2. Saute garlic, onion and tomato in 1 tbsp oil. Add the crab meat and fish sauce and cook for 2 minutes. Let cool.
3. Mix the crab mixture with beaten eggs, salt and pepper.
4. Heat the remaining oil in a pan and pour in the mixture.
5. Cook for 3 minutes per side until golden. Serve with banana ketchup.

Short Description: Spanner crab sautéed in butter, garlic, and a rich, savory sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces curacha (spanner crab), or 2 pieces medium alimasag
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup coconut cream
- 2 tbsp annatto oil
- 3 tbsp crab fat (aligue)
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, minced
- 1 stalk lemongrass, sliced
- 1 tsp turmeric powder
- 1 tsp curry powder
- 2 pieces siling labuyo, chopped
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup crab stock (from boiling the crab)
Steps:
1. Boil the crabs in salted water for 10 minutes. Remove and reserve 1 cup of the stock.
2. Heat annatto oil and saute garlic, ginger, onion and lemongrass until fragrant.
3. Add the crab fat and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in turmeric, curry powder and chilies for 1 minute.
4. Pour in coconut milk and crab stock and simmer for 8 minutes.
5. Add the crabs and coat with the sauce. Stir in coconut cream and brown sugar and simmer until the sauce thickens.
6. Season with salt and serve with rice.

Short Description: Squid stuffed with ground pork and vegetables, then simmered or fried.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces large squid, cleaned (bodies and tentacles)
- 1/2 cup ground pork
- 1 small carrot, minced
- 1 stalk celery, minced
- 1 medium onion, minced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 piece tomato, diced
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 piece egg, beaten
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 4 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Marinate the squid bodies in soy sauce and calamansi juice for 30 minutes.
2. Chop the tentacles. Saute garlic, onion, celery and tomato in 1 tbsp oil. Add ground pork and tentacles and cook for 5 minutes.
3. Add carrot, salt and pepper and cook for 8 minutes. Let cool.
4. Stuff the squid bodies with the filling and secure the openings with toothpicks.
5. Dip in beaten egg and dredge in flour.
6. Pan-fry in the remaining oil for 3 to 5 minutes per side. Do not overcook. Slice and serve.

Short Description: Crispy fried squid rings with a sweet-sour or vinegar dipping sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4-6 medium-sized squid, cleaned and cut into rings
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornstarch
- 1 piece egg
- 1/2 cup cold water
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 cups cooking oil for frying
- 3 tbsp vinegar
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 piece siling labuyo, chopped
Steps:
1. Pat the squid rings dry and season with salt and pepper.
2. Whisk flour, cornstarch, egg and water into a smooth batter.
3. Dip the squid rings in the batter and deep fry in hot oil for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
4. Drain on paper towels.
5. Mix vinegar, garlic and chili for the dip and serve.

Short Description: Squid simmered in creamy coconut milk with ginger and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4-6 medium-sized squid, cleaned and cut into rings
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup coconut cream
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 pieces siling haba
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 handful spinach or kangkong leaves
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Saute garlic, onion and ginger in oil.
2. Add coconut milk and siling haba and simmer for 5 minutes.
3. Add the squid and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, no longer, so it stays tender.
4. Stir in coconut cream and fish sauce.
5. Add the leafy greens, cook for 1 minute and serve.

Short Description: Mussels simmered in ginger broth with chili leaves for a warm, savory soup.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 pound mussels (tahong), cleaned
- 1 cup spinach or hot pepper leaves
- 1 1/2 thumbs ginger, julienned
- 1/2 onion, sliced
- 2–3 cloves garlic, pounded
- 3/4 teaspoon salt or 1 1/2 tablespoons fish sauce
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 1 long green pepper, optional
Steps:
1. Heat a cooking pot and pour in the oil.
2. Sauté the garlic and onion.
3. Add the ginger and mussels, then cook for 1 minute.
4. Pour in the water and let it boil. Cook for 5 minutes.
5. Add the spinach or hot pepper leaves. Cook for 3 minutes.
6. Add salt or fish sauce and pepper. Stir.
7. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.

Short Description: Mussels in a sour tamarind broth with tomatoes and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/3 tablespoons oil
- 1/3 cup onion, sliced
- 2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon ginger, peeled and cut into strips
- 1/3 cup tomato, chopped
- 1 cup gabi, peeled and chopped
- 1 1/3 cups water
- 1 1/3 cups mussels (tahong) with shells, cleaned
- 2/3 cup sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 3/4 cup eggplant, sliced diagonally
- 1 green chili (siling pansigang)
- 2 1/2 tablespoons calamansi juice
- 1 1/2 teaspoons fish sauce
- 1/3 pack AJI-GINISA® Flavor Seasoning Mix
- 2/3 cup kangkong leaves with soft stems
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot. Sauté onions, garlic, and ginger. Add tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
2. Add gabi and water. Cover the pot and boil until the gabi is tender. Add the mussels, sitaw, eggplant, and green chili.
3. Add calamansi juice, fish sauce, and AJI-GINISA®. Mix well.
4. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the mussels and vegetables are cooked. Add the kangkong, cover the pot, then turn off the heat.
5. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.

Short Description: Fresh mussels steamed with garlic and seasonings until tender.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- ½ kilo fresh mussels, cleaned
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small shallot, finely chopped
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- 1 cup water (240 ml)
- 1 teaspoon calamansi juice
- 1 teaspoon chopped spring onion
- 1 teaspoon chopped parsley (optional)
- 1 tablespoon butter
- Salt to taste
- Ground black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Clean the mussels under running water. Discard mussels with cracked shells or those that remain open when tapped.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
3. Add the garlic and shallot. Sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add the mussels and cook uncovered for 1 minute.
5. Pour in the water and cover the pan. Steam for about 3–5 minutes, or until the shells open.
6. Add the calamansi juice, spring onion, and parsley, if using. Season with salt and ground black pepper.
7. Add the butter and stir gently until it melts into the broth.
8. Remove from the heat. Discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking, then serve hot.

Short Description: Fresh oysters in a tangy calamansi and vinegar dressing with ginger and chili.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 kilogram oysters (talaba)
- 1 medium red onion, sliced
- 1 thumb-sized ginger root, thinly sliced
- 3/4 cup vinegar, sukang tuba, or coconut vinegar
- 3 red chilies or labuyo, sliced
- 3 long chili peppers (siling pangsigang), sliced
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Boiling water, as needed
Steps:
1. Clean and wash the oysters in running water and remove dirt.
2. Transfer the oysters to a mixing bowl and pour boiling water into the bowl, just enough to cover the oysters.
3. Let the shells partially open before removing the oysters from the basin.
4. One by one, open the shells and take out the meat. Wash and clean it well under running water if needed.
5. Transfer the oyster meat into another mixing bowl. Add the onion, ginger, vinegar, and chilies. Mix well.
6. Season with salt and pepper. Adjust the flavor to suit your taste.
7. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
8. Serve and enjoy.

Short Description: Tanigue cubed and cured in vinegar and calamansi with ginger, chili, and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 3 hours
Overall Time: At least 3 hours 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram tanigue (wahoo) fillet, cut into cubes
- 1 thumb-sized piece fresh ginger, minced
- 3 red chilies or siling labuyo, chopped
- 5–7 calamansi
- 1/2 medium red onion, chopped into small pieces
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon sugar
- Salt, to taste
Steps:
1. Squeeze the juice out of the calamansi over a large bowl. Use a sieve to filter the seeds. Discard the seeds.
2. In the bowl with the calamansi juice, add the sugar, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and ground black pepper. Stir until the sugar and salt are diluted.
3. Add the ginger, chili, and onion. Stir for a few seconds until all ingredients are well blended.
4. Arrange the raw fish cubes in a large bowl. Pour the calamansi mixture over the fish. Toss until the fish cubes are coated. Let it stay for 10 minutes.
5. Toss one more time and taste. Add more salt if needed. You can also add more calamansi juice if needed. Toss to blend all the ingredients.
6. Securely cover the bowl and place it inside the refrigerator. Let it chill for at least 3 hours.
7. Serve and enjoy.

Short Description: Fresh tuna cubes cured in vinegar with ginger, chilies, and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 2 hours
Overall Time: At least 2 hours 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram tuna, skinned, deboned, and cubed
- 1/2 cup vinegar
- 1 tablespoon ginger, minced
- 1/2 large red onion, minced
- 2/3 teaspoon salt
- 1/3 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 3 tablespoons lemon or calamansi juice
- 1/2–1 tablespoon red chilies, chopped
Steps:
1. Place the cubed tuna meat in a large bowl, then pour in 1/4 cup of the vinegar.
2. Let it stand for 2 minutes, then gently squeeze the tuna by placing a spoon on top and applying a little pressure.
3. Gently wash the tuna meat with vinegar. Drain all the vinegar once done. This will help reduce the fishy smell.
4. Add the remaining 1/4 cup vinegar, calamansi or lemon juice, ginger, salt, ground black pepper, and red chilies, then mix well.
5. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
6. Top with minced red onions and serve.
7. Share and enjoy!

Short Description: Fresh shrimp marinated in vinegar and calamansi with onions, ginger, and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- ¼ kilo fresh medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- ¼ cup white vinegar (60 ml)
- 2 tablespoons calamansi juice
- 1 small thumb-sized piece of ginger, grated
- ½ small onion, chopped
- ½ small red bell pepper, sliced (optional)
- 2 pieces kamias, sliced, or a few strips of green mango
- 1 siling labuyo, chopped
- ¼ teaspoon chili flakes
- 1 stalk green onion, chopped
- Salt to taste
- Ground black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Place the shrimp in a bowl and pour in the vinegar. Stir gently and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
2. In a separate bowl, combine the calamansi juice, salt, and ground black pepper. Stir well.
3. Add the ginger, onion, red bell pepper, kamias or green mango, siling labuyo, chili flakes, and green onion. Mix gently.
4. Drain the excess vinegar from the shrimp.
5. Add the shrimp to the vegetable and calamansi mixture. Mix gently until combined.
6. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.
7. Transfer to a serving dish and serve chilled.

Short Description: A Davao-style kinilaw of grilled pork belly and raw fish in tangy vinegar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 pound grilled pork belly (liempo), chopped
- 1/2 kilogram fresh tuna, cubed
- 1 cup cucumber, seeded and thinly sliced
- 3/4 cup vinegar
- 1/2 medium red onion, sliced
- 1 tablespoon ginger, julienned
- 2 siling haba, sliced
- 4–5 calamansi
- 2–3 siling labuyo, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
Steps:
1. Place the tuna meat in a bowl and pour in 1/4 cup of vinegar. Soak for 8 minutes.
2. Using a spoon or fork, press the tuna meat lightly.
3. Drain the vinegar, then combine the cucumber, onion, ginger, finger chilies, Thai chilies, and salt with the tuna. Mix well.
4. Squeeze the calamansi until all the juice is extracted, then pour in the remaining 1/2 cup vinegar. Mix well and soak for 10 minutes.
5. Add the grilled pork belly and mix thoroughly. Let the mixture stand for at least 1 hour. You may place it inside the refrigerator.
6. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.
7. Share and enjoy!

Short Description: Fresh anchovies coated in seasoned flour and cornstarch, then fried until crispy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- ¼ kilo fresh dilis (anchovies), cleaned
- ¼ teaspoon fine salt
- ¼ teaspoon chili powder
- ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper
- ¼ cup all-purpose flour
- ¼ cup cornstarch
- ⅛ teaspoon salt, for the breading
- ⅛ teaspoon chili powder, for the breading
- ⅛ teaspoon ground black pepper, for the breading
- Cooking oil, for deep-frying
- Spiced vinegar, for dipping
Steps:
1. Wash the fresh dilis under running water and drain thoroughly in a colander. Pat dry to help the coating stick.
2. Place the dilis in a bowl. Add ¼ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon chili powder, and ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper. Mix gently.
3. In another bowl, combine the flour, cornstarch, ⅛ teaspoon salt, ⅛ teaspoon chili powder, and ⅛ teaspoon ground black pepper.
4. Coat the dilis in the flour mixture in small batches.
5. Use a strainer to remove excess breading, then set the coated dilis aside.
6. Heat cooking oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
7. Fry the dilis in small batches until golden brown and crispy.
8. Remove the fried dilis and drain on a colander or paper towels.
9. Serve hot with spiced vinegar.

Recipe Name: Tuyo Fish with Rice and Tomato
Short Description: Crispy fried dried fish, salty and crunchy, perfect with rice and vinegar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 8 minutes
Overall Time: 13 minutes
Ingredients:
- 6 pieces tuyo (salted dried fish)
- 2 cups cooked white rice
- 2 plum tomatoes, cut into wedges
- Cooking oil spray
- 1/3 cup sinamak (spiced vinegar)
Steps:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Arrange the tuyo on a sheet of aluminum foil. Spray both sides lightly with cooking oil.
3. Cover with another sheet of aluminum foil and seal the edges to make a packet.
4. Turn on the kitchen exhaust fan, then bake for 6–10 minutes.
5. Carefully open the foil packet and arrange the tuyo on serving plates with cooked rice and tomato wedges.
6. Serve with sinamak on the side.

Short Description: Filipino smoked fish, commonly made with bangus or galunggong and served with rice, vinegar, and eggs.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 7 hours
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 7 hours 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 kg mackerel
- 3 cups water (720 ml)
- 3/4 cup sea salt
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 whole garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 tablespoon vinegar
- 3 handfuls wood chips, soaked in water
Steps:
1. Clean the fish and remove the guts and scales.
2. Combine the water, sea salt, brown sugar, garlic, black pepper, and vinegar in a large bowl. Soak the fish in the mixture for at least 6 hours.
3. Drain the fish for at least 1 hour, then pat it dry.
4. Place the water-soaked wood chips in a roasting pan.
5. Put the pan on a gas barbecue grill and heat until the wood chips begin to smoke.
6. Place a roasting rack lined with foil above the pan. Arrange the fish side by side on the rack.
7. Lower the heat to medium, cover the grill, and cook until the smoke stops. Turn off the heat and leave the fish inside for another 10 minutes.
8. Open the lid and check that the fish is fully cooked and smoked.

Short Description: Smoked boneless milkfish stuffed with onion, garlic, tomato, and coriander, served with salted egg and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 smoked boneless bangus (tinapa)
- Cooking oil
- 1/2 onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic
- 1/2 tomato, diced
- 1/2 sprig kinchay, chopped
- Salt and pepper, to taste

SIDES
- Salted egg
- 2 cherry tomatoes, halved
Steps:
1. Drizzle a generous amount of olive oil inside the fish.
2. Stuff the bangus with the sliced onion, garlic, diced tomato, and chopped coriander. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
3. Close the bangus and drizzle olive oil all over the fish.
4. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 15 minutes.
5. Serve with your favorite dipping sauce, salted egg, and cherry tomatoes.

Short Description: Fried rice with smoked fish flakes, scrambled eggs, and green onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cold cooked rice
- 1 1/2 tablespoons canola oil
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 pieces tinapang galunggong, deboned and flaked
- 1 green onion, chopped
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Use your hands to break apart the cold rice and separate the grains.
2. Heat 1/2 tablespoon oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the beaten egg and cook, stirring, until set but still moist. Remove from the pan and set aside.
3. Add another 1/2 tablespoon oil to the pan. Sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
4. Add the tinapa flakes and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring regularly. Remove from the pan and set aside.
5. Add the remaining oil and increase the heat to high. Add the rice and spread it across the pan. Cook for about 45 seconds, then toss and repeat until heated through.
6. Add the soy sauce and season with salt and pepper.
7. Return the tinapa flakes and egg to the pan. Add the green onion and toss gently to combine. Cook for another 1–2 minutes until thoroughly heated.
8. Serve hot.

Recipe Name: Tinapa Flakes, Salted Duck Egg and Tomato
Short Description: Smoked fish flakes mixed with salted duck egg and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces tinapa, flaked and deboned
- 1 salted duck egg (itlog na pula), chopped
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1 teaspoon soy sauce
Steps:
1. Remove the bones from the tinapa and flake the fish into small pieces.
2. Chop the salted duck egg and tomato.
3. Combine the tinapa flakes, salted duck egg, tomato, and soy sauce in a bowl.
4. Mix gently until well combined and serve.

Short Description: Spaghetti tossed with crispy tuyo flakes, garlic, tomatoes, and chili flakes, topped with grated cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 175 g spaghetti pasta
- 4 pieces tuyo
- 2 medium tomatoes, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon butter
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- Chili flakes, to taste
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Grated cheese, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the tuyo until cooked. Remove the fish, let it cool slightly, then flake it and remove the bones.
2. Cook the spaghetti in boiling water according to the package instructions until al dente. Reserve some pasta water before draining.
3. Melt the butter in a pan and add the cooking oil. Sauté the garlic until fragrant.
4. Add the chopped tomatoes and chili flakes. Stir, then add the tuyo flakes.
5. Add the cooked spaghetti and toss until coated. Pour in a little reserved pasta water if the pasta is too dry.
6. Season with ground black pepper and mix well.
7. Transfer to a serving plate and top with grated cheese. Serve hot.

Short Description: Dried squid fried until crispy and served with vinegar dip or pickled vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 30 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 12 pieces medium dried squid
- 4 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Soak the dried squid in water for 30 minutes to soften it.
2. Drain the squid and pat it dry with paper towels.
3. Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium-low heat.
4. Add the dried squid and lower the heat. Fry for about 3 minutes on each side, pressing gently with a spatula to help it cook evenly.
5. Before removing the squid, increase the heat to medium and fry for another minute until crispy.
6. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels. Let it cool slightly so it becomes crispier.
7. Serve with vinegar dip or pickled vegetables.

Short Description: Fried tilapia in a sweet and sour sauce with bell peppers and pineapple.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces tilapia, cleaned
- 2 tablespoons Knorr Liquid Seasoning
- 1 red bell pepper, julienned
- 1 green bell pepper, julienned
- 1 carrot, julienned
- 5 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 onion, sliced
- 2 thumbs ginger, julienned
- 2 tablespoons cornstarch
- 2 cups water
- 5 1/2 tablespoons white vinegar
- 8 tablespoons tomato ketchup
- 7 tablespoons white sugar
- 1 1/4 cups oil
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Apply the Knorr Liquid Seasoning all over the tilapia. Let it stand for 10 minutes so the fish can absorb the seasoning.
2. Heat around 1 cup of oil in a pan. Once hot, fry the fish until golden brown. Flip to fry the opposite side. Remove from the pan and set aside.
3. Make the sauce by heating 3 tablespoons of oil in a cooking pot. Sauté the onion and garlic for 10 seconds, then add the ginger and sauté for 12 seconds.
4. Pour in the white vinegar and water. Let it boil.
5. Add the tomato ketchup and stir until completely blended.
6. Add the sugar and stir until fully incorporated.
7. Add the carrots and bell peppers. Cook for 3 minutes.
8. Combine the cornstarch with 3 tablespoons of water. Mix well, then pour into the cooking pot. Stir until the sauce thickens.
9. Season with salt and ground black pepper. Add the tilapia and cook for 3 minutes.
10. Transfer to a serving plate and serve with rice.

Short Description: Steamed grouper fish topped with mayonnaise and garnished with chopped eggs, sweet pickle relish, carrots, and bell peppers.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small whole lapu-lapu, cleaned and scaled
- 2 teaspoons sampalok powder
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
- 1/2 lemon or 2 calamansi
- 2 stalks spring onions
- 1/2 medium carrot, peeled
- 1/2 red bell pepper
- 2 hard-boiled eggs, peeled
- 1/3 cup mayonnaise
- 1 tablespoon atchara
Steps:
1. Rinse the fish thoroughly and pat it dry.
2. Rub the sampalok powder over the fish, inside and out. Season with salt and pepper, then let it stand for 10–15 minutes.
3. Stuff the fish cavity with lemon or calamansi and spring onions.
4. Place the fish in a steamer and steam for 20–25 minutes, or until the flesh flakes easily with a fork.
5. While the fish is steaming, separate the egg whites from the yolks and chop them finely.
6. Boil the carrot until tender but still firm. Let it cool, then dice it. Remove the seeds from the bell pepper and chop it finely.
7. Transfer the cooked fish to a serving platter. Remove the calamansi or lemon and spring onions from the cavity.
8. Let the fish cool, then refrigerate until completely cold.
9. Spread the mayonnaise over the fish.
10. Garnish with the chopped egg whites, egg yolks, carrots, bell pepper, and sweet pickle relish. Add the black olive as an optional decoration.
11. Chill until ready to serve.

Short Description: A Filipino sour soup made with lapu-lapu, fresh vegetables, and tamarind seasoning.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g lapu-lapu, cleaned and cut into serving pieces
- 2 cups rice washing water
- 1 medium onion, quartered
- 2 medium tomatoes, quartered
- 1 long green chili (siling haba)
- 2 pieces okra, halved
- 1/4 medium radish (labanos), sliced into rounds
- 1/2 pack (10 g) Knorr Sinigang sa Sampalok Mix Original
- 1/4 bunch kangkong, cut into 2-inch lengths
Steps:
1. Put the onion, tomatoes, and rice washing water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 8 minutes.
2. Gently add the lapu-lapu to the pot.
3. Add the green chili, okra, radish, and sinigang mix. Simmer until the fish and vegetables are cooked.
4. Add the kangkong and simmer for 1 minute.
5. Taste the broth and adjust the seasoning if needed. Serve hot.

Short Description: Salmon head simmered in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 750 ml water
- 2 tomatoes, cut into quarters
- 1/2 medium onion, cut into quarters
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, cut into 4–5 slices
- 1/2 medium white radish, cut into thin diagonal slices
- 3 pieces yardlong beans, trimmed and cut into 3-inch pieces
- 1 salmon head, gills removed, cleaned, and cut in half
- 1/2 medium eggplant, cut into 1-inch diagonal pieces
- 3 pieces okra
- 2 green chili peppers
- 1/2 packet tamarind soup mix
- 1/2 tablespoon fish sauce
- 1/2 bunch kangkong, hard parts of the stalks trimmed
Steps:
1. In a pot over high heat, bring the water to a boil.
2. Add the tomatoes, onion, ginger, yardlong beans, and white radish. Lower the heat to medium and cover the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the white radish is just half cooked.
3. Add the salmon head, eggplant, okra, and green chili peppers. Pour in the tamarind soup mix and fish sauce. Gently stir to avoid breaking the fish into pieces. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the fish is cooked.
4. Add the kangkong and cook for a few seconds, then turn off the heat.
5. Transfer to a serving soup dish and serve with steamed rice.

Short Description: Shrimp in a sour tamarind broth with tomatoes and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 750 grams large shrimp, head-on and unpeeled
- 2 1/2 cups water
- 1–2 medium ripe tomatoes, cut into quarters
- 1/2 medium onion, cut into quarters
- 1/2 medium radish (labanos), sliced
- 1/2 pack (11 g) tamarind soup mix (sinigang mix)
- 1/2 small bunch yard-long beans (sitaw), cut into 2-inch pieces
- 3 pieces okra
- 1/2 medium eggplant, sliced
- 1–2 green finger chilies (sili sigang)
- 1–1 1/2 tablespoons fish sauce
- 1/2 bunch water spinach (kangkong), tips and upper stalks only
Steps:
1. Bring the water to a boil in a pot over medium-high heat.
2. Add the tomatoes and onions. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the radish and cook for another 2 minutes.
3. Add the shrimp. Once the shrimp turn pink, add the tamarind mix. Simmer for about 2 minutes.
4. Add the beans followed by the okra and chili. Bring back to a boil and cook for 2 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce and add the eggplant. Cook for 1 minute. Lastly, add the water spinach. Push the leaves down gently until submerged. Simmer for another minute.
6. Transfer to serving bowls and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Beef in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 kilogram beef neck bones
- 25 grams MAGGI® Magic Sinigang sa Sampaloc
- 8 pieces sitaw (string beans), cut into 2-inch pieces
- 2 pieces gabi (taro), peeled
- 1 Chinese eggplant (talong), sliced diagonally
- 1–2 siling pansigang (long green peppers)
- 5 pieces okra
- 1/2 labanos (white radish), sliced
- 2 tomatoes, cut into wedges
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium onion, cut into wedges
- 2 cups rice water
- 2 cups water
- 1/2 bunch kangkong, leaves separated from the stalks
- 1/2 tablespoon beef powder
- 1 1/2 tablespoons oil
- Patis (fish sauce), to taste
Steps:
1. Heat the oil in a large pot. Sauté the garlic, onion, and half of the tomatoes until the onions soften.
2. Add the beef and continue to sauté until it browns.
3. Pour in the rice water. Cover the pot and let the liquid boil. Lower the heat and simmer until the beef becomes tender. Add water as needed and skim off any scum that rises to the surface.
4. Add the MAGGI® Magic Sinigang sa Sampaloc and beef powder. Stir.
5. Add the gabi and labanos. Cover and continue cooking until the gabi softens.
6. Add the talong, remaining tomatoes, and siling pansigang. Continue cooking for 5 minutes.
7. Season with patis.
8. Add the okra and sitaw. Continue cooking for another 5 minutes.
9. Add the kangkong and cook for 1 minute.
10. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Corned beef in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 can (about 325 grams) chunky corned beef
- 5 cups water
- 1 small onion, peeled and quartered
- 2 tomatoes, quartered
- 1 tablespoon patis (fish sauce)
- 1 small labanos (radish), peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 pack tamarind soup base mix (about 20 grams)
- 2 bunches pechay, ends trimmed
- Salt, to taste
- 1–2 siling haba (finger chilies), optional
Steps:
1. In a soup pot over medium heat, combine the water, onion, and tomatoes. Bring to a boil.
2. Add the labanos. Lower the heat and cook for about 3 to 5 minutes or until tender-crisp.
3. Add the tamarind soup base mix and stir until dissolved.
4. Add the pechay and cook for about 1 minute.
5. Add the corned beef and cook, gently breaking it apart into large chunks with a spoon, for about 2 to 3 minutes or until heated through.
6. Season with patis and salt to taste.
7. Add the siling haba if desired.
8. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Fish in a sour broth thickened with miso and tamarind.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 medium onion, chopped
- 1/2 thumb-sized ginger, sliced
- 3 tomatoes, chopped
- 1/2 cup miso paste
- 3–4 cups water
- 1/2 medium labanos (radish), sliced
- 1 1/2 tablespoons tamarind soup mix (sinigang mix)
- 1/2 kilogram salmon, cut into pieces
- 2 siling haba (long green peppers)
- 3 pieces okra
- 1/2 medium talong (eggplant), sliced
- 1/2 bunch mustasa (mustard leaves)
- Salt, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat the oil in a large pot. Sauté the garlic and onion, then add the ginger. Cook until aromatic. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften.
2. Add the miso paste and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the water, mix, and bring to a boil.
3. Add the labanos and cook until tender. Add the tamarind soup mix and salt. Stir well.
4. Add the salmon, talong, okra, and siling haba. Gently mix and cook for 5 minutes or until the fish and vegetables are cooked through.
5. Add the mustasa and cook for another minute.
6. Remove from heat and serve.

Short Description: Fish in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram fish, sliced
- 20 grams Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix Original
- 1 tomato, cubed
- 1/2 cup labanos (daikon radish), sliced
- 1/2 onion, cut into wedges
- 1 1/2 cups kangkong (water spinach)
- 5 pieces okra
- 1 talong (Chinese eggplant), sliced
- 1 siling pansigang (long green pepper)
- 1 liter water
- Oil, for frying
- Salt, for seasoning the fish
- Patis (fish sauce) and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Slice the fish as needed. Sprinkle salt all over the fish and rub it in. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes.
2. Heat oil in a pan. Fry the fish slices until golden brown. Turn them over and fry the other side. Remove the fish and place it on a clean plate. Set aside.
3. Boil the water in a large cooking pot. Add the tomato, onion, and labanos. Continue boiling for 5 minutes.
4. Add the Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix and stir.
5. Put the fried fish into the pot. Let the liquid boil, then adjust the heat to low to medium. Continue boiling for 7 minutes.
6. Add the talong and siling pansigang. Cook for 3 minutes.
7. Add the okra. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
8. Season with ground black pepper and patis.
9. Add the kangkong. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
10. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve warm with rice.

Short Description: Beef ribs in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram beef ribs
- 20 grams Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix Original
- 1/2 bunch kangkong, stalks and leaves separated
- 1/2 Chinese eggplant (talong), sliced
- 1 tomato, quartered
- 1–2 siling pansigang (long green peppers)
- 4 pieces okra
- 1/2 small labanos (daikon radish), sliced
- 5 pieces sitaw (snake beans), cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/2 medium onion, quartered
- 4–5 cups water
- 1 tablespoon patis (fish sauce)
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
Steps:
1. Combine the water and beef ribs in a pressure cooker. Pressure cook for 25 to 30 minutes. You can transfer the beef to a larger cooking pot once it becomes tender, if needed.
2. Add the onion and tomato. Cook for 3 minutes.
3. Add the Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc Mix. Stir.
4. Put the labanos into the pot. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
5. Add the siling pansigang, okra, sitaw, talong, and kangkong stalks. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
6. Season with patis and ground black pepper.
7. Add the kangkong leaves. Cover the pot and turn off the heat. Let it sit for 5 minutes.
8. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.
9. Share and enjoy!

Short Description: Pork in a sour broth soured with guava, with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 11 minutes
Overall Time: 21 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups (375 ml) water
- 1/2 onion, cut into quarters
- 1 tomato, cut into quarters
- 1 gabi (taro), peeled and cut into quarters
- 1 pouch (40 g) Mama Sita’s Sinigang sa Bayabas Mix
- 1/2 labanos (radish), peeled and sliced diagonally
- 1 siling haba (finger chili), sliced
- Patis (fish sauce), to taste
- 50 grams talbos ng kamote (sweet potato tops)
Steps:
1. Boil the water, then add the onion, tomatoes, and gabi. Simmer for 5 minutes.
2. Add the Mama Sita’s Sinigang sa Bayabas Mix. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes.
3. Add the labanos and siling haba. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes or until the vegetables are cooked. Season with patis.
4. Remove from heat. Add the talbos ng kamote and cover for a few minutes.
5. Serve hot.

Short Description: Pork ribs in a sour broth soured with kamias.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 57 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 12 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram pork belly (liempo), sliced
- 2 pieces gabi (taro), peeled
- 1/2 bunch kangkong, chopped and cleaned
- 1 tomato, quartered
- 4–5 pieces sitaw (string beans), cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/2 medium onion, quartered
- 1/2 Chinese eggplant (talong), sliced
- 3–4 pieces okra
- 6 pieces kamias (bilimbi)
- 1 siling pansigang (long green pepper)
- 3 cups (750 ml) water
- 1 tablespoon patis (fish sauce)
Steps:
1. Combine the water, tomato, onion, and kamias in a cooking pot. Let boil.
2. Add the pork slices. Let the water re-boil. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
3. Add the gabi and siling pansigang. Cover and continue to simmer for another 30 minutes or until the pork is tender.
4. Add the patis. Stir.
5. Add the okra, sitaw, and talong. Cook for 5 minutes.
6. Add the kangkong. Cover the cooking pot and turn the heat off. Let the residual heat cook the kangkong.
7. Transfer to a serving bowl.
8. Serve and enjoy.

Short Description: Pork baby back ribs soup in sour broth with okra and bok choy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 50 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kg pork baby back ribs
- 1 bunch bok choy (pechay)
- 4 cups water (960 ml)
- 1/2 packet Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc with Gabi (about 18 g)
- 5 pieces sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 3 pieces okra
- 1/2 Chinese eggplant, sliced
- 1 long green chili pepper
- 1/3 cup daikon radish (labanos), sliced
- 1 tomato, quartered
- 1/2 onion, cut into wedges
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- Fish sauce and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat the cooking oil in a pot. Sauté the onion and tomato until the onion softens.
2. Add the pork ribs and sauté until lightly browned.
3. Pour in the water and cover the pot. Bring to a boil, lower the heat, and simmer until the pork is tender. Add more water if needed.
4. Add the Knorr Sinigang sa Sampaloc with Gabi mix and radish. Stir and continue cooking.
5. Add the green chili, sitaw, okra, and eggplant. Cook until the vegetables are tender.
6. Add the pechay and cook for another 3 minutes.
7. Season with fish sauce and ground black pepper to taste.
8. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Squid in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 small alimasag, cut in half
- 1 can (20 oz) young green jackfruit, drained and chopped
- 1 sachet Knorr Ginataang Gulay Recipe Mix (33 g)
- 1/2 cup malunggay leaves
- 1 1/4 cups water (300 ml)
- 1 tablespoon fish sauce
- 1 siling haba or siling labuyo (optional)
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 1/2 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced
- 1 1/2 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat the cooking oil in a pot.
2. Sauté the garlic, onion, and ginger.
3. Add the young jackfruit and sauté for 3 minutes.
4. Combine the Ginataang Gulay Mix with 1 cup water (240 ml). Mix well.
5. Add the chili and pour the mixture into the pot. Stir and bring to a boil. Cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally.
6. Add the crabs, cover, and cook for 10 minutes or until fully cooked.
7. Add the malunggay leaves and fish sauce. Stir and cook for another 5 minutes, or until the sauce reaches your desired consistency.
8. Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Fish cooked in coconut milk and tomatoes with a hint of spice.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram fish (tilapia, galunggong, or tanigue), cleaned and rubbed with salt
- 4 pieces kamias (bilimbi)
- 1 medium tomato, cut into wedges
- 1/2 teaspoon whole peppercorns
- 3/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
Steps:
1. Arrange the fish, kamias, and tomatoes alternately in a wide cooking pot.
2. Sprinkle the salt and whole peppercorns over the fish, then pour in the water.
3. Cover the pot and bring the liquid to a boil over medium heat.
4. Reduce the heat to low once the liquid starts to boil. Continue cooking for 15 to 20 minutes or until the fish is fully cooked.
5. Turn off the heat and carefully transfer the pinangat to a serving plate.
6. Serve with steamed rice.

Recipe Name: Ginataang Alimasag with Sitaw at Kalabasa
Short Description: Blue crabs cooked in coconut milk with snake beans and calabaza squash.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces alimasag (blue crabs)
- 1/4 sachet Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix (10 g)
- 10 pieces sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/2 kilo kalabasa, cubed
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, minced
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed and chopped
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 1 2/3 cups water (400 ml)
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Steam the crabs for 12 minutes. Prepare the vegetables by cutting the sitaw into 2-inch pieces, cubing the kalabasa, mincing the ginger, chopping the onion, and crushing the garlic.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Sauté the garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion becomes translucent.
3. Combine the water and Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix in a bowl. Stir until well blended, then pour the mixture into the pan. Bring to a boil.
4. Add the crabs and kalabasa. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
5. Add the sitaw and cook for another 8 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender and the crabs are fully cooked.
6. Season with salt and ground black pepper if needed.
7. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Grilled cubes of coagulated chicken blood served on skewers with a savory dipping sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 30 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilo coagulated chicken blood
- 1/2 Knorr Chicken Cube
- 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons white vinegar
- 6 tablespoons water (90 ml)
- 2 tablespoons garlic oil

DIPPING SAUCE
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 6 tablespoons white vinegar
- 1 teaspoon fish sauce
- 2–3 cloves garlic, sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2–3 siling labuyo, chopped
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Cut the coagulated chicken blood into cubes.
2. Place the cubes in a pot. Add the soy sauce, vinegar, and water, then bring to a boil. Gently spoon the liquid over the cubes to coat them.
3. Add the garlic powder, ground black pepper, and Knorr Chicken Cube. Cook for 5 minutes.
4. Transfer the chicken blood to a clean plate without the sauce and let it cool. Carefully thread the cubes onto bamboo skewers.
5. Brush the cubes with garlic oil. Arrange them in an air fryer and cook at 200°C for 5 minutes per side, ensuring they are thoroughly heated.
6. Combine all the dipping sauce ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
7. Serve the betamax with the dipping sauce.

Short Description: Tulingan simmered in vinegar, ginger, and chilies for a tangy, savory dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced
- 1 small onion, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 long green chili
- 1/2 teaspoon whole peppercorns
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tablespoon vinegar
- 1 tablespoon fish sauce
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- 2 tablespoons water (30 ml)
- Sugar or MSG, to taste
Steps:
1. Clean the tulingan thoroughly and remove the gills and internal organs.
2. Arrange the fish in a pot. Add the salt, ginger, onion, garlic, long green chili, peppercorns, and bay leaf.
3. Pour in the vinegar, fish sauce, cooking oil, and water.
4. Cover the pot and bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat.
5. Lower the heat and simmer until the fish is cooked and tender. Add a little water if needed to prevent the sauce from drying out.
6. Serve hot with steamed rice.

Short Description: Tulingan simmered in coconut milk with ginger, garlic, and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 40 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces tulingan (bullet tuna)
- 1 1/2 ounces (about 40 grams) pork fat, sliced
- 1 cup (240 ml) coconut milk
- 5 pieces kamias (bilimbi)
- 1 1/2 thumbs ginger, julienned
- 2–3 siling labuyo (Thai chili peppers)
- 1/2 Chinese eggplant (talong), sliced
- 1/2 onion, sliced
- 2–3 cloves garlic, crushed and minced
- 1/2 teaspoon patis (fish sauce)
- 7/8 cup (210 ml) water
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Clean the fish thoroughly. Create a slit on both sides and rub salt all over. Let it stay for 10 to 15 minutes.
2. Arrange the pork fat, kamias, fish, and ginger in a cooking pot. Pour in the water. Cover and let it boil. Continue to cook over medium heat for 40 minutes.
3. Pour the coconut milk into the pot. Add the garlic, onion, and chili. Cover and continue to boil for another 40 minutes over low to medium heat.
4. Add the eggplant. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes.
5. Season with patis and ground black pepper.
6. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.
7. Share and enjoy!

Short Description: Tulingan slow-cooked in salt and spices until tender, bones and all.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours 50 minutes
Overall Time: 3 hours 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram medium-sized tulingan (bullet tuna)
- 125 grams pork fat or pork belly, optional
- Salt, to taste
- 5 pieces dried kamias (bilimbi)
- Water, as needed
Steps:
1. Clean the fish by removing the gills and innards. You may remove the tails by snapping and pulling them away. Wash thoroughly.
2. Make a long slit along the flesh on both sides. Press with your palm to flatten. Do the same with the remaining fish. Soak in a basin or bowl with water for several minutes to remove remaining blood.
3. Drain and lightly pat the fish dry. Rub generous amounts of salt into each fish, including the cavities and crevices.
4. Wrap the top part of each fish with banana leaves.
5. In a pot, arrange the pork fat and kamias at the bottom so the fish will not touch the bottom of the pot. Fill the pot with water just enough to cover the top of the fish.
6. Cover the pot and simmer over low heat for 3 hours or longer. Add water as needed. Once the desired tenderness is achieved, let the water dry out and allow the oil to render from the pork fat.
7. Transfer the cooked fish to a serving plate and enjoy with steaming-hot rice.

Short Description: Mudfish simmered in coconut milk with ginger and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram dalag (mudfish), cleaned and cut as desired
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/2 onion, sliced
- 1/2 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced
- 1 cup (240 ml) coconut milk (gata)
- 1 tablespoon patis (fish sauce)
- 1/2 bunch pechay, chopped
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
- Salt, to taste
Steps:
1. In a pan or casserole, sauté the garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant. Add 1/2 cup of the coconut milk, patis, and ground black pepper. Let it simmer over low heat for 1 minute.
2. Add the dalag and simmer until the fish is cooked.
3. Add the pechay and season with salt to taste. Cook for 1 minute.
4. Pour in the remaining 1/2 cup coconut milk. Let it come to a gentle simmer, then turn off the heat immediately. Do not let it boil for too long so the coconut milk stays creamy.
5. Serve hot with freshly cooked rice.

Short Description: Fish simmered in coconut milk with ginger and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram tanigue (king mackerel), cut into cross-section slices
- 1/2 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced into thin strips
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 medium talong (eggplant), cut into chunks
- 1/2 bunch leafy vegetables, cut into pieces
- 1/2 tablespoon bagoong alamang (shrimp paste)
- 1–2 siling labuyo, whole or sliced
- 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) coconut milk (gata)
- Salt, pepper, and patis (fish sauce), to taste
- Oil, for searing and sautéing
Steps:
1. Season the fish with salt. Heat oil in a wide pan. Sear the fish for about 2 minutes per side or until lightly browned. Set aside.
2. Add the ginger and cook until fragrant. Add the onion and garlic. Sauté until soft and starting to caramelize.
3. Stir in the bagoong alamang and cook for 1 minute. If not using shrimp paste, add patis and salt later.
4. Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Season with patis or salt. Add water if needed to make the sauce thinner.
5. Add the talong and siling labuyo. Simmer until the talong is tender.
6. Layer some leafy vegetables at the bottom of the pan. Place the fish on top, then add the remaining leafy vegetables.
7. Add the remaining leafy vegetables and simmer for about 5 minutes, or until the greens are wilted and the fish has absorbed the flavors.
8. Serve hot with steamed rice.

Short Description: Grilled tuna jaw, smoky, juicy, and flavorful with a savory marinade.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 3 hours 8 minutes
Overall Time: 3 hours 28 minutes
Ingredients:
- 750 grams tuna jaw (panga ng tuna), rinsed

TUNA MARINADE
- 1/2 cup soy sauce
- 3 cloves garlic, crushed and minced
- 4–5 red chilies, chopped
- 2 tablespoons brown sugar
- 2 calamansi, juiced
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper

TUNA BASTING SAUCE
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon white sugar
Steps:
1. Combine the soy sauce, calamansi juice, ground black pepper, and chili in a medium bowl. Stir.
2. Add the garlic and brown sugar. Stir thoroughly until the sugar dissolves.
3. Place the tuna in a resealable plastic bag. Pour in the soy sauce marinade. Let the air out of the bag and seal it. Refrigerate and marinate overnight.
4. Prepare the basting sauce by combining the soy sauce and white sugar in a bowl. Stir well and set aside.
