5. Heat the grill. Arrange the tuna jaw over the cooking grate. Brush a generous amount of basting sauce over the top of the fish. Grill for 3 to 5 minutes.
6. Turn the tuna over. Baste the top and sides. Continue grilling for another 5 minutes.
7. Gently flip the fish jaw again and grill the other side for 5 to 7 minutes.
8. Flip it back for the last time and cook the opposite side for 5 minutes.
9. Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce, calamansi, and chili.
10. Serve and enjoy.

Short Description: Chopped tuna sautéed with onions, chilies, and calamansi for a savory sisig.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Allergens: Fish, Soy, Milk (if using butter or margarine)
Ingredients:
- 450 grams canned tuna
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 2 red chilies, chopped
- 1 tablespoon butter or margarine
- Chicharon, for topping
- Green chili, for topping
- Calamansi, optional
Steps:
1. Drain the canned tuna very well. In a pan over medium heat, cook the tuna until browned.
2. Add the soy sauce and ground black pepper. Stir until well incorporated.
3. Add the onion and red chili. Stir until well distributed. Remove from heat.
4. Place a sizzling plate over medium-high heat. Once heated, melt the butter or margarine.
5. Transfer the tuna mixture to the sizzling plate and let it sizzle for a few minutes.
6. Remove from heat, then top with chicharon, green chili, and calamansi.

Short Description: Fish in a ginger-flavored broth with green papaya and chili leaves.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram fish, cleaned and sliced into serving pieces
- 1 large tomato, coarsely chopped
- 1/2 medium onion, coarsely chopped
- 1 cup malunggay leaves
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, peeled and crushed
- 1/2 stalk lemongrass (tanglad), pounded and tied in a knot
- 1 siling labuyo, optional
- 4 cups (1 liter) water
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
Steps:
1. Fill a cooking pot with about 4 cups of cold water.
2. Add the crushed ginger and lemongrass. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, lower the heat to medium-high and simmer for 15 minutes so the flavors of the ginger and lemongrass infuse the water.
3. Add the siling labuyo, onion, and tomatoes. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 5 minutes.
4. Carefully add the fish slices to the pot. Season with salt and pepper, then cook for another 15 minutes.
5. Turn off the heat and add the malunggay leaves. Stir and allow the leaves to wilt for about 1 minute.
6. Serve hot.

Short Description: Shrimp in a ginger-flavored broth with green papaya and chili leaves.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups water (480 ml)
- 1/2 thumb-sized piece of ginger, crushed
- 1 stalk lemongrass, pounded and tied
- 1 small onion, quartered
- 1 tomato, quartered
- 1 siling panigang
- 1/4 kilogram assorted seafood (shrimp, squid, and tanigue)
- 1 sachet (8 g) MAGGI Magic Sarap
- 1/4 cup malunggay leaves
Steps:
1. Simmer the water with the ginger, lemongrass, onion, tomato, and siling panigang for 10 minutes.
2. Add the shrimp, squid, and tanigue. Season with MAGGI Magic Sarap and cook until the seafood is fully cooked.
3. Stir in the malunggay leaves and cook briefly until wilted.
4. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

Short Description: Sardines mixed with eggs and fried into a savory omelet.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, chopped
- 1 egg
- A pinch of ground black pepper
- A pinch of salt
- 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 2 tablespoons sliced spring onions
- 1 small can sardines in tomato sauce, drained and sauce reserved
- Calamansi juice, for serving
Steps:
1. In a pan over medium heat, add the cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add the onion and garlic. Sauté until fragrant and the onion is translucent. Remove from the pan and transfer to a plate. Turn off the heat for now.
2. Add the egg, all-purpose flour, drained sardines, spring onions, cooked onion, cooked garlic, salt, and pepper to a bowl. Mix everything together.
3. In the same pan over medium heat, add about 2–3 tablespoons of the mixture and cook each side until browned.
4. Drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
5. To serve, place the reserved sardine sauce in a bowl and add calamansi juice. Serve with rice or bread.

Short Description: Shrimp paste sautéed with garlic, onions, and tomatoes, a salty, savory condiment.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup bagoong alamang (shrimp paste)
- 1 tablespoon oil
- 1 tablespoon sugar
- 1 siling labuyo, chopped, optional
- 1/2 teaspoon cornstarch
- 1 teaspoon water
Steps:
1. Using a fine-mesh sieve, rinse the bagoong alamang under cold running water to remove excess saltiness. Drain well.
2. In a wide pan over medium heat, heat the oil.
3. Add the sugar and cook, stirring regularly, until the sugar is dissolved and lightly browned.
4. Add the bagoong and cook, stirring regularly, for about 3 to 5 minutes or until the color darkens.
5. In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch and water. Stir until smooth.
6. Add the cornstarch slurry to the pan and stir until well distributed. Continue to cook until the bagoong is slightly thickened.
7. Add the chopped siling labuyo if desired.
8. Serve as a condiment with green mangoes or other dishes.

Short Description: Small fish folded into egg and fried into a golden omelet.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram dulong (silverfish), rinsed and drained well
- 1/2 sachet (4 g) MAGGI® Magic Sarap®
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1/2 cup oil
Steps:
1. Season the dulong with MAGGI® Magic Sarap®. Mix in the beaten eggs.
2. Preheat the oil in a large pan.
3. Carefully drop 2 spoonfuls of the mixture into the hot oil.
4. Fry until golden brown.
5. Transfer to a cooling rack to drain excess oil.
6. Transfer to a serving plate and serve with your preferred dipping sauce.

Short Description: Snails simmered in creamy coconut milk with ginger and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kilogram kuhol (apple snails), cleaned and shelled
- 1/2 large bunch spinach, washed
- 1 cup (240 ml) coconut milk (gata)
- 3 red chilies or siling labuyo
- 1/2 medium onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed and chopped
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced
- 2 tablespoons bagoong alamang (shrimp paste)
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 1/2 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat the cooking oil in a cooking pot.
2. Once the oil is hot, sauté the garlic and onion. Add the ginger and continue to cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
3. Add the kuhol to the cooking pot. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
4. Add the bagoong alamang and chilies. Stir.
5. Pour in the coconut milk. Let it boil, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
6. Add the ground black pepper and spinach. Stir and cook for 5 minutes without covering.
7. Transfer to a serving bowl.
8. Serve as a pulutan or as a main dish with warm white rice.

Short Description: Frog stuffed with seasoned ground pork and fried until golden, a Kapampangan specialty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 large edible frogs (palakang bukid)
- 60 grams ground pork
- 1 clove garlic, minced

FOR THE PORK STUFFING
- 1/8 teaspoon salt
- 3/4 teaspoon vinegar
- 1/8 teaspoon ground pepper

FOR THE MARINADE
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon vinegar
- 1/4 teaspoon ground pepper
- 1/2 teaspoon brown sugar
Steps:
1. In a bowl, combine the ground pork, minced garlic, salt, vinegar, and ground pepper. Set aside.
2. Clean the frogs and remove the skin, head, and intestines.
3. Use the ground pork mixture as the stuffing. Sew the openings closed to prevent the stuffing from spilling out.
4. Mix the salt, vinegar, ground pepper, and brown sugar to make the marinade.
5. Pour the marinade over the stuffed frogs.
6. Let the frogs stand for 30 minutes.
7. Deep-fry until golden brown.
8. Serve with fried rice or steamed plain rice.

Short Description: Rice-field crickets cooked adobo-style in vinegar, garlic, and tomatoes, crunchy and tangy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram kamaru (rice field crickets), cleaned
- 1 large native onion, finely chopped
- 1/2 cup vinegar
- 3 tablespoons cooking oil
- 6 cloves garlic, peeled and chopped
- 2 medium tomatoes, thinly sliced
- Chili pepper, to taste
- Salt and ground pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Clean the crickets and remove the feet. Wash them properly, then drain.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté the garlic, onion, and tomatoes.
3. When the tomatoes start to simmer, add the kamaru and mix well.
4. Add the vinegar and continue cooking.
5. After 10 to 15 minutes, season with salt, ground pepper, and chili to taste.
6. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

Short Description: Fermented rice and fish, tangy and salty, a traditional Kapampangan condiment.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 30 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 8–10 days
Ingredients:
- 1 cup rice
- 1 piece tilapia fillet, or another fish of your choice
- Rock salt, as needed
- Water, for cooking the rice
Steps:
1. Wash the rice at least 4 times or until the water becomes clear. Cook it in a rice cooker with 1 1/2 cups water to make it soft and mashy.
2. Once cooked, set the rice aside and let it cool completely. The source suggests covering it and placing it in the refrigerator to speed up the cooling.
3. Season the cooled rice with rock salt. Add enough salt according to your taste.
4. Clean and fillet the fish. Remove the blood and fat.
5. Place the fish fillet in a colander or strainer to drain the water.
6. Once drained, add salt to the fillet, covering each side as if making salted fish.
7. In a clean fermentation container, layer the rice and fish. Make sure the top and bottom layers are rice and press each layer down evenly.
8. Continue layering until all the rice and fish have been used.
9. Cover the container with cling wrap to prevent air from coming in, or use an airlock container.
10. Store at room temperature for 8–10 days. The longer it ferments, the more sour it becomes.

Short Description: Fermented rice and shrimp, tangy and salty, a traditional Kapampangan condiment.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Fermenting Time: 3 days
Overall Time: 3 days and 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 Chinese eggplants
- 1 egg
- 2 tablespoons chopped green onions
- 2 tablespoons cornstarch
- 4 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 1/4 teaspoon baking powder
- 2 teaspoons salt for removing moisture
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 cup water (240 ml)
- Cooking oil, for deep-frying

DIPPING SAUCE
- 1/2 cup white vinegar
- 1 teaspoon soy sauce
- 1/4 red onion, chopped
- 1 tablespoon chopped green onions
- 1 siling labuyo, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon sugar
- 1/8 teaspoon salt
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
Steps:
1. Grate the eggplants into a bowl. Add the salt and toss until evenly coated. Let them sit for 10 minutes.
2. Add the water and rinse the eggplants to remove the salt. Squeeze them thoroughly to drain the water, or place them in a clean cheesecloth and wring them out.
3. Combine the cornstarch, flour, and baking powder in a separate bowl. Mix well and set aside.
4. Beat the egg in a large bowl. Add the drained eggplant, green onions, and ground black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
5. Gradually add the flour mixture and stir until all ingredients are well combined.
6. Heat enough cooking oil in a small pan for deep-frying.
7. Scoop about 3 tablespoons of the mixture into the hot oil for each fritter. Fry until both sides are brown and crispy. Drain excess oil on a plate lined with paper towels.
8. For the dipping sauce, combine the vinegar, sugar, salt, ground black pepper, and soy sauce in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave for 30 seconds, then stir until well blended.
9. Add the chopped siling labuyo, red onion, garlic, and green onions to the sauce.
10. Serve the crispy eggplant fritters with the spicy vinegar dipping sauce.

Short Description: Fermented mustard greens, tangy and slightly sour, a traditional pickle.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 3–5 days
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram fresh mustard greens (mustasa)
- 1 cup water
- 2 tablespoons rock salt
Steps:
1. Wash every leaf thoroughly with water.
2. Pat the leaves dry with a paper towel and leave them to dry and slightly wither for a few hours or overnight.
3. Tie each leaf into a knot or cut them into pieces about 1 inch long.
4. Place the leaves in a bowl. Sprinkle them with the rock salt and add the water.
5. Gently massage the leaves by rubbing and slightly squeezing them with your hands for 3 to 5 minutes.
6. Transfer the leaves to a jar and fill it with the same brine solution, making sure the leaves are fully submerged.
7. Cover the jar and place it in a dark place at room temperature for 3 to 5 days.
8. Once ready, place it in the refrigerator if you are not using it immediately.

Short Description: Salty, rich crab fat sautéed with garlic, a savory spread for rice.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked rice
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1/2 tbsp chopped ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, chopped
- 2 tbsp chopped onion
- 1 tbsp taba ng talangka
- 1/4 kg shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp tinapa flakes
- 1/4 cup squid rings
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt to taste
- 2 tbsp green peas
- 1 egg, hard-boiled and sliced
- 1 spring onion, sliced
Steps:
1. Heat the cooking oil in a wok or large frying pan.
2. Sauté the ginger, garlic, and onion until fragrant.
3. Add the taba ng talangka, shrimp, bay leaf, tinapa flakes, and squid rings.
4. Cook for about 3 minutes, or until the seafood changes color and is cooked through.
5. Season with salt to taste.
6. Add the cooked rice and green peas. Mix well and stir-fry until the rice is heated through.
7. Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with sliced hard-boiled egg and spring onion.
8. Serve immediately.

Short Description: Taro leaves wrapped around a seasoned filling and simmered in creamy coconut milk, a Bicolano favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 6 young gabi leaves
- 1/4 kg shrimp, peeled and chopped
- 1/4 kg flaked fish, cooked and deboned
- 1 cup chopped buko meat
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp minced ginger
- 1 tbsp bagoong alamang
- 1 cup coconut milk (240 ml)
- 2 tbsp thick coconut cream
- Salt and ground black pepper to taste
- Clean kitchen thread for tying the leaves
Steps:
1. In a bowl, combine the chopped shrimp, flaked fish, buko meat, onion, and ginger.
2. Wash the gabi leaves carefully and wipe off excess water.
3. Place a portion of the filling in the center of each gabi leaf. Fold the sides over the filling and secure with kitchen thread.
4. Arrange the wrapped leaves in a pan, placing them close together so they stay folded.
5. Spread the bagoong alamang over the wrapped leaves and pour in the coconut milk.
6. Bring to a gentle boil over low heat. Cover and simmer until the gabi leaves are completely tender and the filling is fully cooked, adding a little water if needed.
7. Season with salt and ground black pepper to taste.
8. Remove the kitchen thread before serving. Drizzle with thick coconut cream and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Flaked fish simmered with malunggay leaves and chilies, a Bicolano favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kg tanigue, cut into pieces
- 1 medium onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, chopped
- 2 siling pangsigang
- 1 siling labuyo
- 1/2 cup malunggay leaves
- 1/4 cup vinegar (60 ml)
- 1/8 tsp salt
- 1/8 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp water (30 ml)
- 1 cup coconut milk (240 ml)
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced
Steps:
1. Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add the tanigue and ginger, then boil for about 10 minutes or until the fish is cooked.
2. Remove the fish and let it cool. Remove the skin and bones, then flake the fish into bite-sized pieces.
3. Combine the fish with the vinegar, salt, pepper, and half of the garlic. Let it marinate for 5 minutes.
4. Place the coconut milk and sliced onion in a pan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring gently, until the onion softens.
5. Drain the fish and add it to the coconut milk. Simmer for about 10 minutes.
6. Add the malunggay, siling pangsigang, siling labuyo, and remaining garlic.
7. Cook for another 5–7 minutes, until the sauce thickens and the leaves are tender.
8. Let rest for 5 minutes, then serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Crispy Bicolano fried bananas coated in a rice flour batter and sprinkled with sugar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4 pieces saba bananas, peeled and cut lengthwise in half
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup water (120 ml)
- Cooking oil for frying
Steps:
1. Place the flour in a mixing bowl. Gradually add the water and mix until a smooth, thin batter forms.
2. Add the sliced saba bananas to the batter and coat them well so the pieces stick together.
3. Heat the cooking oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
4. Gather about 4 banana slices together and carefully place them in the hot oil to form one fritter.
5. Fry until golden brown, turning as needed so both sides cook evenly.
6. Remove from the pan and drain on a rack or paper towels.
7. Repeat with the remaining bananas and batter. Serve warm.

Short Description: Taro stems or leaves cooked in coconut milk with chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 2 bundles gabi leaves
- 1 small red onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger
- 2 siling labuyo
- 3 stalks lemongrass
- 1 tsp whole black peppercorns
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 1/2 cups dulong
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 egg
- 2 pieces shrimp
- 1/4 cup calcag (optional)
- 2 cups coconut milk (480 ml)
- Salt and ground black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Wash the gabi leaves and cut off the stalks. Pound the onion, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, siling labuyo, and peppercorns together to make an aromatic paste.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Sauté the aromatic paste until fragrant, then remove from the heat and let it cool slightly.
3. In a bowl, combine the sautéed paste, dulong, flour, and egg. Season with salt and ground black pepper, then mix well.
4. Place two gabi leaves on top of each other. Add 1–2 tablespoons of the dulong mixture, one shrimp, some calcag if using, and about 2 tablespoons of coconut milk.
5. Fold the gabi leaves over the filling and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.
6. Arrange the rolls closely in a pot. Pour the remaining coconut milk over them and add the remaining lemongrass and siling labuyo.
7. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then lower the heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes, or until the gabi leaves are fully cooked and tender.
8. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Taro leaves simmered in creamy coconut milk with chilies, a comforting Bicolano vegetable dish.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces eggplant
- 1/4 kg ground chicken
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1 small onion, minced
- 5 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 red bell pepper, chopped
- 1/2 cup green peas
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 3 eggs
- Salt and ground black pepper to taste
- 8 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat 3 tablespoons of cooking oil in a pan. Sauté the garlic, onion, and tomato until the tomato softens.
2. Add the ground chicken and cook, stirring frequently, until browned and fully cooked.
3. Add the bell pepper and green peas. Sauté for 2 minutes.
4. Add the soy sauce and season with salt and ground black pepper. Cook until the liquid evaporates, then set aside.
5. Grill the eggplants until the inside softens. Let them cool, then peel off the skin.
6. Place each eggplant on a plate and flatten it gently with a fork to form a fan shape.
7. Beat the eggs in a bowl and season with salt and ground black pepper.
8. Dip each flattened eggplant in the beaten eggs and let it soak for 1 minute.
9. Heat the remaining cooking oil in a pan. Place one eggplant in the pan and fry for about 1 1/2 minutes.
10. Spread half of the chicken filling over the eggplant. Pour some beaten egg over the filling, then spoon a little hot oil over it to help bind the filling.
11. Carefully flip the eggplant and cook the other side for about 2 minutes over low to medium heat, until the egg is set and the filling is heated through.
12. Repeat with the remaining eggplant and filling. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Young santol fruit simmered in coconut milk with chilies and shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 37 minutes
Overall Time: 47 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces santol, peeled and seeds removed
- 125 grams ground pork
- 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) coconut cream (gata)
- 1 siling pansigang (long green pepper), sliced crosswise
- 2–3 siling labuyo (Thai chili), chopped
- 1 1/2 tablespoons bagoong alamang (shrimp paste)
- 1/2 medium red onion, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 1/2 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Mince the santol into very small pieces using a food processor or by hand.
2. Place the minced santol in the middle of a cheesecloth. Secure the santol inside the cloth and wring it until all the liquid comes out. Set aside.
3. Heat the oil in a pan. Sauté the garlic and onion.
4. Once the onion starts to become translucent, add the ground pork. Continue cooking until the pork turns light brown.
5. Add the minced santol. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
6. Pour the coconut cream into the pan. Let it boil, then stir and cover the pan. Continue cooking over medium heat until the liquid reduces by half.
7. Add the bagoong alamang, siling pansigang, and siling labuyo. Stir and continue cooking until the liquid completely evaporates.
8. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

Short Description: Fried rice with sweet-savory longanisa, garlic, and egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked rice
- 1 piece longanisa
- 1/3 cup frozen green peas
- 1/3 cup carrots, diced
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1 egg
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and ground black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Crack the egg into a bowl and beat until smooth.
2. Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a pan. Pour in the beaten egg and cook until set. Flip and cook the other side, then remove and set aside.
3. Add the remaining cooking oil to the same pan. Remove the longanisa from its casing if needed, then cook for 5–7 minutes, breaking it into small pieces and stirring occasionally, until fully cooked.
4. Add the butter and let it melt.
5. Add the cooked rice and stir-fry for about 3 minutes until well combined.
6. Cut the cooked egg into small pieces and add it to the pan. Stir-fry for another minute.
7. Add the green peas and diced carrots. Cook for 3–5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
8. Season with salt and ground black pepper. Mix well and serve hot.

Short Description: Bitter melon sautéed with garlic, onion, and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 8 minutes
Overall Time: 18 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 small ampalaya (bitter melon), cleaned and sliced thinly
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 tomato, diced
- 1 onion, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2–3 grams MAGGI® Magic Sarap®
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 1 tablespoon salt, for optional soaking
- Warm water, for optional soaking
Steps:
1. Slice the ampalaya in half lengthwise. Scoop out the seeds and white pith with a spoon.
2. Slice each half into thin half-moon pieces and place them in a large bowl.
3. If you want a milder taste, dissolve 1 tablespoon of salt in warm water. Soak the sliced ampalaya for 5 to 8 minutes, rinse under running water, and gently squeeze it using cheesecloth.
4. Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
5. Sauté the garlic, onion, and tomato until the onion softens and the tomato starts to break down.
6. Add the ampalaya. Sauté for about 1 1/2 minutes, then season with ground black pepper.
7. Pour the beaten eggs over the ampalaya. Let the eggs sit for about 20 seconds before stirring.
8. Continue cooking for about 1 minute, stirring gently until the eggs are just set.
9. Sprinkle the MAGGI® Magic Sarap® over the dish. Stir gently until well blended.
10. Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Bitter melon scrambled with eggs, tomatoes, and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Soaking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 medium ampalaya, sliced
- 3 eggs, beaten
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 2 medium tomatoes, chopped
- 1/4 kilogram pork, bite-sized, optional
- 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Salted water, for soaking the ampalaya
Steps:
1. Soak the bitter melon in salted water for at least 15 to 20 minutes.
2. Place the pork in a hot pan and fry until the oil comes out and the pork is light brown.
3. In the same pan, sauté the garlic, onion, and tomatoes until soft and fragrant. Stir with the meat for a few minutes.
4. Add the bitter melon. Season with salt and pepper. Stir until combined.
5. Pour in the water. Cover and simmer until the bitter melon is tender.
6. When the bitter melon is tender, add the beaten eggs and allow the eggs to cook. Stir for a few minutes, then turn off the heat.
7. Serve with steamed rice and fried fish.

Short Description: Bottle gourd sautéed with garlic, onions, and tomatoes in a light broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium upo, sliced
- 4 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/2 medium onion, diced
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 125 grams ground pork
- 1 1/2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, optional
Steps:
1. Heat the pan and pour in the cooking oil.
2. Sauté the garlic, onion, and tomatoes.
3. Add the ground black pepper and ground pork. Simmer for 3–5 minutes.
4. Add the upo, cover the pan, and simmer for 6 minutes.
5. Add salt to taste. If you want more sauce, add the water and adjust the seasoning.
6. Serve hot.

Short Description: Chayote sautéed with garlic, onions, and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 large sayote
- 2 medium tomatoes
- 3 cloves garlic
- 1 medium onion
- 1/4 kilogram ground pork
- 1 tablespoon fish sauce (patis)
- 2 tablespoons oil
- 1 cup (240 ml) water
- Salt, to taste
Steps:
1. Peel and slice the sayote.
2. Heat oil over medium heat in a pan or wok. Sauté the onion and garlic until soft and aromatic.
3. Add the tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes or until tender.
4. Add the ground pork. Break apart the lumps and cook until no longer pink. Add the patis and cook for about 1 minute.
5. Pour in the water. Cover and simmer for 3–5 minutes. Season with salt if needed.
6. Add the sayote and mix to combine. Cover and cook for about 5 minutes or until tender but still slightly crisp.
7. Remove from heat and transfer to a serving plate.
8. Serve with plain rice or with fried fish or meat.

Short Description: Mung beans sautéed with garlic and tomatoes, topped with crunchy pork rinds.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup dried mung beans
- 3 cups (720 ml) water
- 1/2 tablespoon vegetable oil
- 1/2 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 large tomato, chopped
- 1 cup chicharon with attached meat, chopped
- 1/2 bunch fresh spinach, stems trimmed
- 1/2 tablespoon patis
- Salt and pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Sort through the mung beans, discarding discolored or shriveled beans and any dirt. Rinse under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well.
2. In a large pot, combine the mung beans and water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, skimming off any froth.
3. Lower the heat, cover, and cook for about 45–50 minutes or until the beans have softened and the skins have burst. Add more water as needed to maintain a soupy consistency.
4. In another pot over medium heat, heat the oil. Add the onion and garlic and cook until tender and aromatic.
5. Add the tomatoes and cook, mashing with the back of a spoon, until softened.
6. Add the patis and continue to cook for 1–2 minutes.
7. Add the cooked mung beans, including the liquid. Bring to a boil.
8. Add the chicharon and continue to cook until softened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Add the spinach, turn off the heat, and cover the pot for 1–2 minutes or until the spinach is just wilted.
10. Serve hot with rice.

Recipe Name: Pata at Hipon sa Gata na May Monggo at Langka
Short Description: Pork trotters and shrimp simmered in coconut milk with mung beans and jackfruit.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kg pork pata, sliced
- 1/4 kg shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 pork broth cube
- 2 cups coconut milk (480 ml)
- 1/2 cup hot pepper leaves or malunggay leaves
- 3/4 cup unripe jackfruit, sliced
- 1/4 cup mung beans
- 1 tbsp bagoong alamang
- 1/2 tbsp whole peppercorn
- 2 dried bay leaves
- 1/2 medium onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1–2 siling labuyo
- 1/8 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- 8 cups water (1.92 liters), for boiling the pork
Steps:
1. Pour 4 cups of water into a pressure cooker. Add the pork pata and boil for 15 minutes. Remove the pata and discard the water.
2. Add fresh water to the pressure cooker and bring it to a boil. Add the whole peppercorns, bay leaves, and pata.
3. Cover and pressure-cook for about 25 minutes, following your pressure cooker's instructions. Release the pressure safely before opening.
4. Remove the tender pata and set aside.
5. Heat the cooking oil in a separate pot. Pan-fry the shrimp for about 1 minute per side, then remove and set aside.
6. Add the onion to the pot and sauté for about 30 seconds. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
7. Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add the pork broth cube and stir until dissolved.
8. Add the mung beans. Cover and cook for 15–18 minutes, or until tender.
9. Add the unripe jackfruit. Cover and cook for another 10–12 minutes.
10. Add the siling labuyo, bagoong alamang, and ground black pepper. Stir well.
11. Add the cooked pata. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors combine.
12. Add the hot pepper leaves or malunggay leaves and stir.
13. Return the shrimp to the pot and cook for another 3 minutes, or until fully cooked.
14. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Bean sprouts sautéed with garlic, onions, and shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kilogram mung bean sprouts (togue)
- 1 block extra-firm tofu
- 1 carrot, julienned
- 1/4 kilogram shrimp, shelled and deveined
- 1 medium tomato, cubed
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 green bell pepper, sliced
- 1 tablespoon oyster sauce
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Oil, for frying and sautéing
Steps:
1. Fry the tofu until golden brown. Remove from the pan, slice into cubes, and set aside.
2. Sauté the garlic, onion, and tomato until the onion and tomato soften.
3. Add the shrimp and sauté for about 1 minute.
4. Add the fried tofu and cook for 30 seconds.
5. Add the mung bean sprouts and carrot. Sauté for 1 minute.
6. Add the red and green bell peppers. Cook for another minute.
7. Season with oyster sauce and ground black pepper.
8. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Cabbage sautéed with garlic, onions, and shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kilogram ground pork
- 1/4 kilogram shrimp, shelled and deveined
- 1/2 small cabbage, sliced
- 1 medium red bell pepper, sliced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1–2 tablespoons Knorr Liquid Seasoning
- 2 tablespoons oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil, onion, and garlic. Cook until fragrant.
2. Add the ground pork and sauté until cooked through.
3. Add the shrimp and bell pepper. Cook for about 1 minute.
4. Add the cabbage and sauté over high heat for 2 minutes.
5. Season with Knorr Liquid Seasoning and ground black pepper.
6. Serve with or without rice.

Short Description: Bok choy sautéed with garlic, onions, and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram pechay, chopped
- 1/4 kilogram pork, chopped and thinly sliced
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 tablespoon fish sauce (patis)
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 cup (240 ml) water
- 1 tablespoon oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat the pan and add the cooking oil.
2. Sauté the garlic, onion, and tomato.
3. Add the pork and cook for 5 minutes.
4. Add the fish sauce and ground black pepper.
5. Add the water and simmer for 10–15 minutes.
6. When the pork is tender, add the pechay. Cook for a few seconds, then turn off the heat.
7. Let the pechay sit in the pan for 5 minutes before serving.
8. Serve hot.

Short Description: A Filipino omelet with onions, tomatoes, and ground meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 8 minutes
Overall Time: 13 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 large eggs
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 1/2 medium red onion, diced
- 1/8 tsp ground black pepper
- 1/8 tsp salt
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add the salt and ground black pepper, then beat with a fork or whisk until well combined.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
3. Add the onion and tomato. Sauté for about 2 minutes, or until softened.
4. Pour the beaten eggs into the pan. Tilt the pan to spread the mixture evenly.
5. Cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, gently pushing the cooked edges inward so the uncooked egg can reach the pan.
6. Carefully flip the omelet using a wide spatula and cook the other side for about 3 minutes, or until fully set.
7. Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with pandesal or garlic rice, and banana ketchup if desired.

Recipe Name: Chicken Adobo Fried Rice and Tortang Corned Beef
Short Description: Chicken adobo fried rice served with a savory corned beef omelet.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
For the Chicken Adobo Fried Rice:
- 1/2 cup cooked chicken adobo, shredded and chopped
- 2 cups leftover cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1 1/2 tbsp cooking oil

For the Tortang Corned Beef:
- 3/4 cup sautéed corned beef
- 1 egg
- 1/8 tsp ground black pepper
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. In a bowl, combine the sautéed corned beef, egg, and ground black pepper. Mix well.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Divide the corned beef mixture into two portions. Scoop each portion into the pan and flatten gently.
3. Fry each portion for 1–2 minutes, then flip and cook the other side until done. Remove and set aside.
4. Combine the leftover rice and salt, gently separating any clumps.
5. Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Add the crushed garlic and cook until light brown.
6. Add the chopped chicken adobo and stir-fry for 1 minute.
7. Add the rice and stir-fry for 3–5 minutes, until heated through.
8. Transfer the fried rice to a serving plate and serve with the tortang corned beef on top.

Short Description: String beans and squash simmered in coconut milk with shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram kalabasa, cubed
- 1/4 kilogram sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/4 kilogram pork belly, boiled and cut into pieces
- 2 cups (480 ml) coconut milk
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 thumb-sized ginger, sliced into strips
- 4 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 Knorr Pork Cube
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil
- Patis, to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan. Add the pork and cook until brown and crispy.
2. Add the garlic, onion, and ginger. Sauté until the onion begins to soften.
3. Pour in the coconut milk. Cover and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to medium and continue boiling for 5 minutes.
4. Add the Knorr Pork Cube and kalabasa. Cook for 5 minutes.
5. Add the sitaw and cook for another 5–8 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked but not too soft.
6. Season with ground black pepper and patis to taste. Mix well.
7. Transfer to a serving plate and serve with warm rice.

Short Description: Young jackfruit simmered in coconut milk with chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram unripe langka, peeled and chopped
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 5 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 3–5 siling labuyo, chopped
- 1 Knorr Shrimp Cube
- 2 cups (480 ml) coconut milk
- 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
- 1/2 cup fried dried fish (daing), bones removed
Steps:
1. Heat a wok or cooking pot and pour in the coconut milk. Bring to a boil.
2. Add the garlic and onion. Cook for 3–5 minutes while continuously stirring.
3. Add the tomatoes and siling labuyo. Continue stirring.
4. Add the fried dried fish and cook for 5 minutes.
5. Pour in the water and allow the mixture to boil again.
6. Add the chopped langka and mix with the other ingredients. Simmer for 5–8 minutes.
7. Add the shrimp cube and stir to distribute it evenly. Simmer until the liquid dries up.
8. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

Short Description: Bamboo shoots simmered in coconut milk with chilies and shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Soaking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram labong (bamboo shoots), sliced into strips
- 1/4 kilogram pork belly, cut into small cubes
- 1/4 kilogram small fresh shrimp, peeled
- 2 siling haba
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon seasoning powder
- Salt, to taste
- 1 cup (240 ml) coconut cream
- 2 cups (480 ml) water, for extracting coconut milk
Steps:
1. Soak the labong in water for 1 hour. Drain and squeeze out the water. Set aside.
2. If using fresh coconut, add 1 cup lukewarm water to the grated coconut. Squeeze and strain the coconut milk. Set aside.
3. Make a second extraction by adding 2 cups water to the grated coconut. Squeeze and strain the coconut milk directly into the pan or pot.
4. Add the ginger, garlic, onion, pork, shrimp, and seasoning.
5. Bring to a boil while stirring gently.
6. After 3 minutes of boiling, add the labong. Cover and simmer for about 10 minutes.
7. Add the thick coconut cream and simmer until the labong is cooked and the sauce thickens.
8. Add the siling haba about 2 minutes before the cooking is finished.
9. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Banana blossoms simmered in coconut milk with chilies and shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium puso ng saging, sliced into strips
- 1/4 kilogram ground pork
- 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) coconut milk
- 1 cup (240 ml) water
- 1 medium onion, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons patis
- 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1 Knorr Shrimp Cube
- 1/4 kilogram shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2–3 siling labuyo, optional
- Salt, for preparing the banana blossom
Steps:
1. Remove the outer peel of the banana blossom and use the light-colored inner part.
2. Slice the banana blossom into strips. Place in a bowl, add salt, and let it stand for 15 minutes.
3. Squeeze the banana blossom several times to remove the bitter sap. Soak in water, drain, and squeeze again to remove excess water.
4. Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Sauté the garlic and onion until soft.
5. Add the patis and simmer for a few seconds.
6. Add the ground pork and black pepper. Stir and cook until the pork turns brown.
7. Add the banana blossom. Stir to combine, cover, and simmer for 3 minutes.
8. Add the vinegar and simmer for 1 minute.
9. Add the water and shrimp cube. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
10. Add the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Continue cooking until the sauce becomes thick and oily.
11. Add the shrimp and cook for about 2–3 minutes, until cooked through.
12. Turn off the heat and serve hot with rice.

Short Description: Bitter melon simmered in coconut milk with shrimp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 medium ampalaya, sliced
- 1/4 kilogram shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/4 kilogram pork belly, sliced
- 2 tablespoons ginger, julienned
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 tablespoon bagoong alamang
- 1 can (400 ml) coconut milk
- 2–3 siling pansigang
- 1 cup malunggay leaves
- Fish sauce, salt, and pepper, to taste
- Oil, as needed
Steps:
1. Cut the ampalaya in half lengthwise. Remove the seeds and white center, then slice. For less bitterness, massage with salt and let sit for 20 minutes. Rinse well and gently squeeze out the water.
2. Season the shrimp with salt and pepper. Heat a little oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the shrimp for about 1 minute per side, just until pink. Transfer to a plate.
3. Add the pork and a little water to the same pan. Cook over medium heat until the water evaporates and the pork releases some of its fat. Season lightly with salt and continue cooking until browned and slightly crisp.
4. Add the ginger and cook until fragrant. Add the garlic and onion, then cook until softened.
5. Stir in the bagoong alamang and cook for about 1 minute.
6. Pour in the coconut milk and add the siling pansigang. Bring to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes, until slightly thickened.
7. Add the ampalaya and cook for about 5 minutes, until tender but not mushy.
8. Add the shrimp and malunggay leaves. Cook for 1–2 minutes, until the leaves wilt and the shrimp is heated through.
9. Add more coconut milk or a little water if needed. Season with fish sauce, salt, and black pepper to taste.
10. Turn off the heat and serve with steamed rice.

Short Description: Mixed vegetables simmered in coconut milk with shrimp and pork.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram kalabasa, cubed
- 1/4 kilogram sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/4 kilogram pork belly, sliced into small pieces
- 1 pack (45 g) Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix
- 1/4 kilogram shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 cups (480 ml) water
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
Steps:
1. Boil the water in a saucepan. Add the pork. Cover and cook over low to medium heat for 20 minutes.
2. Remove the pork from the saucepan and set aside. Reserve the water.
3. Heat oil in a pan. Sauté the onion and garlic until the onion softens.
4. Add the boiled pork and sauté for 1 minute.
5. Combine the Knorr Ginataang Gulay Mix with the water used to boil the pork. Stir until dissolved, then pour the mixture into the pan. Let it boil.
6. Add the kalabasa. Cover and cook for 3 minutes.
7. Add the shrimp and sitaw. Cover and continue cooking for 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are cooked.
8. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

Short Description: Grilled eggplant dipped in egg and pan-fried into a savory omelet.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces Chinese eggplant (talong)
- 2 eggs
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 3 tablespoons cooking oil, as needed
Steps:
1. Grill the eggplants directly over a gas flame or on a grill. Turn them occasionally until the skin is charred and the flesh becomes soft.
2. Place the grilled eggplants on a plate and let them cool until easy to handle.
3. Peel off the charred skin while keeping the stems attached.
4. Arrange each eggplant on a flat surface. Gently flatten the flesh using a fork, spreading it into a wide oval shape without breaking it apart.
5. Crack the eggs into a wide bowl. Add the salt and beat until well combined.
6. Dip one flattened eggplant into the beaten egg, making sure both sides are coated.
7. Heat about 1 tablespoon of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Place the coated eggplant in the pan, then spoon a little more beaten egg over any uncovered areas.
8. Fry for 3–4 minutes, or until the bottom is golden brown and the egg has set. Carefully turn it over and cook the other side for another 2–3 minutes.
9. Transfer the cooked tortang talong to a serving plate. Repeat with the remaining eggplant, adding more oil as needed.
10. Serve with warm rice and banana ketchup.

Short Description: A pan-fried omelet filled with ground pork, onion, and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kilogram ground pork or beef
- 3 eggs
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1 small green bell pepper, minced
- 1 small red bell pepper, minced
- 1/4 cup green peas
- 3/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- Banana ketchup, for serving
Steps:
1. Heat a frying pan or wok and pour in 1 tablespoon of cooking oil.
2. When the oil is hot, sauté the onion, garlic, and tomato.
3. Add the ground meat and cook for 8–10 minutes.
4. Add the bell peppers and green peas. Cook for 3 minutes.
5. Add the salt and pepper, then stir to distribute. Transfer to a bowl and let it cool.
6. When the cooked ground meat reaches room temperature, beat the eggs and pour them into the same bowl. Stir to combine all the ingredients.
7. Heat a clean non-stick pan and add the remaining cooking oil.
8. Scoop the egg and pork mixture into the pan.
9. Cook each side for about 3 minutes or until the eggs are fully cooked. Repeat until the mixture is consumed.
10. Turn off the heat and transfer to a serving plate.
11. Serve with banana ketchup.

Short Description: Pork chops marinated in soy sauce and calamansi and pan-fried until juicy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kg pork chops (about 2 pieces)
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 3 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp calamansi juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Cooking oil
Steps:
1. Rinse the pork chops and pat dry. Season with ground black pepper.
2. In a bowl, combine the soy sauce, calamansi juice, and minced garlic.
3. Add the pork chops and coat them with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
4. Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
5. Drain the pork chops, discarding the marinade.
6. Pan-fry the pork chops for 2–3 minutes on one side. Turn and cook for another 1–2 minutes, or until cooked through. Adjust the time depending on the thickness.
7. Remove from the pan and let rest for 2–3 minutes before serving.

Short Description: Crispy fried eggplant and meat patties, golden and savory.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 Chinese eggplant
- 1/4 kg ground pork
- 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 small onion, minced
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- 1 egg
- 3/4 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- Cooking oil for frying
- 2 cups water (480 ml), for boiling the eggplant

For the Dipping Sauce:
- 1/4 cup mayonnaise
- 2 tbsp banana ketchup
Steps:
1. Bring the water to a boil in a pot. Add the eggplant and boil for about 6 minutes, or until tender.
2. Remove the eggplant from the pot and let it cool. Peel off the skin and chop the flesh into small pieces.
3. Place the chopped eggplant in a bowl. Add the ground pork, onion, salt, pepper, garlic powder, egg, and flour. Mix until well combined.
4. Heat the cooking oil in a pot or deep pan over low to medium heat.
5. Scoop portions of the mixture and shape them into balls. Roll each ball in breadcrumbs.
6. Deep-fry the balls for about 8 minutes, turning as needed, until cooked through and golden brown. Fry in batches if necessary.
7. Combine the mayonnaise and banana ketchup in a small bowl to make the dipping sauce.
8. Drain the fried bola-bola on a rack and serve hot with the dipping sauce.

Short Description: Crispy shrimp and vegetable fritters, golden and crunchy, served with vinegar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kilogram small shrimp, cleaned
- 1 1/2 cups mung bean sprouts (togue)
- 1 cup cornstarch
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 egg
- 1/4 teaspoon baking powder
- 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) water
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
- Oil, for deep-frying
- Sinamak, for serving
Steps:
1. Combine the cornstarch, flour, baking powder, egg, water, salt, and ground black pepper. Stir until well combined.
2. Add the shrimp and mung bean sprouts. Lightly stir to distribute.
3. Heat oil in a frying pan or small cooking pot.
4. When the oil is hot, scoop about 2–3 tablespoons of the mixture and carefully drop it into the hot oil.
5. Cook each side for 2–3 minutes or until golden brown. Repeat until the mixture is consumed.
6. Remove the ukoy from the pan and place on a plate lined with paper towels to absorb excess oil.
7. Remove the paper towels and serve with sinamak.
8. Share and enjoy.

Short Description: Grilled eggplant with tomatoes and onions in a tangy vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces Chinese eggplant (talong)
- 2 medium tomatoes
- 1 medium onion
- 3/4 cup vinegar
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons bagoong alamang
Steps:
1. Grill the eggplant or cook it directly on the stovetop until the skin is charred and the eggplant is cooked.
2. Peel the skin, cut off the stems, and lightly mash the eggplant with a fork.
3. Cube the tomatoes and onion.
4. Combine the tomatoes, onion, mashed eggplant, salt, ground black pepper, and vinegar. Toss to mix.
5. Top with bagoong alamang.
6. Serve and enjoy.

Short Description: Ripe or green mango with tomatoes and onions in a tangy shrimp-paste dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 large green mango, peeled and sliced into cubes
- 2 medium tomatoes, cubed
- 1 medium red or white onion, cubed
- 2–3 calamansi, juiced
- 2–3 tablespoons bagoong alamang
Steps:
1. Combine the green mango, onion, and tomato in a bowl.
2. Pour in the calamansi juice and add the bagoong alamang.
3. Toss until all the ingredients are well blended.
4. Add more bagoong if desired.
5. Serve with fried or grilled food.
6. Share and enjoy.

Short Description: Fern tips with tomatoes and onions in a tangy, light dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 bundle young pako (fiddlehead fern)
- 2 medium tomatoes, thinly sliced
- 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
- 2 salted eggs, cubed
- 2 tablespoons white vinegar
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Soak the young pako fronds in cold water for a few minutes and rinse well. You may also blanch them in boiling water beforehand.
2. In a small bowl, dissolve the sugar in the vinegar and add freshly ground black pepper. Set aside.
3. In a large bowl, mix the pako, tomatoes, and onions.
4. Pour in the vinegar mixture and toss until well mixed.
5. Add the salted eggs and toss one last time.

Short Description: Sea grapes with tomatoes and onions in a tangy vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 6 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Resting Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 16 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kilogram lato (sea grapes), rinsed
- 1 large tomato, cored and diced
- 1 medium red onion, minced
- 1/4 cup vinegar
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon sugar
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
Steps:
1. In a bowl, combine the vinegar, salt, pepper, sugar, tomato, and onion. Stir to mix.
2. Add the lato or sea grapes. Toss well.
3. Let it sit for at least 10 minutes.
4. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.
5. Share and enjoy.

Short Description: Jicama and vegetables in a sweet-sour vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small singkamas, peeled and julienned
- 1 medium tomato, cubed
- 1/2 cup cilantro, chopped
- 1/2 cup whole corn
- 1/4 cup red onion, chopped
- 1/4 cup carrot, julienned
- 1 tablespoon ginger, julienned
- 1/4 cup red or green bell pepper

FOR THE SAUCE
- 4 tablespoons white vinegar
- 2 teaspoons white sugar
- 1/2 teaspoon salt or fish sauce
- 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2 tablespoons tinapa flakes, optional
Steps:
1. Chop and combine all the vegetables in a bowl.
2. In a cup, combine the vinegar, sugar, salt or fish sauce, and ground black pepper. Mix well.
3. Pour the sauce over the vegetables.
4. Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.
5. Add tinapa flakes if desired.
6. Serve cold.

Short Description: Thin cucumber slices in a sweet-sour vinegar dressing, chilled.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 2 hours
Overall Time: At least 2 hours 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 large cucumber, thinly sliced
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/8 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1 tablespoon sugar
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 3 tablespoons white vinegar or apple cider vinegar
Steps:
1. Wash the cucumber thoroughly and pat it dry. Using a mandoline, vegetable peeler, or sharp knife, slice it into paper-thin rounds. Leave the skin on or peel if preferred.
2. In a mixing bowl, combine the salt, ground black pepper, sugar, minced ginger, and vinegar. Whisk until the sugar dissolves completely.
3. Add the sliced cucumber and red onion to the dressing. Toss gently to coat evenly.
4. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
5. Stir gently before transferring to a serving dish. Drain any excess liquid if needed.
6. Serve cold.

Short Description: Salted eggs and tomatoes in a light, savory dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 minute
Overall Time: 6 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 salted duck egg
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 1/2 tsp patis
Steps:
1. Cut the salted egg in half.
2. Scoop out the egg white and yolk, then place them in a bowl.
3. Add the diced tomato and patis.
4. Mix gently until combined.
5. Serve as a side dish with grilled or fried food.

Short Description: A classic Filipino salad of fresh vegetables and sweet-sour dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 Chinese eggplant
- 1/2 medium tomato
- 1/2 medium onion
- 1/4 cup vinegar (60 ml)
- 1/8 tsp ground black pepper
- 1/4 tsp sugar
- 1/8 tsp salt
- 2 tbsp bagoong alamang (optional)
Steps:
1. Preheat the grill. Grill the eggplant until the inside is soft, about 10–12 minutes per side or longer if needed. Grill the tomato and onion for about 3 minutes per side.
2. Let the vegetables cool. Peel the eggplant and slice it. Slice the tomato and onion, then arrange them on a serving plate.
3. In a bowl, combine the vinegar, sugar, salt, and ground black pepper. Stir until the sugar and salt dissolve.
4. Pour the vinegar dressing over the vegetables.
5. Serve with bagoong alamang on the side, if desired.

Short Description: Thinly sliced radish with tomatoes and onions in a tangy vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Salting Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kilogram labanos, thinly sliced
- 2 medium tomatoes, thinly sliced
- 1 small onion, thinly sliced
- 1/3 cup vinegar
- 2 tablespoons salt, for salting the labanos
- Salt and pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Peel and slice the labanos very thinly.
2. Place the labanos in a bowl and sprinkle with 2 tablespoons salt. Mix well and set aside for about 25 minutes.
3. Squeeze the salted labanos. Wash with water and drain.
4. Squeeze again, making sure to remove the excess salt and water.
5. In a bowl, combine the tomatoes, onion, and vinegar. Add the labanos.
6. Add more salt and pepper according to taste.
7. Serve with fried fish or pork.

Short Description: Sweet potato leaves with tomatoes and onions in a tangy dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 large bunch talbos ng kamote, stems removed and cleaned
- 3 medium tomatoes, sliced
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, shredded
- 1 medium red onion, sliced
- 6 tablespoons sugar cane vinegar
- 1/2 teaspoon white sugar
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
- 2 cups (480 ml) water
Steps:
1. Place the water in a cooking pot and bring to a boil.
2. Blanch the talbos ng kamote by placing the leaves in the boiling water for about 20–30 seconds.
3. Remove the leaves and immediately submerge them in a bowl of cold water for 30 seconds. Let them dry.
4. In a large bowl, combine the talbos ng kamote, tomatoes, ginger, onion, sugar, salt, pepper, and vinegar.
5. Gently toss until all the ingredients are evenly distributed.
6. Serve as an appetizer or side dish.

Short Description: Salted egg with tomatoes and onions in a tangy vinegar dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 salted duck eggs, chopped
- 1/2 cup chopped tomatoes
- 1/2 cup chopped cucumber
- 1/4 small red onion, diced or thinly sliced
- 1 teaspoon red wine vinegar or cane vinegar
- 1/2 teaspoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon olive oil, optional
- Salt and pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, vinegar, soy sauce, and olive oil in a bowl. Toss together.
2. Cut the salted eggs in half and scoop them out of the shells. Chop into bite-sized pieces.
3. Gently mix the salted eggs with the vegetables.
4. Taste before adding salt, then add pepper as needed.
5. Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate until ready to eat.

Short Description: A savory Ilocano vegetable stew flavored with fermented fish sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 whole bangus, sliced and grilled
- 1 bunch malunggay leaves, cleaned
- 1 cup squash flowers (bulaklak ng kalabasa)
- 6–8 pieces okra
- 1/2 bunch sitaw, cut into 3-inch pieces
- 1 medium ampalaya, cored and sliced
- 1–2 tablespoons bagoong isda
- 1 thumb-sized piece ginger, sliced
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1/2 medium onion, chopped
- 2 cups (480 ml) water
Steps:
1. Bring the water to a boil in a large cooking pot.
2. Add the ginger, onion, and tomato. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
3. Pour in the bagoong isda and stir.
4. Add the okra and sitaw. Stir, then add the ampalaya. Cook over medium heat for 7–10 minutes.
5. Add the squash flowers and malunggay leaves. Cook for 3–5 minutes.
6. Add the grilled bangus and let it cook with the vegetables for 3–5 minutes to add flavor.
7. Serve hot.

Short Description: A light Visayan vegetable soup with leafy greens and squash.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups water or rice-washing water
- 1 cup squash, cubed
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 4 pieces okra
- 1 cup string beans, cut into short lengths
- 1 cup malunggay or camote leaves
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1 small onion, sliced
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Bring the water, onion, and tomato to a boil.
2. Add squash and simmer for 5 minutes.
3. Add eggplant, okra, and string beans; cook until just tender.
4. Stir in leafy greens and cook for 1–2 minutes.
5. Season lightly with salt and serve hot.

Short Description: A simple Filipino vegetable soup with leafy greens and squash.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 cups water
- 1 cup squash, cubed
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 4 pieces okra
- 1 cup string beans, cut into short lengths
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1 small onion, sliced
- 1 cup malunggay or spinach leaves
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Bring water, tomato, and onion to a boil.
2. Add squash and simmer until partly tender.
3. Add eggplant, okra, and string beans; simmer until tender.
4. Add leafy greens and cook briefly.
5. Season with salt and serve with rice.

Short Description: String beans in coconut milk with chilies, savory and mildly spicy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g ground pork
- 1 cup sitaw, sliced
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1–2 pieces red chili, sliced
- 1 tsp bagoong alamang
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
2. Add ground pork and cook until no longer pink.
3. Stir in bagoong and sliced chili.
4. Add sitaw and water; cover and cook until tender-crisp.
5. Pour in coconut milk and simmer gently until slightly thick.

Short Description: A Tagalog vegetable stew with shrimp paste and pork.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g pork belly, sliced
- 1 cup squash, cubed
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 4 pieces okra
- 1 cup sitaw, cut short
- 1 small ampalaya, sliced
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp bagoong alamang
- 1/3 cup water
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato in a pot.
2. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in bagoong and water; simmer for 5 minutes.
4. Add squash first, then eggplant, okra, sitaw, and ampalaya.
5. Cover and simmer until vegetables are tender but not mushy.

Short Description: Stuffed eggplant with ground meat, fried until golden.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants
- 120 g ground pork
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Grill or broil eggplants until soft; peel while keeping stems attached and flatten gently.
2. Sauté garlic, onion, tomato, and pork until cooked; season with soy sauce and pepper.
3. Spread the eggplants flat and place the pork mixture over them.
4. Dip each stuffed eggplant in beaten egg.
5. Pan-fry in oil until the egg coating is set and golden on both sides.

Short Description: Okra sautéed with garlic, onions, and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups okra, sliced diagonally
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp water
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
2. Add tomato and cook until softened.
3. Add okra and water; toss to coat.
4. Cover and cook for 4–6 minutes, stirring once, until tender-crisp.
5. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

Short Description: Sweet potato tops sautéed with garlic and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 7 minutes
Overall Time: 12 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 bunch talbos ng kamote, washed and tough stems removed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp water
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
2. Add tomato and cook until juicy.
3. Add sweet potato leaves and water.
4. Toss and cook just until wilted, about 2–3 minutes.
5. Season with salt and serve immediately.

Short Description: Chayote tops sautéed with garlic and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 7 minutes
Overall Time: 12 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 bunch sayote tops, washed and trimmed
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp water
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
2. Add tomato and cook until softened.
3. Add sayote tops and water; toss well.
4. Cover briefly and cook until tender but still green.
5. Season with salt and serve.

Short Description: Bok choy and tofu sautéed with garlic and soy sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Allergens: Soy, wheat (if regular soy sauce is used)
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces firm tokwa, cubed
- 2 cups pechay, halved
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/2 cup water or vegetable stock
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Pan-fry tofu cubes until lightly golden; set aside.
2. Sauté garlic in the same pan.
3. Add water and soy sauce and bring to a simmer.
4. Return tofu and add pechay; cook until leaves wilt and stems soften.
5. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer until the sauce lightly thickens.

Short Description: Tofu sizzling on a hot plate with onions and a savory sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 pieces firm tokwa, cubed and patted dry
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 small green chili, sliced
- 2 tbsp mayonnaise
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp calamansi juice
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Pan-fry tofu cubes until golden on all sides.
2. Mix mayonnaise, soy sauce, calamansi juice, and pepper in a bowl.
3. Sauté onion and chili briefly in a hot pan.
4. Add tofu and sauce; toss quickly until coated and hot.
5. Serve immediately on a hot plate if available.

Short Description: Chopped tofu with onions, chilies, and creamy mayonnaise.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 pieces firm tokwa, cubed
- 1/2 small onion, finely chopped
- 1 green chili, sliced
- 2 tbsp mayonnaise
- 1 tsp calamansi juice
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Fry tofu cubes until crisp and golden; drain.
2. Combine mayonnaise, calamansi juice, soy sauce, and pepper.
3. Sauté onion and chili for 1 minute.
4. Toss tofu with the dressing and onion mixture.
5. Serve hot with extra calamansi if desired.

Short Description: Crispy fried tofu, golden outside and soft inside.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 pieces firm tokwa, cut into cubes
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp vinegar
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 small chili, optional
Steps:
1. Pat tofu dry and cut into bite-sized cubes.
2. Heat oil and fry tofu until golden and crisp on several sides.
3. Mix vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, onion, and chili for the dip.
4. Drain tofu briefly on paper towels.
5. Serve hot with the dipping sauce.

Short Description: Tofu and vegetables sautéed with garlic and soy sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Allergens: Soy, wheat (if soy sauce is used)
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces firm tokwa, cubed
- 1 cup cabbage, sliced
- 1 small carrot, sliced
- 1 cup green beans, cut short
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/3 cup water
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Pan-fry tofu until golden and set aside.
2. Sauté garlic in oil, then add carrot and green beans.
3. Add water and soy sauce; simmer for 2 minutes.
4. Add cabbage and tofu and toss until vegetables are just tender.
5. Taste and serve hot.

Short Description: Radish in a tangy vinegar dressing with ginger and chili.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium white radish, thinly sliced
- 3 tbsp cane vinegar
- 1/4 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 tsp grated ginger
- 1 small chili, sliced
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tsp sugar, optional
Steps:
1. Toss sliced radish with salt and let stand for 10 minutes.
2. Squeeze out excess liquid and place radish in a bowl.
3. Add vinegar, onion, ginger, chili, and optional sugar.
4. Mix and chill for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
5. Serve as a tart side dish.

Short Description: A Visayan vegetable stew with squash and leafy greens.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Allergens: Fish (if fish sauce or fish is added)
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 cups water
- 1 cup squash, cubed
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 4 pieces okra
- 1 cup sitaw, cut short
- 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 cup malunggay or alugbati leaves
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Bring water to a boil with lemongrass and ginger.
2. Add squash and simmer for 5 minutes.
3. Add sitaw, eggplant, and okra; cook until tender.
4. Stir in leafy greens and cook for 1–2 minutes.
5. Remove lemongrass, season with salt, and serve.

Short Description: A Visayan vegetable soup with squash, okra, and leafy greens.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 8–10 pieces small shrimp, peeled
- 2 1/2 cups water
- 1 cup squash, cubed
- 4 pieces okra
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 1 cup alugbati or saluyot leaves
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1 small onion, sliced
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Bring water, tomato, and onion to a boil.
2. Add squash and cook for 5 minutes.
3. Add okra, eggplant, and shrimp; simmer until shrimp turn pink.
4. Add leafy greens and cook briefly until wilted.
5. Season lightly with salt and serve hot.

Short Description: A Visayan chicken soup with coconut water and ginger.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken, bone-in
- 2 cups young coconut water
- 1/2 cup young coconut meat, sliced
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 small onion, sliced
- 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised
- 1 cup sayote, cubed
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté ginger and onion.
2. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
3. Pour in coconut water and add lemongrass; simmer for 25–30 minutes until chicken is tender.
4. Add sayote and coconut meat; simmer until the sayote softens.
5. Season with fish sauce and serve hot.

Short Description: A Visayan stew of pork, jackfruit, and kadyos beans.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 5 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g pork belly, cut into chunks
- 1 cup cooked kadyos (pigeon peas)
- 1 cup young jackfruit, sliced
- 2–3 batuan fruits or 1 tbsp tamarind paste
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 cups water
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Simmer pork in water with onion and garlic until nearly tender, about 35–45 minutes.
2. Add kadyos and young jackfruit.
3. Add batuan or tamarind and simmer until the pork and jackfruit are tender.
4. Add water if needed to keep a stew-like broth.
5. Season with salt and serve with rice.

Short Description: Mixed vegetables sautéed with garlic and onions.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup cabbage, sliced
- 1 small carrot, sliced
- 1 cup sitaw, cut short
- 1 small sayote, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1/3 cup water
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
2. Add tomato and cook until soft.
3. Add carrot, sitaw, and sayote with water; cover and cook for 4–5 minutes.
4. Add cabbage and cook until just tender.
5. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

Short Description: Crispy fried vegetable rolls filled with cabbage, carrots, green beans, and optional tofu; served with spiced vinegar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup cabbage, finely shredded
- 1/2 cup carrot, cut into thin strips
- 1/4 cup green beans, thinly sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup firm tofu, diced and lightly fried (optional)
- 1 tsp soy sauce or fish sauce, to taste
- 1 tbsp cooking oil, for the filling
- 8 small lumpia wrappers
- Oil for deep-frying
- Spiced vinegar, for serving
Steps:
1. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add carrot and green beans first and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in cabbage and optional fried tofu, then season with soy sauce or fish sauce.
3. Cook only until the vegetables are just tender. Transfer to a strainer or plate and cool completely; drain any liquid so the wrappers do not split.
4. Put a spoonful of filling near the lower edge of each wrapper. Fold in the sides, roll tightly, and seal the final edge with a little water.
5. Heat frying oil over medium heat. Fry the rolls in batches, turning until evenly golden and crisp; avoid crowding the pan.
6. Drain on a rack or paper towel and serve hot with spiced vinegar.

Short Description: Fresh, unfried spring rolls filled with sautéed heart of palm, pork, and shrimp, wrapped with lettuce and served with peanut-garlic sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 25 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Allergens: Wheat, shellfish, egg (if wrapper contains egg)
Ingredients:
Filling:
- 1 cup ubod (heart of palm), cut into thin strips
- 75 g pork belly, finely diced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and chopped
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 4 lettuce leaves

Wrappers:
- 1/3 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 egg
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tsp cooking oil, plus a little for the pan

Peanut sauce:
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp peanut butter
- 1 tbsp ground peanuts
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water
Steps:
1. Whisk flour, egg, water, and oil until smooth. Lightly oil a nonstick pan, pour in a thin layer of batter, and cook each side briefly to make four thin crepe wrappers. Cool them on a plate.
2. Heat a little oil in a pan. Sauté onion and garlic, add pork, and cook until browned. Add shrimp and stir until pink.
3. Add ubod and water. Cover and cook for 5-8 minutes, until the heart of palm softens but still has a slight bite. Season with fish sauce and drain off excess liquid.
4. For the sauce, simmer water, soy sauce, brown sugar, and garlic. Stir in peanut butter and ground peanuts. Add the cornstarch slurry gradually and simmer until lightly thickened.
5. Put one lettuce leaf and a portion of the cooled filling on each wrapper. Fold the sides and roll gently; do not deep-fry.
6. Place the fresh rolls on a plate, spoon over the peanut-garlic sauce, and garnish with extra peanuts if available.

Short Description: Fried rolls centered on mung bean sprouts (togue), with tofu and dried shrimp for a savory, lightly briny filling.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups mung bean sprouts (togue), rinsed and drained
- 1/2 cup firm tofu, diced and lightly fried
- 1 tbsp dried shrimp (hibe), rinsed (optional)
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 small onion, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 6-8 small lumpia wrappers
- 1 tbsp cooking oil for filling
- Oil for deep-frying
- Spiced vinegar with onion, for serving
Steps:
1. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add dried shrimp if using, then add fried tofu and carrot. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
3. Add mung bean sprouts, fish sauce, and pepper. Toss for just 2-3 minutes; the sprouts should soften slightly but remain crisp.
4. Transfer the filling to a plate and drain any liquid. Cool fully before wrapping.
5. Put a small portion of filling on each wrapper, fold in the sides, roll tightly, and seal with water.
6. Deep-fry over medium heat until golden and crisp. Drain and serve with spicy vinegar and onion.

Short Description: Small, crispy fried rolls filled with raw seasoned ground pork, carrot, onion, garlic, and egg binder.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g ground pork
- 1/4 small carrot, finely grated
- 1/4 small onion, minced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
- 8 small lumpia wrappers
- Oil for deep-frying
- Sweet chili sauce, banana ketchup, or sweet-and-sour sauce, for serving
Steps:
1. In a bowl, mix the raw ground pork, carrot, onion, garlic, beaten egg, soy sauce, and black pepper until evenly combined. Do not pre-cook the filling; it cooks inside the wrapper.
2. Lay a wrapper on a clean surface. Place a narrow strip of filling near the lower edge, fold in both sides, then roll tightly. Seal the edge with a little water.
3. Heat oil over medium to medium-low heat. Fry a small test roll first to check that the wrapper browns gradually while the pork cooks through.
4. Fry the remaining rolls in batches, turning as needed, until golden and the center is fully cooked. Keep the oil from getting too hot, or the wrapper may darken before the filling cooks.
5. Drain on a rack or paper towel. Serve hot with sweet chili, banana ketchup, or sweet-and-sour sauce.

Short Description: Fresh rolls with vegetables and a peanut sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Allergens: Peanuts, soy, shellfish (if shrimp paste is used)
Ingredients:
- 1 cup cabbage, sliced
- 1/2 cup carrots, sliced
- 1/2 cup green beans, sliced
- 1/2 cup ubod or bean sprouts
- 100 g pork, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp peanut butter
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1/3 cup water
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic and pork in oil until cooked.
2. Add carrots, green beans, ubod, and cabbage; cook until just tender.
3. Simmer water, peanut butter, soy sauce, and brown sugar into a pourable sauce.
4. Arrange the vegetables on a plate and spoon sauce over them.
5. Serve warm without wrappers.

Short Description: Steamed or fried rolls of ground pork and vegetables, a popular street food.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Allergens: Soy, wheat (if wrapper or soy sauce contains wheat)
Ingredients:
- 150 g ground pork
- 1/2 cup singkamas, finely chopped
- 1 small carrot, grated
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 sheets bean-curd skin or spring-roll wrapper
