- 1/2 tsp ground pepper
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Mix pork, singkamas, carrot, garlic, soy sauce, and pepper.
2. Divide mixture between bean-curd skin or wrappers and roll tightly.
3. Steam the rolls for 15 minutes, then cool slightly.
4. Slice into pieces and shallow-fry until golden.
5. Serve with sweet chili or vinegar dip.

Short Description: A simple boiled chicken soup with potatoes, cabbage, and corn.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken, bone-in
- 1 small potato, quartered
- 1 cup cabbage, chopped
- 1 small onion, quartered
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 4 cups water
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- 1 tsp fish sauce, optional
Steps:
1. Put chicken, onion, ginger, peppercorns, and water in a pot.
2. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then simmer until chicken is nearly tender.
3. Add potato and cook until soft.
4. Add cabbage and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce if desired and serve hot.

Short Description: Boiled saba bananas, sweet and soft, a simple snack.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4 pieces saba bananas, unpeeled
- Water to cover
Steps:
1. Rinse the bananas and place in a pot.
2. Add enough water to cover.
3. Bring to a boil and simmer for 15–20 minutes until tender.
4. Drain and cool slightly before peeling.
5. Serve warm.

Short Description: A clear wonton-style soup of pork dumplings in chicken broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Allergens: Wheat, shellfish, soy, egg (depending on wrappers)
Ingredients:
- 8 wonton wrappers
- 100 g ground pork
- 6 pieces small shrimp, chopped
- 1 tbsp chopped onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup cooked shredded chicken
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp chopped spring onion
Steps:
1. Mix pork, shrimp, onion, and a little pepper; place small portions on wonton wrappers and seal.
2. Sauté garlic in oil, add broth, and bring to a simmer.
3. Add the dumplings and simmer until cooked through, about 5–7 minutes.
4. Stir in shredded chicken and fish sauce; heat through.
5. Serve topped with spring onion.

Short Description: A noodle soup with pork, liver, and crunchy toppings from Iloilo.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 50 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 150 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 75 g pork liver, thinly sliced
- 150 g fresh miki noodles
- 3 cups pork or chicken broth
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp crushed chicharon
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic in oil until fragrant; add pork and cook through.
2. Add broth and soy sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
3. Add liver and simmer just until cooked.
4. Blanch miki noodles separately, drain, and divide between two bowls.
5. Ladle hot broth and meat over noodles; top with chicharon and spring onion.

Short Description: A Tagalog-style noodle soup with pork and liver in a savory broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 75 g pork liver, thinly sliced
- 1 bundle misua or 50 g bihon
- 3 cups pork broth
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in oil.
2. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
3. Pour in broth and simmer until pork is tender.
4. Add liver and cook through, then stir in misua or bihon until soft.
5. Season with fish sauce and serve hot.

Short Description: A comforting noodle soup with chicken and egg noodles.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g chicken breast or thigh
- 150 g fresh egg noodles
- 3 cups chicken broth
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 small carrot, julienned
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Simmer chicken in broth until cooked; remove and shred.
2. Sauté garlic in oil, add broth and soy sauce, and bring to a simmer.
3. Cook noodles according to package directions and divide between bowls.
4. Add shredded chicken and carrot to the broth and simmer briefly.
5. Pour broth over noodles and garnish with spring onion.

Short Description: A comforting rice porridge with beef tripe, ginger, and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice
- 150 g cleaned beef tripe, pre-cooked and sliced
- 5 cups beef broth or water
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp toasted garlic
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
Steps:
1. Rinse rice and set aside.
2. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in oil; add tripe and cook for 2 minutes.
3. Add rice and broth; simmer, stirring often, until rice breaks down into porridge.
4. Add water as needed and season with fish sauce.
5. Serve topped with toasted garlic and spring onion.

Short Description: A simple rice porridge with garlic, ginger, and toppings.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice
- 5 cups water or light broth
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Rinse rice until the water is mostly clear.
2. Sauté garlic and ginger in oil in a pot.
3. Add rice and water; bring to a boil.
4. Lower heat and simmer, stirring often, until the rice is soft and porridge is creamy.
5. Season with salt and serve hot.

Short Description: Chicken rice porridge with ginger and garlic, a comfort-food classic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken, bone-in
- 1/2 cup rice
- 5 cups chicken broth or water
- 1 thumb ginger, julienned
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
- 1 tbsp toasted garlic
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in oil until fragrant.
2. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in rice, then pour in broth and bring to a boil.
4. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is soft and chicken is cooked through.
5. Season with fish sauce and top with spring onion and toasted garlic.

Short Description: A chocolate rice porridge, sweet and creamy, served with milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice
- 3 cups water
- 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder or tablea, chopped
- 2 tbsp sugar, or to taste
- 1/4 cup evaporated milk, optional
Steps:
1. Rinse glutinous rice and combine with water in a pot.
2. Bring to a boil, then simmer while stirring until the rice is soft.
3. Whisk cocoa or tablea with a little hot liquid, then stir into the pot.
4. Add sugar and simmer until thick and glossy.
5. Serve warm with optional evaporated milk.

Short Description: A creamy macaroni soup with milk and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup elbow macaroni
- 100 g cooked chicken, shredded
- 1/2 small carrot, diced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 3 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Cook macaroni in water until just tender; drain.
2. Sauté garlic and onion in oil, then add carrot and chicken.
3. Pour in broth and simmer until carrot softens.
4. Add macaroni and evaporated milk; heat gently without boiling hard.
5. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

Short Description: A light noodle soup with misua and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Allergens: Wheat, soy (if soy sauce is used)
Ingredients:
- 1 bundle misua noodles
- 100 g ground pork
- 3 cups chicken broth or water
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato in oil.
2. Add ground pork and cook until no longer pink.
3. Pour in broth and simmer for 8 minutes.
4. Add misua and cook for 2–3 minutes until soft.
5. Season with fish sauce and serve immediately.

Short Description: A light noodle soup with misua and sponge gourd.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Allergens: Wheat, soy (if soy sauce is used)
Ingredients:
- 1 bundle misua noodles
- 1 small patola, peeled and sliced
- 100 g ground pork
- 3 cups broth or water
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
2. Add ground pork and cook through.
3. Add broth and patola; simmer until patola is tender.
4. Stir in misua and cook for 2–3 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce and serve hot.

Short Description: A light noodle soup with misua and meatballs.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 bundle misua noodles
- 150 g ground pork
- 1 egg, optional
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 3 cups chicken broth
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
Steps:
1. Mix ground pork with half the garlic, onion, and pepper; shape into small meatballs.
2. Sauté remaining garlic in oil and add broth.
3. Bring to a simmer and add meatballs; cook for 8–10 minutes.
4. Add misua and cook for 2–3 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce and garnish with spring onion.

Short Description: A comforting glass noodle soup with chicken and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 100 g sotanghon noodles
- 100 g cooked shredded chicken
- 3 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
Steps:
1. Soak sotanghon in warm water until pliable; drain.
2. Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
3. Add broth, soy sauce, carrot, and chicken; simmer for 5 minutes.
4. Add noodles and simmer until tender, adding water if needed.
5. Garnish with spring onion and serve.

Short Description: A light vegetable soup with simple seasoning.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 cups water or rice-washing water
- 1 cup squash, cubed
- 1 small sayote, sliced
- 4 pieces okra
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 cup leafy greens
- 1 tsp fish sauce, optional
Steps:
1. Bring water, tomato, and onion to a boil.
2. Add squash and sayote; simmer until partly tender.
3. Add okra and cook until the vegetables are tender.
4. Stir in leafy greens and cook for 1–2 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce if desired and serve hot.

Short Description: A thick noodle soup with pork, liver, and eggs.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g fresh lomi noodles
- 100 g pork, thinly sliced
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup cabbage, sliced
- 1/2 small carrot, sliced
- 3 cups chicken broth
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Rinse fresh noodles briefly if needed and drain.
2. Sauté garlic and pork in oil until cooked.
3. Add broth and soy sauce; bring to a simmer.
4. Add carrot, cabbage, and noodles; cook until noodles are tender.
5. Stir in cornstarch slurry, then slowly add beaten egg while stirring.

Short Description: Batangas-style lomi is a very thick fresh-egg-noodle soup loaded with pork, liver, kikiam, and egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g fresh lomi egg noodles
- 100 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 50 g pork liver, thinly sliced
- 1 small kikiam, sliced
- 3 cups pork or chicken broth
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
- 1 tbsp crushed chicharon, for topping (optional)
- Ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Rinse the fresh lomi noodles briefly if the package recommends it, then drain.
2. Heat oil in a pot. Sauté garlic and pork until the pork is lightly browned.
3. Add broth and soy sauce, bring to a simmer, and cook for 8-10 minutes until the pork is tender.
4. Add liver and sliced kikiam and simmer until the liver is cooked through.
5. Add lomi noodles and cook just until tender, following package directions.
6. Stir the cornstarch slurry and add gradually to make the broth very thick. Slowly pour in the beaten egg while stirring so it forms fine ribbons in the soup.
7. Finish with black pepper and optional crushed chicharon. Serve immediately; the noodles will continue to thicken the soup as they stand.

Short Description: A Visayan sour fish soup with ginger and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces firm fish steaks
- 2 tomatoes, chopped
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 small onion, sliced
- 2 cups water
- 1–2 tbsp tamarind pulp or calamansi juice to taste
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 small eggplant, sliced, optional
Steps:
1. Place water, ginger, onion, and tomatoes in a pot and bring to a boil.
2. Add the souring agent and simmer for 3 minutes.
3. Add fish and eggplant, if using; simmer gently until fish is cooked.
4. Season with fish sauce and adjust sourness to taste.
5. Serve hot with rice.

Short Description: A light fish soup with ginger, tomatoes, and leafy greens.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces fish steaks
- 3 cups water
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 tomato, quartered
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 small sayote, sliced
- 1 cup pechay or leafy greens
- 1 tsp fish sauce
Steps:
1. Bring water, ginger, tomato, and onion to a boil.
2. Add sayote and simmer until partly tender.
3. Add fish and simmer gently until cooked through.
4. Add leafy greens and cook for 1–2 minutes.
5. Season with fish sauce and serve.

Short Description: A Chinese-Filipino soup with meatballs and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 100 g chicken breast, thinly sliced
- 75 g pork, thinly sliced
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 3 cups chicken broth
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic in oil, then add chicken and pork and cook until no longer pink.
2. Pour in broth and soy sauce; simmer for 8 minutes.
3. Add carrot and cabbage and cook until tender-crisp.
4. Slowly pour in beaten egg while stirring the broth.
5. Season with pepper and serve hot.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of beef tapa, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Marinating Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g beef sirloin, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Marinate beef with soy sauce, calamansi, garlic, and sugar for 15 minutes.
2. Pan-fry beef until browned and cooked through.
3. In a separate pan, sauté a little garlic and toss with cooked rice.
4. Fry the egg to your liking.
5. Serve beef with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of longganisa, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces Filipino longganisa
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Place longganisa and water in a pan; cover and cook until heated through.
2. Uncover and cook until water evaporates and sausages brown, adding a little oil if needed.
3. Sauté garlic and toss with rice until fragrant.
4. Fry the egg in the same pan.
5. Serve longganisa with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of tocino, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g pork tocino
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 2 tbsp water
Steps:
1. Cook tocino with water in a pan over medium heat until tender.
2. When water evaporates, allow tocino to caramelize lightly; avoid burning the sugar.
3. Sauté garlic and toss with rice.
4. Fry the egg to your liking.
5. Serve tocino with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of fried milkfish, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces boneless bangus portions
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp calamansi juice
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Season bangus with calamansi, salt, and pepper.
2. Pan-fry bangus in oil until golden and cooked through.
3. Sauté garlic and toss with cooked rice.
4. Fry the egg in the same pan.
5. Serve bangus with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of hotdog, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Allergens: Egg, possible wheat/soy depending on hotdog
Ingredients:
- 2 Filipino hotdogs
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Slice hotdogs if desired and pan-fry until browned and heated through.
2. Sauté garlic in a little oil.
3. Add cooked rice and toss until fragrant.
4. Fry the egg to your liking.
5. Serve hotdogs with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of corned beef, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small can corned beef (about 150 g)
- 1/4 small onion, sliced
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Sauté onion in oil until softened.
2. Add corned beef and cook, breaking it into flakes, until heated through.
3. Sauté garlic in a separate pan and toss with rice.
4. Fry the egg to your liking.
5. Serve corned beef with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of fried danggit, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4–6 pieces dried danggit
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Rinse danggit quickly if very salty and pat dry.
2. Pan-fry in oil until crisp; drain.
3. Sauté garlic and toss with cooked rice.
4. Fry the egg to your liking.
5. Serve danggit with garlic rice, egg, and calamansi.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of embutido, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 slices cooked embotido
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Pan-fry embotido slices until lightly browned and heated through.
2. Sauté garlic in a little oil.
3. Add rice and stir-fry until fragrant.
4. Fry the egg to your liking.
5. Serve embotido with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A breakfast plate of sisig, garlic rice, and a fried egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g cooked pork sisig
- 1 cup cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Calamansi and chili, optional
Steps:
1. Reheat sisig in a hot pan until sizzling and lightly crisp.
2. Sauté garlic and toss with cooked rice.
3. Fry the egg to your liking.
4. Season sisig with calamansi and chili if desired.
5. Serve sisig with garlic rice and egg.

Short Description: A Chinese-Filipino rice dish with sausage and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Allergens: Soy, wheat (if soy sauce contains wheat)
Ingredients:
- 1 cup rice
- 100 g pork belly, diced
- 3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 1/2 cups water or broth
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Rinse rice and set aside.
2. Sauté garlic, onion, pork, and mushrooms in oil.
3. Add soy sauce and rice; stir to coat.
4. Pour in water or broth, cover, and simmer until rice is cooked.
5. Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff, and serve.

Short Description: Rice fried with shrimp paste, served with green mango and sweet pork.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cold cooked rice
- 1 tbsp bagoong alamang
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1/2 small green mango, julienned, for serving
- 1 egg, optional
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
2. Add bagoong and cook for 1 minute to mellow its aroma.
3. Add cold rice and stir-fry until evenly seasoned and hot.
4. Fry an egg separately if desired.
5. Serve with green mango on the side.

Short Description: Fried rice flavored with adobo sauce and meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Allergens: Soy, wheat (if soy sauce contains wheat)
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cold cooked rice
- 1 cup cooked chicken or pork adobo, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp adobo sauce
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 spring onion, sliced
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic until fragrant.
2. Add chopped adobo and cook briefly.
3. Add rice and adobo sauce; break up clumps and stir-fry until hot.
4. Taste and adjust with a little more sauce if needed.
5. Garnish with spring onion and serve.

Short Description: Fried rice with flaked dried fish and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cold cooked rice
- 2 pieces tuyo, fried and flaked
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 spring onion, sliced
- Calamansi, optional
Steps:
1. Fry tuyo until crisp and remove bones; flake the fish.
2. Sauté garlic in oil until pale golden.
3. Add rice and stir-fry until hot.
4. Fold in tuyo flakes and spring onion.
5. Serve with calamansi if desired.

Short Description: Fried rice with sweet longganisa and garlic.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces Filipino longganisa, casings removed
- 2 cups cold cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Cook crumbled longganisa in a pan until browned and fully cooked.
2. Add garlic and onion and sauté briefly.
3. Add cold rice and stir-fry, breaking up clumps.
4. Cook until rice is hot and evenly coated.
5. Serve immediately.

Short Description: A Kapampangan sticky rice dish with coconut milk, chicken, and spices.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice, rinsed
- 2 pieces chicken, cut into small portions
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 1/2 small carrot, diced
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp turmeric
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic and onion in oil; add chicken and brown lightly.
2. Stir in turmeric, rice, carrot, coconut milk, and broth.
3. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally.
4. Add a splash of water if the rice dries before becoming tender.
5. Season with salt and pepper and rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.

Short Description: A Spanish-style rice dish with seafood, meat, and saffron.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup short-grain rice
- 2 pieces chicken, cut small
- 6–8 pieces shrimp
- 1 small chorizo, sliced
- 1/2 small red bell pepper, sliced
- 1/2 cup peas
- 2 cups chicken stock
- 1/2 tsp paprika
- 1/4 tsp saffron or turmeric
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Sauté onion and garlic in oil in a wide pan.
2. Add chicken and chorizo and cook until lightly browned.
3. Stir in rice, paprika, and saffron or turmeric.
4. Pour in stock, arrange shrimp and vegetables on top, and simmer uncovered until rice is tender.
5. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

Short Description: A black paella cooked with squid ink and seafood.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup short-grain rice
- 2 medium squid, cleaned and sliced
- 6 pieces shrimp
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 2 cups seafood stock
- 1–2 tsp squid ink
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Calamansi or lemon, for serving
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic, onion, and tomato in olive oil.
2. Add squid and shrimp and cook briefly; remove shrimp if they cook quickly.
3. Stir in rice and squid ink until the grains are evenly dark.
4. Add seafood stock and simmer until rice is tender, adding seafood back near the end.
5. Serve with calamansi or lemon.

Short Description: Chicken and rice cooked together with tomatoes and spices.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces chicken, bone-in
- 1 cup rice
- 2 1/2 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 small carrot, diced
- 1/2 tsp paprika
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
2. Add chicken and brown lightly on all sides.
3. Stir in rice, carrot, and paprika.
4. Pour in broth, cover, and simmer on low until rice is tender and chicken is cooked.
5. Season with salt and pepper and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

Short Description: Rice cooked with turmeric and spices for a golden color.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked rice
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp annatto oil or 1/2 tsp annatto powder mixed with oil
- 1/2 tsp paprika
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic until fragrant.
2. Add annatto oil and paprika; stir briefly.
3. Add cooked rice and break up clumps.
4. Stir-fry until the rice is evenly colored and hot.
5. Season lightly with salt and serve.

Short Description: A rice porridge with chicken and ginger, a classic Filipino comfort food.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice
- 2 pieces chicken, bone-in
- 5 cups water or chicken broth
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in a pot.
2. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
3. Add rice and water or broth; bring to a boil.
4. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice softens and chicken is cooked through.
5. Season with fish sauce and garnish with spring onion.

Short Description: Rice and viand wrapped in banana leaves, a convenient meal.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Allergens: Soy (if adobo or soy-seasoned meat is used)
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked rice
- 200 g cooked pork or chicken adobo
- 2 banana leaves, cleaned and softened over heat
- 1 small tomato, sliced
- 1/4 small cucumber, sliced
Steps:
1. Briefly pass banana leaves over low heat to soften and wipe clean.
2. Place one cup of rice in the center of each leaf.
3. Add half the adobo to each serving, with tomato and cucumber on the side.
4. Fold the leaves into secure packets.
5. Serve warm; unwrap before eating.

Short Description: Wheat egg noodles stir-fried with pork, shrimp, cabbage, carrot, and snow peas in a savory soy-oyster sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g pancit canton egg noodles
- 100 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 small carrot, cut into matchsticks
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup snow peas, trimmed
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 3/4 cup chicken broth, plus a little more if needed
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Calamansi wedges, for serving
Steps:
1. Prepare the noodles according to the package. If they need boiling, stop when just tender, drain, and set aside so they do not become mushy in the wok.
2. Heat the oil in a wok or wide pan. Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
3. Add the pork and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned. Add the shrimp and cook just until they turn pink; transfer the shrimp to a plate to avoid overcooking.
4. Add the carrot, snow peas, cabbage, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and chicken broth. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender.
5. Add the noodles and toss until the noodles absorb most of the seasoned broth. Return the shrimp to the pan and toss briefly to heat through.
6. Season with black pepper. Serve immediately with calamansi.

Short Description: A Filipino rice-noodle stir-fry in which softened bihon absorbs chicken broth, soy sauce, pork, shrimp, and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 120 g dried bihon (thin rice noodles)
- 100 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 small carrot, cut into matchsticks
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup snow peas, trimmed
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 1 1/2 cups chicken broth
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Calamansi wedges, for serving
Steps:
1. Place the dry bihon in a bowl and cover with room-temperature water for 8-10 minutes, or until flexible but not falling apart. Drain well.
2. Heat oil in a wide pan. Sauté garlic and onion, then add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
3. Add broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce. Bring to a simmer, then add the carrot and snow peas.
4. Add the drained bihon and toss gently as it softens and drinks up the broth. Add a small splash of water only if the noodles are still firm and the pan has become dry.
5. Add the cabbage and shrimp near the end. Toss until the shrimp turns pink and the cabbage just wilts, about 2-3 minutes.
6. Taste before adding more salt because the sauces are salty. Serve hot with calamansi.

Short Description: Thin rice noodles topped with a separate orange shrimp-and-pork sauce, then finished with egg, tinapa, chicharon, and calamansi.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g thin bihon rice noodles
- 75 g ground pork
- 6 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp annatto oil or 1 tsp annatto powder dissolved in warm water
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 1/4 cups shrimp stock or chicken broth
- 1 tbsp fish sauce, plus more to taste
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
- 1 hard-boiled egg, sliced
- 2 tbsp crushed chicharon
- 2 tbsp tinapa (smoked fish) flakes
- 1 spring onion, sliced
- Calamansi wedges, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak the bihon according to the package instructions. Boil briefly if needed, drain, and arrange on a serving plate; do not stir-fry the noodles with the sauce.
2. Heat annatto oil in a saucepan. Sauté the garlic, add the ground pork, and cook until no longer pink.
3. Pour in the shrimp stock and fish sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes so the pork flavors the orange sauce.
4. Add the shrimp and cook just until pink. Stir the cornstarch slurry, then pour it in gradually while stirring. Simmer until the sauce lightly coats a spoon; add a splash of stock if it becomes paste-like.
5. Spoon the sauce over the noodles. Top with sliced egg, chicharon, tinapa flakes, and spring onion.
6. Serve with calamansi. Keep crunchy toppings until the end so they do not go soggy.

Short Description: Malabon-style thick rice noodles coated in a shrimp-and-annatto sauce and topped generously with seafood, tinapa, egg, and chicharon.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g thick Pancit Malabon or palabok rice noodles
- 6 medium shrimp, peeled (reserve shells for stock if available)
- 1 small squid, cleaned and sliced
- 50 g pork belly, boiled and diced
- 1 tbsp annatto oil or annatto water
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 1/4 cups shrimp stock or seafood broth
- 1 tbsp fish sauce, plus more to taste
- 2 tbsp tinapa flakes
- 1 hard-boiled egg, sliced
- 2 tbsp crushed chicharon
- 1 tbsp toasted garlic
- 1 spring onion, sliced
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak or cook the thick rice noodles following the package instructions. Drain well; they should be tender but still hold their shape.
2. Heat the annatto oil in a pan. Sauté the garlic briefly, then add the diced boiled pork and cook for 2 minutes.
3. Pour in the shrimp stock and fish sauce. Bring to a simmer. Add the shrimp and squid and cook briefly until just done; remove the seafood so it does not overcook.
4. Toss the noodles with the seafood sauce until the sauce coats the thick noodles. This version is mixed through the noodles, rather than served as a separate thick flour gravy.
5. Transfer to a platter and arrange the shrimp, squid, tinapa flakes, egg, chicharon, and toasted garlic on top.
6. Garnish with spring onion and serve with calamansi.

Short Description: A Lucban, Quezon pancit made with fresh miki noodles, pork, shrimp, and vegetables, traditionally served on banana leaf with vinegar.
Flavor profiles: Savory, lightly smoky, tangy at the table
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g fresh Lucban miki noodles
- 100 g pork belly or pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 small carrot, cut into matchsticks
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup green beans, sliced diagonally
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 3/4 cup pork or chicken broth
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Banana leaf pieces, washed and softened for serving
- Cane vinegar, for serving
Steps:
1. Rinse fresh miki briefly if needed and drain. Cut the vegetables and pork into thin, even pieces so they cook quickly.
2. Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, then add pork and cook until lightly browned.
3. Add shrimp and cook just until pink. Add carrot and green beans and toss for 1-2 minutes.
4. Add soy sauce, optional oyster sauce, broth, and fresh miki. Toss until the noodles soften and absorb the seasoning; add a small splash of broth if they stick or remain firm.
5. Stir in the cabbage last and cook just until wilted. Taste and adjust the soy sauce.
6. Serve portions on softened banana leaf with cane vinegar on the side. The banana leaf and vinegar are the identifying serving style; the noodles are not served in a soup bowl.

Short Description: A Tuguegarao noodle dish with fresh miki and meat, topped with egg and served with a separate egg-drop broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g fresh miki noodles
- 100 g beef, thinly sliced
- 50 g pork, finely chopped
- 1/2 small carrot, cut into matchsticks
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 1/2 cups beef broth
- 2 eggs (one for topping and one for the broth)
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Calamansi or vinegar-onion dip, for serving
Steps:
1. Warm the beef broth in a small saucepan and keep it at a gentle simmer for the soup served on the side.
2. Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, then add beef and pork. Stir-fry until the meat is lightly browned and nearly cooked through.
3. Add soy sauce, carrot, cabbage, and about 1/2 cup of the broth. Simmer briefly until the vegetables soften.
4. Add the miki noodles and toss until tender and glossy, adding only enough broth to stop them from sticking.
5. Fry or poach one egg for the noodle topping. Beat the other egg and drizzle it into the simmering broth while stirring to make fine egg ribbons; season with pepper.
6. Serve the noodles topped with the egg, with the egg-drop broth in a separate bowl. Offer calamansi or vinegar-onion dip.

Short Description: Thick fresh egg noodles in a hearty, thickened soup with pork, liver, cabbage, and beaten egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g fresh lomi egg noodles
- 100 g pork, thinly sliced
- 50 g pork liver, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup cabbage, sliced
- 1 small carrot, sliced thinly
- 3 cups chicken or pork broth
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
- Ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Rinse the fresh lomi noodles briefly if the package recommends it, then drain well.
2. Heat oil in a pot and sauté the garlic. Add pork and cook until lightly browned.
3. Pour in the broth and soy sauce. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5-8 minutes until the pork is cooked.
4. Add the liver, carrot, and cabbage. Simmer until the liver is cooked through and the vegetables are just tender.
5. Add the lomi noodles and cook according to their package, usually a few minutes, until tender.
6. Stir the cornstarch slurry and add it gradually until the broth thickens. Keep it soupy and glossy rather than dry.
7. Slowly pour in the beaten egg while stirring to form fine ribbons. Season with pepper and serve immediately, before the thick noodles absorb too much broth.

Short Description: Glass noodles stir-fried with chicken, mushrooms, and vegetables, with optional annatto for a warm golden color.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g dried sotanghon (glass noodles)
- 100 g boneless chicken thigh, thinly sliced
- 3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced (or 1/2 cup fresh mushrooms)
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup snow peas or green beans
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp annatto water, optional
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak the sotanghon in water until flexible, following the package timing, then drain and cut the bundle once or twice so it is easy to serve.
2. Heat the oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, add the chicken, and cook until lightly browned.
3. Add mushrooms and carrot. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add soy sauce, fish sauce, broth, and optional annatto water.
4. Bring the liquid to a simmer. Add the soaked sotanghon and toss gently as the glass noodles turn translucent and absorb the broth.
5. Add snow peas and cabbage near the end; cook only until crisp-tender. Add a splash of broth if the noodles become dry before softening.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with calamansi.

Short Description: A stir-fried fresh miki noodle dish with pork, chicken, vegetables, and a lightly thickened soy-oyster seasoning.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g fresh miki noodles
- 75 g grilled or roast pork, thinly sliced
- 75 g boneless chicken, thinly sliced
- 1/2 small carrot, shredded
- 1/2 cup cabbage, chopped
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Separate the fresh miki strands and rinse briefly only if the package instructions recommend it; drain well.
2. Heat the oil in a wok. Sauté onion and garlic, then add chicken and cook until no longer pink. Add the sliced pork and warm through.
3. Add carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
4. Mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, and broth, then pour into the wok. Add miki and toss until the noodles are hot and coated; avoid over-stirring so fresh noodles do not break.
5. Simmer uncovered for 1-2 minutes until the sauce clings lightly. Season with pepper and serve with calamansi.

Short Description: A home-style pancit guisado with fresh egg noodles, pork, chicken, vegetables, and a glossy soy-oyster sauce.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Allergens: Wheat or soy depending on noodle type, soy
Ingredients:
- 150 g fresh miki or egg noodles
- 75 g pork belly, thinly sliced
- 75 g boneless chicken, thinly sliced
- 4 small shrimp, peeled and deveined (optional)
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup green beans, sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 3/4 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Prepare the noodles according to the package and drain. If they are fresh miki, keep them only slightly underdone because they will finish in the sauce.
2. Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, then add pork and chicken. Cook, stirring, until the meat is lightly browned; add shrimp and cook until pink if using.
3. Add carrot and green beans and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Bring to a gentle boil, then add cabbage.
5. Add the noodles and toss to coat. Stir the cornstarch slurry again and add a little at a time until the sauce is glossy and clings to the noodles.
6. Season with black pepper and serve immediately. This is a sauced home-style guisado, not a separate palabok-style topping sauce.

Short Description: Pampanga-style thick rice noodles dipped in boiling water and topped with orange seafood sauce and traditional crunchy garnishes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g thick palabok/luglug rice noodles
- 6 medium shrimp, peeled; reserve shells if making stock
- 50 g ground pork
- 1 small squid, cleaned and sliced (optional)
- 1 tbsp annatto oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 1/4 cups shrimp or seafood broth
- 1 tbsp fish sauce, plus more to taste
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
- 1 hard-boiled egg, sliced
- 2 tbsp tinapa flakes
- 2 tbsp crushed chicharon
- 1 spring onion, sliced
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak the thick rice noodles according to the package; some dried luglug noodles need a long soak. Drain, then blanch in boiling water until tender. Drain and place on a serving plate.
2. Heat annatto oil in a saucepan. Sauté garlic, add ground pork, and cook until no longer pink.
3. Add seafood broth and fish sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes, then add shrimp and optional squid and cook just until done.
4. Stir the cornstarch slurry and add gradually, stirring until the sauce lightly thickens. The sauce should pour over the noodles, not become a solid paste.
5. Spoon the sauce onto the noodles. Top with egg, tinapa, chicharon, and spring onion.
6. Serve with calamansi. Compared with Malabon, luglug noodles are typically blanched separately and topped with sauce rather than tossed together with it.

Short Description: A Cavite specialty that uses mung bean sprouts as the main noodle, with a smoky tinapa-annatto sauce and kamias or calamansi for sourness.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups mung bean sprouts (togue), rinsed and drained
- 75 g pork belly, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp tinapa (smoked fish) flakes
- 1/2 small onion or 2 shallots, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp annatto oil or annatto water
- 1 small kamias, thinly sliced, or 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water, if needed
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Crushed peanuts, optional garnish
Steps:
1. Heat the oil in a wide pan. Sauté shallot or onion and garlic until fragrant.
2. Add pork and cook until browned and cooked through. Add shrimp and sauté until pink; remove the shrimp temporarily so it does not overcook.
3. Stir in tinapa flakes and annatto oil. Pour in the broth and add kamias; simmer for 3-4 minutes so the smoky and sour flavors infuse the sauce.
4. If the broth is very thin, stir in a little cornstarch slurry and simmer until lightly glossy.
5. Add the mung bean sprouts and toss only briefly, about 1-2 minutes, so they stay crisp instead of collapsing like noodles.
6. Return the shrimp, taste, and adjust sourness. Serve warm, optionally topped with crushed peanuts. This Cavite style uses togue in place of ordinary pancit noodles.

Short Description: Caviteño black pancit made with squid ink, rice vermicelli, squid, vinegar, soy sauce, and seafood stock.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g sotanghon or bihon rice noodles, soaked and drained
- 200 g small squid, cleaned and sliced; reserve ink sacs if using fresh ink
- 1-2 tsp squid ink (or ink from the cleaned squid)
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bay leaf
- 2 tbsp vinegar
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 3/4 cup seafood stock or water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp tinapa flakes, for topping
- Crushed chicharon and calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak the rice noodles until pliable and drain. If using fresh squid, remove the ink sac carefully and mix the ink with the vinegar and 2 tbsp water; bottled squid ink may be used instead.
2. Heat oil in a wide pan. Sauté garlic, onion, and bay leaf until fragrant.
3. Add squid and cook for only 1-2 minutes until just opaque. Remove it to a plate so it does not turn rubbery.
4. Pour in the ink mixture, soy sauce, fish sauce, and seafood stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes.
5. Add the soaked noodles and toss over low heat until they absorb the black sauce and become tender but not mushy. Add a splash of stock if needed.
6. Return the squid for the last minute only. Top with tinapa and chicharon, and serve with calamansi.

Short Description: A Filipino coconut-based pancit variation that uses thin young-coconut strips as the main noodle instead of ordinary bihon.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups young coconut meat (buko), cut into thin noodle-like strips
- 75 g boneless chicken, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 3/4 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp coconut oil or neutral cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Cut the tender buko meat into thin, noodle-like strips. Keep it separate from the vegetables because it softens faster than dried noodles.
2. Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and onion, then add chicken and cook until no longer pink.
3. Add shrimp and cook just until pink. Add carrot, soy sauce, fish sauce, and broth; simmer for 2-3 minutes.
4. Add cabbage and buko strips. Toss gently for only 1-2 minutes, until hot but still retaining some bite.
5. Season with black pepper and adjust the fish sauce. Serve immediately with calamansi. This version deliberately uses young coconut meat as the noodle base; some regional versions add wheat or rice noodles as well.

Short Description: A Cebuano noodle dish combining canton egg noodles and sotanghon glass noodles with pork, chicken, shrimp, and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 75 g pancit canton egg noodles
- 75 g sotanghon glass noodles
- 75 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 50 g cooked chicken, shredded
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup green beans, sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 cup chicken broth, plus more if needed
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak the sotanghon until flexible and drain. Prepare the canton noodles according to their package directions; keep them separate for now.
2. Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, then stir-fry the pork until lightly browned.
3. Add shrimp and cook until pink, then add carrot and green beans. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
4. Add broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Bring to a simmer, then add the canton noodles and toss until they begin to soften.
5. Add sotanghon and shredded chicken. Toss gently until both noodle types are cooked and most of the liquid has been absorbed; add a splash of broth if needed.
6. Fold in cabbage at the end so it remains slightly crisp. Serve hot with calamansi.

Short Description: Isabela-style fresh miki noodles cooked in beef broth and topped with boiled quail eggs, crispy pork, and optional igado.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g fresh miki noodles
- 100 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup beef broth, plus 1 cup for the noodles
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp fish sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed or minced
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 small bell pepper, sliced
- 1/2 cup cabbage, chopped
- 4 quail eggs, hard-boiled and peeled
- 50 g chopped lechon kawali or crispy pork, for topping
- 50 g cooked igado or pork liver stew, optional topping
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
- Vinegar-onion dip, optional
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a wok and sauté the garlic until lightly golden.
2. Add pork and stir-fry until it begins to brown. Pour in the beef broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce; cover and simmer for about 10-12 minutes, until the pork is tender. Add a splash of broth if the pan gets dry.
3. Add the fresh miki and toss for about 2 minutes so the noodles absorb the seasoned broth.
4. Add carrot, bell pepper, and cabbage. Toss for another 3-5 minutes until the vegetables are just tender and the noodles remain saucy.
5. Season with pepper. Top with halved quail eggs, crispy pork, and optional igado just before serving so the toppings stay distinct.
6. Serve with vinegar-onion dip. Cabagan is generally saucier than dry pancit and commonly uses fresh miki and quail eggs.

Short Description: Lucena-style thick miki noodles in a glossy sweet-spicy sauce with pork, shrimp, vegetables, and a little brown sugar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g fresh flat miki noodles
- 100 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 small carrot, cut into strips
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 small bell pepper, sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp banana ketchup
- 1 tsp brown sugar, or to taste
- 3/4 cup pork or chicken broth
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Chili, optional; calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a wok and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
2. Add pork and stir-fry until lightly browned. Add shrimp and cook just until pink, then remove shrimp temporarily.
3. Add carrot and bell pepper. Pour in the broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce, banana ketchup, and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer and taste for the sweet-spicy balance.
4. Add fresh miki and toss for 3-5 minutes, until it softens and absorbs some sauce.
5. Stir the cornstarch slurry, add a little at a time, and toss until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the noodles. Add cabbage and return shrimp for the last 1-2 minutes.
6. Add optional chili and serve with calamansi. Keep the sauce glossy and slightly saucy rather than dry.

Short Description: A party-style pancit that combines three noodle types—canton, sotanghon, and miki—with pork, chicken, and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 50 g pancit canton egg noodles
- 50 g sotanghon glass noodles
- 50 g fresh miki noodles
- 75 g ground pork
- 75 g cooked shredded chicken
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined (optional)
- 1/2 small carrot, cut into strips
- 1/4 cup green beans, sliced
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 1/2 cups chicken broth, plus more if needed
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 tbsp crushed chicharon, for topping (optional)
- 1 spring onion, sliced
Steps:
1. Soak sotanghon in water until flexible and drain. Prepare canton and miki noodles according to their package instructions; set each type aside.
2. Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, then add ground pork and cook until browned.
3. Add shrimp if using, then add carrot and green beans. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
4. Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Bring to a simmer.
5. Add miki and canton first, tossing until they soften. Add sotanghon and shredded chicken, then toss gently until all three noodle types are tender and seasoned; add more broth if needed.
6. Fold in cabbage for the final 1-2 minutes. Top with spring onion and optional crushed chicharon before serving.

Short Description: Pork-and-vegetable glass noodles colored with annatto and finished with toasted garlic and green onion.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g sotanghon (glass noodles), soaked and drained
- 100 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/4 cup snow peas or green beans
- 1/2 small red bell pepper, sliced (optional)
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp fish sauce, or to taste
- 1 cup pork or chicken broth
- 1 tsp annatto seeds or 1 tsp annatto water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Soak the sotanghon for 10-12 minutes, or until pliable, then drain.
2. Heat the oil and fry the garlic until golden. Remove the toasted garlic and reserve it as a topping.
3. If using annatto seeds, briefly stir them in the garlic-infused oil until the oil turns orange, then discard the seeds. (Skip this step if using annatto water.)
4. Add pork and cook until browned. Add onion and carrot and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
5. Add soy sauce, fish sauce, broth, cabbage, and snow peas. Bring to a simmer, then add sotanghon and toss until the noodles turn translucent and absorb the liquid.
6. Add bell pepper if using and cook until just tender. Season with black pepper and top with the reserved toasted garlic before serving.

Short Description: A mixed pancit combining fresh miki and rice bihon, so each bite has both chewy egg noodles and softer rice noodles.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 75 g fresh miki noodles
- 75 g dried bihon rice noodles
- 100 g pork or chicken, thinly sliced
- 4 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined (optional)
- 1/2 small carrot, julienned
- 1/2 cup cabbage, shredded
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 1/4 cups chicken broth
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Calamansi, for serving
Steps:
1. Soak bihon in water until flexible and drain. Prepare the fresh miki separately according to its package directions.
2. Heat oil in a wok. Sauté garlic and onion, then add pork or chicken and stir-fry until cooked. Add shrimp if using and cook until pink.
3. Add carrot, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and broth. Bring to a simmer.
4. Add miki first and toss for 1-2 minutes. Add bihon and keep tossing until both noodles are tender and most broth is absorbed; give bihon a splash of extra broth if it firms up before the miki is done.
5. Stir in cabbage at the end and cook until just wilted. Serve with calamansi.

Short Description: Sweet-style Filipino spaghetti with hotdogs and cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g spaghetti
- 150 g ground pork or beef
- 2 Filipino hotdogs, sliced
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 1/2 cups Filipino-style spaghetti sauce
- 1/4 cup grated cheese
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Cook spaghetti in salted water according to package directions; drain.
2. Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
3. Add ground meat and cook until browned, then add hotdog slices.
4. Stir in spaghetti sauce and simmer for 10–15 minutes.
5. Toss with pasta and top with grated cheese.

Short Description: Sweet-style baked spaghetti topped with melted cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g spaghetti
- 150 g ground pork or beef
- 2 Filipino hotdogs, sliced
- 1 1/2 cups Filipino-style spaghetti sauce
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup grated mozzarella or quick-melt cheese
- 1 tsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Cook spaghetti until just al dente and drain.
2. Sauté garlic and onion; add ground meat and cook through.
3. Add hotdogs and spaghetti sauce; simmer for 10 minutes.
4. Combine pasta and sauce in a small baking dish and top with cheese.
5. Bake at 180°C for 15–20 minutes until cheese melts and edges bubble.

Short Description: A noodle soup with egg noodles and savory toppings.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 200 g fresh miki noodles
- 150 g pork shoulder, thinly sliced
- 3 cups pork broth
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic in oil, add pork, and cook until lightly browned.
2. Add broth and soy sauce; simmer until pork is tender.
3. Add noodles and cook until tender.
4. Stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken the broth, then slowly pour in beaten egg while stirring.
5. Season with pepper and serve hot.

Short Description: Grilled chicken intestines skewers, a popular Filipino street food.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g cleaned chicken or pork intestines
- 2 tbsp vinegar
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- Water for boiling
- Spiced vinegar, for serving
Steps:
1. Rinse cleaned intestines thoroughly and boil with garlic, bay leaf, and pepper until tender.
2. Drain and cut into manageable lengths; thread onto skewers.
3. Mix vinegar and soy sauce and brush over the intestines.
4. Grill over medium heat, turning often, until lightly charred and heated through.
5. Serve with spiced vinegar.

Short Description: Orange-battered fried quail eggs, a popular street food.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 chicken eggs, hard-boiled and peeled
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornstarch
- 1/3 cup water, approximately
- 1/2 tsp annatto powder
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Oil for frying
- Spiced vinegar, for serving
Steps:
1. Whisk flour, cornstarch, annatto, salt, and water into a thick batter.
2. Pat eggs dry and coat each one evenly.
3. Heat oil over medium heat.
4. Fry eggs until the coating is crisp and orange.
5. Drain, halve if desired, and serve with spiced vinegar.

Short Description: Steamed pork dumplings, a Chinese-Filipino snack.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 150 g ground pork
- 6 pieces small shrimp, finely chopped
- 1 tbsp chopped onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp sesame oil, optional
- 8 siomai wrappers
- Water for steaming
- Calamansi and chili garlic, for serving
Steps:
1. Mix pork, shrimp, onion, garlic, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
2. Place a spoonful of filling in each wrapper and gather the edges around the filling.
3. Arrange dumplings in a lightly oiled steamer basket.
4. Steam over boiling water for 10–12 minutes until cooked through.
5. Serve with calamansi, soy sauce, and chili garlic.

Short Description: Deep-fried saba bananas coated in caramelized brown sugar on a stick.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4 pieces saba bananas, peeled
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- Oil for frying
- 2 bamboo skewers
Steps:
1. Heat enough oil in a pan to shallow-fry the bananas.
2. Add bananas and fry until they begin to turn golden.
3. Sprinkle in brown sugar and let it melt and coat the bananas.
4. Turn carefully until the sugar forms a glossy caramel coating.
5. Drain briefly, skewer, and serve warm.

Short Description: Deep-fried sweet potato coated in caramelized brown sugar on a stick.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cut into thick pieces
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- Oil for frying
Steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
2. Fry sweet potato pieces until tender and lightly golden.
3. Add brown sugar and allow it to melt around the pieces.
4. Turn gently until the sweet potato is coated in caramel.
5. Drain briefly and serve warm.

Short Description: Banana and jackfruit rolled in a thin wrapper, fried until crisp and caramelized.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces saba bananas, sliced lengthwise
- 1/4 cup ripe jackfruit strips, optional
- 4 lumpia wrappers
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- Oil for frying
Steps:
1. Place banana and optional jackfruit on each wrapper and sprinkle with a little brown sugar.
2. Fold in the sides and roll tightly, sealing the edge with water.
3. Heat oil over medium heat and fry the rolls until lightly golden.
4. Sprinkle remaining sugar into the pan and turn rolls until the sugar caramelizes.
5. Drain briefly and serve warm.

Short Description: Banana fritters, golden and sweet, a popular merienda.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces ripe saba bananas, sliced lengthwise
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup water or milk
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 tsp baking powder
- Oil for frying
- Extra sugar for sprinkling
Steps:
1. Whisk flour, egg, water or milk, sugar, and baking powder into a thick batter.
2. Dip banana slices into the batter and coat evenly.
3. Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan over medium heat.
4. Fry battered bananas until golden on both sides and cooked through.
5. Drain and sprinkle with sugar before serving.

Short Description: Fried banana, sweet and caramelized.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces ripe saba bananas, peeled
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- 1 tsp brown sugar, optional
Steps:
1. Peel the saba bananas and slice lengthwise if they are thick.
2. Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
3. Fry the bananas, turning occasionally, until golden and tender on both sides.
4. Sprinkle with a little brown sugar if desired and let it melt briefly.
5. Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

Short Description: Crispy banana chips, sweet and crunchy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 firm saba or cooking bananas, peeled
- 1 tsp calamansi or lemon juice, optional
- Oil for deep-frying
- 1 tbsp sugar, optional
Steps:
1. Slice the peeled bananas very thinly and evenly.
2. If desired, toss the slices lightly with calamansi or lemon juice to help limit browning.
3. Heat oil over medium heat and fry the slices in small batches, stirring gently, until crisp and lightly golden.
4. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain well; the chips will crisp further as they cool.
5. Add a light dusting of sugar if desired, cool completely, and store in an airtight container.

Short Description: Crispy sweet potato chips, sweet and crunchy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 medium sweet potato (about 250 g)
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Oil for deep-frying
Steps:
1. Scrub and peel the sweet potato, then slice it very thinly and evenly.
2. Rinse the slices briefly and pat completely dry.
3. Heat oil over medium heat and fry the slices in batches until golden and crisp.
4. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.
5. Sprinkle with salt while warm, then cool slightly before serving.

Short Description: A colorful Filipino dessert of shaved ice, sweetened fruits, beans, and milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Allergens: Dairy; possible allergens depend on canned toppings
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup sweetened banana, jackfruit, or mixed fruit preserves
- 1/2 cup sweetened red beans or garbanzo beans, drained
- 1/2 cup nata de coco or kaong, drained
- 2 cups finely shaved ice
- 1/4 cup evaporated milk
- 2 small scoops ube ice cream, optional
- 2 tbsp leche flan, diced, optional
- 2 tbsp pinipig or crushed toasted rice, optional
Steps:
1. Divide the sweetened fruits, beans, and nata de coco or kaong between two tall glasses.
2. Add shaved ice, piling it high above the rim.
3. Pour evaporated milk over each serving.
4. Top with ube ice cream, leche flan, and pinipig if using.
5. Serve immediately and mix together before eating.

Short Description: A refreshing dessert of sweet corn, shaved ice, and milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup sweet corn kernels, cooked and chilled
- 2 cups shaved ice
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 2 tbsp sugar, or to taste
- 2 tbsp condensed milk, optional
Steps:
1. Divide the chilled corn kernels between two glasses or dessert bowls.
2. Stir the evaporated milk with sugar until the sugar dissolves; add condensed milk if desired.
3. Add shaved ice over the corn.
4. Pour the milk mixture evenly over the ice.
5. Serve immediately, stirring before eating.

Short Description: A chilled dessert of young coconut, pandan jelly, and cream.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 25 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: At least 1 hour 25 minutes
Allergens: Dairy; check jelly mix for additives or allergens
Ingredients:
- 1 cup young coconut strips, drained
- 1 cup pandan-flavored gulaman, set and diced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose cream, chilled
- 1/3 cup condensed milk
- 1/4 cup nata de coco, drained, optional
Steps:
1. Prepare pandan gulaman according to its package directions, let it set, and cut it into small cubes.
2. In a bowl, combine the chilled cream and condensed milk.
3. Fold in the young coconut, pandan gulaman, and nata de coco if using.
4. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend.
5. Stir gently and serve chilled.

Short Description: A creamy fruit salad with young coconut, fruit cocktail, and condensed milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Allergens: Dairy; possible allergens depend on canned fruit and add-ins
Ingredients:
- 1 cup young coconut strips, drained
- 1 cup canned fruit cocktail, well drained
- 1/2 cup nata de coco, drained, optional
- 1/2 cup all-purpose cream, chilled
- 1/3 cup condensed milk
Steps:
1. Drain the fruit cocktail and nata de coco well to prevent a watery salad.
2. In a mixing bowl, stir together the chilled cream and condensed milk.
3. Add young coconut, fruit cocktail, and nata de coco if using.
4. Fold gently until the fruit is evenly coated.
5. Cover and chill for at least 1 hour before serving.

Short Description: A creamy, chilled fruit salad with condensed milk and cream, a staple on Filipino party tables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Chilling Time: 3 hours
Overall Time: 3 hours 5 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small can (about 250–300 grams) fruit cocktail, drained
- 1 small jar (about 200 grams) nata de coco, drained
- 1 small jar (about 200 grams) kaong, drained
- 1 small carton (250 ml) all-purpose cream
- 1/2 can (about 150–170 ml) condensed milk
- 1 cup fresh coconut strips
- 1/4 cup cheese, diced
Steps:
1. Drain the syrup from the fruit cocktail, nata de coco, and kaong.
2. Combine the fruit cocktail, nata de coco, kaong, all-purpose cream, condensed milk, fresh coconut strips, and diced cheese in a large bowl.
3. Gently fold the mixture until all ingredients are evenly combined.
4. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 3 hours.
5. Serve chilled.

Short Description: A smooth, creamy coconut milk pudding with corn kernels, topped with toasted coconut curds.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 8 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Chilling Time: At least 1 hour
Overall Time: At least 1 hour 43 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 can (400 ml) coconut milk
- 1/4 cup cornstarch
- 1 small can condensed milk (use about 1/2 of a 300–390 g can)
- 1/4 cup fresh milk
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar
- 1 small can sweet kernel corn (about 150–200 g, drained)
- 2 tablespoons toasted grated coconut, for topping
Steps:
1. Pour the coconut milk into a cooking pot and bring it to a boil, stirring occasionally.
2. Add the sugar, condensed milk, and sweet kernel corn. Stir until evenly combined.
3. Let the mixture simmer for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. In a separate bowl, combine the fresh milk and cornstarch. Whisk until the cornstarch is fully dissolved.
5. Pour the milk and cornstarch mixture into the pot while stirring thoroughly.
6. Continue cooking and stirring until the mixture becomes thick and smooth.
7. Transfer the mixture to a serving tray and flatten the top using a spatula.
8. Allow it to cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour or until firm.
9. Top with toasted grated coconut or latik, if available.
10. Serve cold.

Short Description: A soft meringue roll filled with rich, sweet custard, a classic Filipino pastry.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 5 large eggs, yolks and whites separated
- 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar
- 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1/3 cup granulated sugar
- 1 1/2 tablespoons confectioners' sugar
- 1 small can condensed milk (use about 1/2 of a 300–390 g can)
Steps:
1. Combine the egg whites and cream of tartar in a bowl. Beat with an electric mixer until soft peaks form.
2. Gradually add the granulated sugar while mixing. Continue beating until the meringue becomes semi-firm.
3. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
4. Line a baking sheet or large rectangular baking tray with wax paper and lightly grease it.
5. Spread the meringue evenly over the greased wax paper using a spatula.
6. Bake for 20–22 minutes, or until the top turns light to medium brown.
7. While the meringue bakes, combine the egg yolks and condensed milk in a small pot. Cook over low heat, stirring continuously until thick.
8. Turn off the heat, add the vanilla extract, and mix thoroughly. Set the filling aside.
9. Remove the meringue from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes.
10. Sprinkle the confectioners' sugar over the meringue. Place another sheet of wax paper on top, then carefully flip the meringue using another tray. Remove the tray and the wax paper from the exposed side.
11. Spread the custard filling evenly over the meringue.
12. Starting from the longest side, carefully roll the meringue with the filling on the inside.
13. Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

Short Description: A chewy, sweet sticky rice cake cooked in coconut milk and brown sugar, topped with latik.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice (malagkit)
- 3/4 cup water (180 ml)
- 1 cup brown sugar
- 2 cups coconut milk (480 ml)
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
Steps:
1. Wash the glutinous rice, then combine it with the water in a rice cooker. Cook until the rice is ready but not overly soft.
2. While the rice cooks, combine the coconut milk, brown sugar, and salt in a separate pot.
3. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the coconut milk mixture thickens.
4. Add the cooked rice to the thickened coconut milk mixture and mix well.
5. Continue cooking and stirring until the rice absorbs the mixture and most of the liquid evaporates. Avoid overcooking.
6. Transfer the biko to a serving plate or tray and flatten the surface.
7. Let it cool slightly, then serve.

Short Description: A soft, fluffy rice cake baked in banana leaves and topped with butter, sugar, and cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup rice flour
- 1/8 teaspoon salt
- 2 1/2 teaspoons baking powder
- 3 tablespoons butter, softened
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 1 cup coconut milk (240 ml)
- 1/4 cup fresh milk (60 ml)
- 3 eggs
- 1 salted duck egg, sliced
- 1/2 cup grated cheese
- 1/4 cup grated coconut
- Banana leaves, enough to line the baking pan
Steps:
1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. Combine the rice flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Mix well and set aside.
3. Cream the butter while gradually adding the sugar and whisking.
4. Add the eggs and whisk until well combined.
5. Gradually add the rice flour mixture and continue mixing.
6. Pour in the coconut milk and fresh milk. Whisk for another 1–2 minutes.
7. Line a baking pan with banana leaves, then pour in the batter.
8. Bake for 15 minutes.
9. Remove the bibingka from the oven and top with sliced salted egg and grated cheese.
10. Return the pan to the oven and bake for another 15–20 minutes, or until the top turns medium brown.
11. Remove from the oven and let cool.
12. Brush the top with butter and sprinkle with grated coconut.
13. Serve.

Short Description: A soft, springy rice cake made with rice flour batter, baked and topped with butter and cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice flour
- 1/4 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/3 cup coconut milk
- 1 egg
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- 1/4 tsp baking powder
- Pinch of salt
- 2 tbsp grated cheddar cheese
- 2 thin salted egg slices (optional)
- Grated coconut, to serve
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 180°C and grease a small baking dish or two ramekins.
2. Whisk rice flours, sugar, baking powder and salt; mix in coconut milk, egg and melted butter until smooth.
3. Pour into the dish and top with cheese and salted egg, if using.
4. Bake 25–30 minutes, until set and lightly golden; cool briefly and serve with grated coconut.

Short Description: A sticky glutinous rice cake baked in coconut milk with a caramelized top.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 5 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice
- 1/2 cup water
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- Pinch of salt
- For topping: 1/3 cup coconut cream
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
Steps:
1. Rinse glutinous rice and cook with water until tender and sticky.
2. Simmer coconut milk, brown sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves; stir in the cooked rice.
3. Press mixture into a small greased baking dish.
4. Mix coconut cream and brown sugar, spread on top and bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until glossy and lightly caramelized.

Short Description: Soft, fluffy steamed rice cakes, lightly sweet and perfect for breakfast or merienda.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup rice flour
- 1/2 cup coconut milk or water
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- Pinch of salt
- Water for steaming
Steps:
1. Mix rice flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
2. Stir in coconut milk and melted butter until the batter is smooth.
3. Pour into lightly greased small molds, filling each about three-quarters full.
4. Steam over simmering water for 15–20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

Short Description: Purple steamed rice cakes served with butter, grated coconut, and muscovado sugar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/2 cup purple yam or purple rice flour
- 3/4 cup water, as needed
- 2 tbsp muscovado sugar
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/3 cup grated coconut
Steps:
1. Combine the rice flours and add water gradually to make a moist, crumbly mixture.
2. Press the mixture into small greased narrow steaming molds or shape in parchment-lined tubes.
3. Steam for 10–15 minutes, until cooked through and chewy.
4. Brush with butter and serve hot with grated coconut and muscovado sugar.

Short Description: Fluffy, slightly tangy steamed rice cakes from Calasiao, lightly sweet and springy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Fermenting Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: At least 2 hours
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 3/4 cup rice flour
- 1/4 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/2 cup water, plus extra as needed
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/8 tsp instant yeast
- Water for steaming
Steps:
1. Mix the flours, sugar, yeast and water into a thick, smooth batter.
2. Cover and let stand in a warm spot until slightly bubbly, about 30–60 minutes; avoid over-fermenting.
3. Spoon small drops into lightly greased mini molds or a lined steamer tray.
4. Steam 8–12 minutes, until the cakes look translucent and feel springy.

Short Description: Soft steamed rice cakes topped with melted cheese, sweet and slightly salty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 1 egg
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- 1/4 cup grated cheddar cheese
- Water for steaming
Steps:
1. Whisk flour, sugar and baking powder in a bowl.
2. Beat in evaporated milk, egg and melted butter until no dry flour remains.
3. Fill greased puto molds three-quarters full and add cheese on top.
4. Steam 12–15 minutes until set; let rest for 3 minutes before unmolding.

Short Description: Soft steamed rice cakes from Lanson, a simple, lightly sweet treat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups finely grated cassava, squeezed lightly
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 2 tbsp grated coconut
- Pinch of salt
- Banana leaves or lightly greased molds
Steps:
1. Combine grated cassava, brown sugar, coconut and salt.
2. Line small molds with softened banana leaf or grease them lightly.
3. Press the mixture into the molds without packing it too hard.
