4. Steam for 20–25 minutes until translucent and cooked through; cool slightly before serving.

Short Description: Sticky rice steamed in coconut milk and served with sweet mango or ripe banana.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1 small ripe mango, sliced
Steps:
1. Rinse glutinous rice until the water runs mostly clear and drain.
2. Combine rice, coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a pot.
3. Cover and cook over low heat, stirring once or twice, until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed; add a splash of water if needed.
4. Serve warm with sliced ripe mango.

Short Description: Chewy, translucent brown rice cakes topped with fresh grated coconut.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup tapioca flour
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- 3/4 cup water
- 1/4 tsp annatto powder dissolved in 1 tbsp water
- 1/4 tsp food-grade lye water (optional)
- Grated coconut, to serve
Steps:
1. Whisk all-purpose flour, tapioca flour and brown sugar together.
2. Stir in water, annatto water and optional food-grade lye water until smooth; strain if lumpy.
3. Pour into small greased molds and steam 25–30 minutes until translucent and set.
4. Cool before unmolding and serve with grated coconut.

Short Description: A colorful layered sticky rice dessert with coconut milk and a sweet, chewy texture.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/3 cup condensed milk
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp ube halaya
- 1 tbsp langka jam or jackfruit, mashed (optional)
- Pinch of salt
- Latik or toasted coconut, to serve
Steps:
1. Mix rice flour, coconut milk, condensed milk, sugar and salt into a smooth batter.
2. Divide into three portions; leave one plain, mix ube into one and jackfruit into another if using.
3. Pour one layer into a greased heatproof dish and steam 10–12 minutes; repeat with remaining layers.
4. Steam the final layer until set, about 20 minutes more; cool, slice and top with latik.

Short Description: Soft, chewy cassava jellies coated in fresh grated coconut.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups grated cassava, thawed and drained
- 1/3 cup sugar
- 1/2 cup water
- 1/4 tsp pandan extract (optional)
- 1/2 cup grated coconut
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Mix cassava, sugar, water, salt and optional pandan until combined.
2. Spoon into small greased molds, leaving a little room at the top.
3. Steam 25–30 minutes until translucent and firm.
4. Cool until easy to handle, unmold and roll in grated coconut.

Short Description: Flat, chewy rice cakes boiled and rolled in grated coconut, sugar, and sesame seeds.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- About 1/2 cup water
- 1/3 cup grated coconut
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
Steps:
1. Mix glutinous rice flour with water a little at a time until a soft dough forms.
2. Shape into small balls and flatten into ovals.
3. Drop into gently boiling water in batches; remove when each piece floats, then drain.
4. Mix coconut, sugar and sesame; coat the warm cakes and serve.

Short Description: Sticky rice cooked in coconut milk and wrapped in banana leaves, a traditional Filipino treat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Soaking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Banana leaves, softened over a flame
- Sugar or ripe mango, to serve
Steps:
1. Rinse and soak glutinous rice for 30 minutes, then drain.
2. Simmer rice with coconut milk, sugar and salt until the liquid is mostly absorbed but the rice is still firm.
3. Spoon onto softened banana leaves, fold into tight parcels and tie if needed.
4. Steam parcels for 35–45 minutes until the rice is tender; serve warm.

Short Description: Sticky rice cooked with lye water and wrapped in coconut leaves for a chewy, smooth texture.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Soaking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp food-grade lye water
- Banana leaves, softened
- Latik or sugar, to serve
Steps:
1. Rinse the rice and soak for 30 minutes; drain well.
2. Mix rice with coconut milk, sugar, salt and a small measured amount of food-grade lye water.
3. Wrap portions tightly in banana leaves, making compact parcels.
4. Steam 45–55 minutes until the rice is fully tender; cool slightly and serve with latik or sugar.

Short Description: Chocolate sticky rice rolls wrapped in banana leaves, sweet and chewy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Allergens: Coconut, dairy if using milk chocolate
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp cocoa powder
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- Pinch of salt
- Banana leaves, softened
Steps:
1. Mix rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, butter and salt into a pliable dough.
2. Divide in half and knead cocoa into one half; leave the other plain.
3. Roll small portions of both doughs together into short logs and wrap in banana leaves.
4. Steam for 35–45 minutes until firm and cooked through; cool before unwrapping.

Short Description: Sticky rice wrapped in banana leaves, simmered until sweet and chewy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 55 minutes
Soaking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Ibos or young palm leaves woven into tubes, or banana leaves as substitute
- Sugar, to serve
Steps:
1. Rinse glutinous rice and soak for 30 minutes; drain.
2. Warm coconut milk with salt and stir in the rice until it begins to absorb the liquid.
3. Fill ibos tubes loosely, seal the ends and tie securely; use banana-leaf parcels if tubes are unavailable.
4. Steam 45–60 minutes until tender; serve with sugar.

Short Description: A traditional Filipino sweet rice cake (kakanin) made with whole glutinous rice grains, cooked in coconut milk, and sweetened with sugar, often flavored with pandan or jackfruit.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- For the Sticky Rice Base:
- 1 cup glutinous rice (malagkit), washed and drained
- 3/4 cup pure coconut cream (kakang gata)
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 pandan leaves

- For the Caramel Sauce (Arnibal):
- 1 cup pure coconut cream (kakang gata)
- 3/4 cup dark brown sugar or muscovado sugar
- 30 g ripe jackfruit (langka), cut into strips (optional)
Steps:
1. Combine the washed glutinous rice, water, coconut cream, and pandan leaves in a small pot. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and simmer for about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft and sticky and most of the liquid is absorbed. Add a little water if needed. Remove the pandan leaves and set aside.
2. In a separate pan, combine the coconut cream and brown sugar. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring continuously until the sugar dissolves and the mixture begins to bubble.
3. Add the optional jackfruit strips. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy.
4. Add the cooked sticky rice to the caramel sauce. Mix thoroughly until the rice is evenly coated.
5. Continue cooking over low heat for about 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture becomes thick and sticky and begins to pull away from the pan.
6. Lightly grease two small serving bowls or a plate with coconut oil, or line them with clean banana leaves. Transfer the kalamay kanin into the prepared containers and flatten the surface.
7. Allow the kalamay kanin to cool slightly and set before serving.

Short Description: A sweet and sticky Filipino delicacy made with glutinous rice flour, coconut milk, and sugar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 50 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice flour
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- 1 tbsp coconut cream
- Pinch of salt
- Small banana leaves or a greased dish
Steps:
1. Whisk rice flour and coconut milk until smooth, then stir in brown sugar and salt.
2. Cook in a heavy pan over low heat, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
3. When thick and glossy, mix in coconut cream and cook for 3–5 minutes more.
4. Spoon into banana-leaf-lined cups or a dish and cool until set.

Short Description: A sweet, chewy coconut strips and rice flour confection from the Philippines.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 45–60 minutes
Overall Time: Approximately 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
For the Kalamay
- 75 g glutinous rice flour
- 25 g rice flour
- 50 ml pure coconut milk
- 50 g white sugar
- 1/2 cup water

For the Bukayo Topping
- 1/2 cup grated young coconut meat
- 5 tbsp brown sugar
Steps:
1. Combine the grated young coconut and brown sugar in a small pan. Cook over low heat, stirring continuously for 8-12 minutes, until the coconut softens and the mixture becomes sticky. Set aside.
2. In a bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour, rice flour, white sugar, coconut milk, and water. Mix well until smooth and free of lumps.
3. Pour the mixture into a nonstick pan. Cook over low to medium-low heat, stirring continuously to prevent lumps and burning.
4. Continue stirring for 10-15 minutes, or until the mixture becomes thick, smooth, sticky, and dough-like. If it becomes too thick before the flour is fully cooked, add a small amount of water and continue stirring.
5. Lightly grease a small heat-safe dish or line it with a banana leaf. Transfer the cooked kalamay into the dish and spread it evenly.
6. Allow the kalamay to cool until warm, then spread the prepared bukayo topping evenly over the surface.
7. Let it cool completely until set. Slice into two portions and serve.

Short Description: A dense, chewy cassava cake topped with a creamy, custard-like layer.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups grated cassava, thawed and squeezed lightly
- 1/3 cup condensed milk
- 1/3 cup coconut milk
- 1 egg
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/4 cup evaporated milk
- Topping: 1/4 cup condensed milk
- 2 tbsp coconut cream
- 1 tbsp grated cheese (optional)
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 180°C and grease a small baking dish.
2. Mix cassava, condensed milk, coconut milk, egg and sugar; pour into the dish.
3. Bake 35–40 minutes until nearly set.
4. Stir topping ingredients together, spread over the cake and bake 10–15 minutes more until golden; cool before slicing.

Short Description: Light, fluffy, and soft sponge cakes, sweet and buttery.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 eggs, separated
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/4 cup cake flour
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- 1 tbsp milk
- 1/4 tsp baking powder
- Pinch of salt
- Sugar for coating
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 170°C and grease two small muffin molds.
2. Beat egg yolks with half the sugar, then mix in butter, milk, flour, baking powder and salt.
3. Beat egg whites with remaining sugar to soft peaks and gently fold into the yolk mixture.
4. Bake 15–20 minutes until springy; brush with butter and dust with sugar.

Short Description: Soft, purple pandesal filled with cheese for a sweet-and-salty bite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours
Overall Time: 2 hours 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups bread flour
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/3 cup warm milk
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tbsp softened butter
- 2 tbsp ube halaya
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/3 cup cheddar cheese cubes
- Breadcrumbs for coating
Steps:
1. Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt; add warm milk, egg yolk, butter and ube halaya.
2. Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth; cover and rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
3. Divide into 6 pieces, fill each with cheese, seal and roll in breadcrumbs.
4. Place on a tray, rise 30 minutes and bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes.

Short Description: A sweet and creamy ube dessert made with macapuno strings.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup ube halaya
- 1/3 cup evaporated milk
- 2 tbsp condensed milk
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/3 cup macapuno strings
- 1/4 tsp vanilla extract
Steps:
1. Warm butter in a small saucepan over low heat.
2. Add ube halaya, evaporated milk and condensed milk; stir until smooth and warmed through.
3. Fold in vanilla and half the macapuno strings.
4. Spoon into serving cups and top with the remaining macapuno; chill or serve warm.

Short Description: Sweet, soft custard candies made from egg yolks and condensed milk, a Filipino favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 3 egg yolks
- 1/2 cup condensed milk
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/4 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 tbsp finely chopped peanuts (optional)
Steps:
1. Whisk egg yolks and condensed milk in a small heavy saucepan.
2. Cook over low heat, stirring continuously, until thick enough to hold its shape.
3. Stir in butter and vanilla; fold in peanuts if using.
4. Cool, shape into small balls or pyramids, and wrap if desired.

Short Description: A soft, sweet cake topped with yema custard frosting.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 50 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 1 small sponge cake (about 15 cm), homemade or plain store-bought
- 2 egg yolks
- 1/2 cup condensed milk
- 1/4 cup evaporated milk
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp grated cheddar cheese
Steps:
1. Bake or prepare a small sponge cake and let it cool completely.
2. Whisk egg yolks, condensed milk, evaporated milk and cornstarch in a saucepan.
3. Cook over low heat, stirring until thick; stir in butter.
4. Spread custard over the cake, sprinkle with cheese and chill until the frosting firms.

Short Description: Crumbly, powdery milk candy with toasted flour and a sweet, nutty flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/3 cup powdered milk
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 3 tbsp melted butter
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Toast flour in a dry pan over low heat, stirring until pale golden and nutty; cool completely.
2. Mix toasted flour, powdered milk, sugar and salt.
3. Add melted butter and mix until the crumbs hold when squeezed.
4. Press firmly into a polvoron mold, release carefully and chill until set.

Short Description: Soft, sweet milk candies rolled in sugar, a Bulacan specialty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup powdered milk
- 1/3 cup condensed milk
- 2 tbsp sugar for coating
- Wax paper, optional
Steps:
1. Mix powdered milk and condensed milk until a soft, moldable paste forms.
2. Chill 15–20 minutes if the mixture is too sticky.
3. Roll into short cylinders or small balls.
4. Coat with sugar and wrap in wax paper if desired.

Short Description: Sweet cashew nougat wrapped in a thin wafer, a classic Filipino candy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup roasted cashews, chopped
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp honey
- 4 small lumpia wrappers, cut in halves
- Water or beaten egg to seal
- Oil for shallow-frying
Steps:
1. Mix cashews, brown sugar and honey until the filling clumps together.
2. Place a small amount on each wrapper and roll tightly, sealing the edge with water or beaten egg.
3. Shallow-fry over medium-low heat, turning until crisp and golden.
4. Drain and cool slightly; the filling will be hot.

Short Description: Crunchy, sweet coconut strips caramelized in brown sugar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup grated young coconut
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- 2 tbsp water
- 1 tsp calamansi juice
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Combine brown sugar, water and salt in a pan; simmer until dissolved.
2. Add grated coconut and stir over low heat until the syrup thickens and coats the coconut.
3. Stir in calamansi juice and cook until sticky but still moist.
4. Spoon into small mounds on parchment and cool until firm.

Short Description: A flaky pie filled with sweet young coconut custard, a Laguna specialty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 5 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 small ready-made pie crust (about 15 cm) plus top crust
- 1 cup young coconut strips
- 1/3 cup evaporated milk
- 1/4 cup condensed milk
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tbsp butter
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 180°C and set the bottom crust in a small pie dish.
2. Whisk milk, condensed milk, cornstarch and egg yolk in a saucepan; cook until lightly thickened.
3. Fold in young coconut and butter, then cool slightly.
4. Fill crust, cover with top crust, seal and vent; bake 35–40 minutes until golden.

Short Description: A sweet and buttery tart filled with creamy young coconut custard.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4 small tart shells
- 1/2 cup young coconut strips
- 1/4 cup condensed milk
- 2 tbsp evaporated milk
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tsp butter
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 175°C and arrange tart shells on a baking tray.
2. Whisk condensed milk, evaporated milk, egg yolk and cornstarch until smooth.
3. Fold in coconut strips and melted butter.
4. Fill the shells and bake 20–25 minutes until the custard sets and the edges are golden.

Short Description: A soft, rolled sponge cake with a light, buttery flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 eggs, separated
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/4 cup cake flour
- 1 tbsp milk
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- 1/4 tsp baking powder
- 2 tbsp softened butter
- 1 tbsp powdered sugar
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 180°C and line a small shallow pan with parchment.
2. Beat yolks with half the sugar; mix in flour, milk, melted butter and baking powder.
3. Beat whites with remaining sugar to soft peaks and gently fold into batter; bake 10–12 minutes.
4. Turn warm cake onto sugared parchment, peel away the liner, spread softened butter, roll gently and cool.

Short Description: A chilled, creamy dessert of layered graham crackers, cream, and sweet mango.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: At least 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup ripe mango slices
- 3/4 cup all-purpose cream, chilled
- 1/3 cup condensed milk
- 6 graham crackers
- 1 tbsp crushed graham crackers, for topping
Steps:
1. Whip chilled cream until slightly thick, then fold in condensed milk.
2. Arrange graham crackers in a small container to form the first layer.
3. Spread cream mixture over the crackers and add mango slices; repeat layers.
4. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.

Short Description: A chilled, creamy dessert of layered graham crackers, cream, and ripe avocado.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 3 hours
Overall Time: 3 hours 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 ripe avocado, diced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose cream, chilled
- 2 tbsp condensed milk
- 6 graham crackers
- 1 tsp calamansi juice (optional)
Steps:
1. Mash half the avocado with condensed milk and optional calamansi; leave the rest in small pieces.
2. Fold the mashed avocado into the chilled cream.
3. Layer graham crackers, cream mixture and avocado pieces in a small container.
4. Chill for 2–3 hours until the crackers soften; serve cold.

Short Description: A sweet, creamy dessert of ripe mango and tapioca pearls in milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Chilling Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup small tapioca pearls
- 1 ripe mango, diced
- 1/2 cup evaporated milk
- 1/4 cup coconut milk or all-purpose cream
- 2 tbsp condensed milk
- 1 cup water
Steps:
1. Boil tapioca pearls in water, stirring often, until mostly translucent; follow package directions.
2. Drain and rinse under cool water until no longer sticky.
3. Mix milk, coconut milk or cream, and condensed milk in a bowl.
4. Fold in tapioca and mango, chill for 1 hour and serve cold.

Short Description: A sweet, refreshing drink of tapioca pearls, gulaman jelly, and brown sugar syrup.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Cooling Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: At least 1 hour
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup small tapioca pearls
- 1 cup water for tapioca
- 1/2 cup gulaman jelly, cubed
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1/4 cup water for syrup
- 2 cups cold water
- 1 tsp vanilla extract (optional)
Steps:
1. Cook tapioca pearls in boiling water until translucent, then drain and rinse.
2. Simmer brown sugar with 1/4 cup water until dissolved; cool the syrup.
3. Divide tapioca and gulaman between two glasses.
4. Add syrup, cold water and optional vanilla, stir and serve with ice.

Short Description: A warm, creamy dessert of sticky rice balls, sweet potatoes, and saba in coconut milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice flour
- About 1/4 cup water
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water
- 1 small saba banana, sliced
- 1/2 cup kamote cubes
- 1/4 cup cooked sago pearls
- 2 tbsp sugar
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Mix glutinous rice flour with enough water to form a soft dough; roll into small balls.
2. Bring coconut milk and water to a gentle simmer with sugar and salt.
3. Add kamote and cook until almost tender, then add rice balls and simmer until they float.
4. Add banana and cooked sago; simmer 3–5 minutes more and serve warm.

Short Description: A sweet, creamy corn and sticky rice porridge cooked in coconut milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup glutinous rice
- 2 cups water
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup sweet corn kernels
- 2 tbsp sugar
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Rinse glutinous rice and simmer in water until soft, stirring occasionally.
2. Add coconut milk, corn, sugar and salt.
3. Cook on low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring often so the bottom does not scorch.
4. Add a little water if too thick and serve warm or chilled.

Short Description: A coconut-milk dessert with rice-flour bilo-bilo, taro, sweet potato, saba banana, and jackfruit.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice flour
- About 1/4 cup water, added gradually for the rice balls
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 cup water, plus more if needed
- 1/2 cup gabi (taro), peeled and cubed
- 1/2 cup kamote (sweet potato), cubed
- 1 small saba banana, sliced
- 1/4 cup jackfruit strips
- 2 tbsp sugar, or to taste
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Add water gradually to the glutinous rice flour and knead into a soft dough. Roll into small marble-sized balls and cover them so they do not dry out.
2. Simmer gabi and kamote in 1 cup water until nearly tender, about 8-10 minutes.
3. Add coconut milk, sugar, and salt and bring back to a gentle simmer; stir the bottom of the pot so the coconut milk does not scorch.
4. Add the rice balls a few at a time, stirring gently. Simmer until they float and are cooked through, about 5-8 minutes.
5. Add saba and jackfruit for the last 3-5 minutes. Add more water or coconut milk if the dessert becomes too thick.
6. Serve warm. The rice-flour balls (bilo-bilo) are the defining element of Ginataang Halo-Halo in this version.

Short Description: Ripe saba bananas simmered in sweet coconut milk, warm and comforting.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 ripe saba bananas, sliced
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- Pinch of salt
- 1/4 cup cooked sago pearls (optional)
Steps:
1. Bring coconut milk, water, brown sugar and salt to a gentle simmer.
2. Add sliced saba and cook gently for 10–15 minutes until tender but not falling apart.
3. Stir in cooked sago if using.
4. Serve warm or chill before serving.

Short Description: A Visayan coconut dessert thickened with glutinous rice, gabi, kamote, saba, and optional jackfruit; it does not rely on rice-flour bilo-bilo.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup glutinous rice, rinsed
- 1/2 cup gabi (taro), peeled and cubed
- 1/2 cup kamote (sweet potato), cubed
- 1 small saba banana, sliced
- 1/4 cup jackfruit strips, optional
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1 1/2 cups water, plus more if needed
- 2 tbsp brown sugar, or to taste
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Rinse the glutinous rice until the water is mostly clear. Simmer it in 1 1/2 cups water, stirring occasionally, until the grains begin to soften and thicken the liquid.
2. Add gabi and kamote and simmer until almost tender, about 10-12 minutes. Add a little water if the rice has absorbed too much liquid.
3. Stir in coconut milk, brown sugar, and salt. Keep the heat low and simmer gently rather than boiling hard.
4. Add saba and optional jackfruit. Cook until the fruit and root crops are tender and the rice has thickened the dessert.
5. Taste and adjust sweetness. Serve warm. This version uses whole glutinous rice to thicken the porridge-like base, instead of forming individual bilo-bilo balls.

Short Description: Sticky rice and coconut grilled in banana leaves, sweet, smoky, and chewy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/2 cup grated young coconut
- 1/4 cup coconut milk
- 3 tbsp brown sugar
- Pinch of salt
- Banana leaves, softened
Steps:
1. Mix glutinous rice flour, coconut, coconut milk, brown sugar and salt into a thick sticky mixture.
2. Place a thin strip of mixture onto a softened banana leaf and fold into a flat parcel.
3. Grill over medium-low charcoal or in a grill pan, turning frequently.
4. Cook 20–25 minutes until the leaf is charred in spots and the rice mixture is firm.

Short Description: Chewy glutinous rice cakes filled with sweet bean paste, a Kapampangan treat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- About 1/2 cup warm water
- 1/3 cup sweetened mung bean paste
- 1/4 cup grated coconut, optional
- 1 tbsp sugar, optional
Steps:
1. Add warm water gradually to glutinous rice flour until a smooth, soft dough forms.
2. Divide into 6 balls and flatten each into a small disc.
3. Place a teaspoon of mung bean paste in the center, seal and roll smooth.
4. Boil gently until the dumplings float and cook 2–3 minutes more; serve plain or roll in coconut.

Short Description: Soft, chewy rice cakes dusted with toasted rice flour and coconut.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/2 cup rice flour for toasting
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp grated coconut
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Toast the rice flour in a dry pan over low heat until lightly fragrant; set aside.
2. Simmer coconut milk, sugar, coconut and salt until the sugar dissolves.
3. Add glutinous rice flour gradually, stirring constantly until the mixture becomes thick and elastic.
4. Dust a board with toasted flour, shape mixture into short logs and coat in more toasted flour; cool before cutting.

Short Description: Toasted young rice flakes, sweet and crunchy, served with milk.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup pinipig
- 1 tbsp butter or margarine
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Toast pinipig in a dry pan over low heat, stirring until crisp and fragrant.
2. Add butter and stir to coat evenly.
3. Sprinkle with brown sugar and a pinch of salt; toss briefly.
4. Cool completely to crisp up before serving.

Short Description: A soft, buttery sponge cake with a creamy frosting, a Camiguin specialty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours 10 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups bread flour
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/3 cup warm milk
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/3 cup yema or sweet custard filling
Steps:
1. Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt; add warm milk, yolk and butter.
2. Knead until smooth and elastic, cover and let rise until doubled.
3. Divide into 6 portions, flatten each, add a spoon of filling and pinch closed.
4. Set seam-side down, rise 30 minutes and bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes until golden.

Short Description: A thick, sticky, and sweet rice and coconut milk sweet treat from Mindanao.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- Pinch of salt
- Banana leaf or lightly greased dish
Steps:
1. Whisk rice flour with coconut milk until smooth.
2. Add brown sugar and salt in a heavy pan and cook over low heat, stirring continuously.
3. Continue cooking 45–60 minutes until very thick, dark and glossy; lower heat if it sticks.
4. Spread into a greased dish or banana-leaf-lined tray and cool fully before slicing.

Short Description: Thin, flaky flatbread filled with sweet muscovado, a Negrense specialty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 tbsp shortening or butter
- 1/4 cup water, as needed
- 1/3 cup muscovado sugar
- 1 tbsp flour for filling
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Mix flour, salt and shortening; add water gradually to make a soft dough.
2. Divide into 4 balls and rest 10 minutes.
3. Mix muscovado with 1 tbsp flour; fill each dough ball, seal and flatten gently into a thin disc.
4. Cook in a dry skillet over medium-low heat until both sides have brown spots and the filling is melted.

Short Description: Crisp, thin wafer rolls made of egg whites and flour, sweet and delicate.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 tbsp melted butter
- 2 tbsp milk
- 1/4 tsp vanilla
Steps:
1. Whisk egg and sugar until combined.
2. Stir in flour, melted butter, milk and vanilla to make a smooth thin batter.
3. Spread a very thin layer onto a lightly greased hot wafer iron or nonstick pan; cook until golden.
4. Roll immediately around a clean pencil or narrow dowel and cool until crisp.

Short Description: Crunchy peanut brittle coated in caramelized sugar, a classic Filipino snack.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup roasted peanuts
- 1/2 cup sugar
- 1 tbsp water
- 1 tsp butter
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Line a small tray with parchment and lightly grease it.
2. Heat sugar and water in a heavy saucepan without stirring until amber; swirl the pan gently if needed.
3. Stir in peanuts, butter and salt quickly.
4. Spread thinly on the tray and cool completely before breaking into pieces.

Short Description: A buttery tart filled with sweet pili nut filling.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 4 small tart shells
- 1/3 cup pili nuts, chopped
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 egg yolk
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 175°C and place tart shells on a baking tray.
2. Mix chopped pili nuts, brown sugar, butter, honey and egg yolk.
3. Spoon filling into shells without overfilling.
4. Bake 18–22 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is set; cool before serving.

Short Description: Crunchy brittle made with pili nuts and caramelized sugar.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup pili nuts
- 1/2 cup sugar
- 1 tbsp water
- 1 tsp butter
- Pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Line a small tray with parchment and grease lightly.
2. Cook sugar and water in a heavy pan until deep golden, swirling the pan carefully.
3. Stir in pili nuts, butter and salt until coated.
4. Spread thinly on the tray and leave to cool fully before snapping into pieces.

Short Description: Crispy, buttery meringue cookies sandwiched with creamy buttercream.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Freezing Time: 3 hours
Overall Time: At least 4 hours
Ingredients:
- 2 egg whites
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/3 cup ground cashews or cashew crumbs
- 1 tbsp flour
- 1/3 cup softened butter
- 1/3 cup powdered sugar
- 2 tbsp condensed milk
- 1/2 cup crushed butter cookies
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 150°C and line a tray with parchment.
2. Beat egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add sugar and beat to stiff peaks; fold in ground cashews and flour.
3. Pipe small discs and bake 25–30 minutes until dry; cool completely.
4. Beat butter, powdered sugar and condensed milk until fluffy; sandwich two meringues with buttercream, coat sides with crushed cookies and freeze.

Short Description: A dense, chewy cassava cake with a creamy topping and a caramelized top.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups grated cassava
- 1/3 cup coconut milk
- 1/4 cup condensed milk
- 1 egg
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- 2 tbsp grated cheese (optional)
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 180°C and grease a small baking dish.
2. Mix grated cassava, coconut milk, condensed milk, egg, sugar and melted butter.
3. Spread mixture evenly and sprinkle cheese on top if using.
4. Bake 35–45 minutes until set and golden around the edges; cool before slicing.

Short Description: A soft, jelly-like carabao milk dessert, creamy and lightly sweet.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups fresh carabao milk or whole milk
- 1/4 cup rice flour
- 1/4 cup sugar
- Pinch of salt
- 2 tbsp latik or toasted coconut curds
Steps:
1. Whisk milk, rice flour, sugar and salt in a saucepan until smooth.
2. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and pudding-like.
3. Pour into a shallow dish and smooth the surface.
4. Cool until set, cut into squares and top with latik.

Short Description: Soft, buttery bread rolls with a golden crust and a slightly sweet flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups bread flour
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup warm milk
- 1 tbsp softened butter
Steps:
1. Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt; add warm milk and butter.
2. Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth, then cover and rise until doubled.
3. Divide into 4 small rolls, shape into tight ovals and press a shallow crease across each.
4. Rise 25–35 minutes and bake at 180°C for 18–22 minutes until golden.

Short Description: Soft, buttery bread rolls with a sweet filling, a Filipino bakery favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours
Overall Time: 2 hours 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups bread flour
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/3 cup warm milk
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Filling: 1/3 cup fine breadcrumbs
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1 tsp red food coloring diluted in 1 tsp water
Steps:
1. Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt; add milk, yolk and butter, kneading into a smooth dough.
2. Cover and let rise until doubled; mix breadcrumbs, sugar, butter and diluted food coloring for the filling.
3. Divide dough into 4 pieces, fill and seal each, then shape into rolls.
4. Rise 30 minutes and bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes until cooked through.

Short Description: Soft bread rolls filled with a buttery, sweet filling and coated in breadcrumbs.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours
Overall Time: 2 hours 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups bread flour
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/3 cup warm milk
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tbsp butter
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Filling: 2 tbsp butter
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 2 tbsp milk
- Extra breadcrumbs for coating
Steps:
1. Combine flour, yeast, sugar and salt; add milk, yolk and butter and knead until smooth.
2. Cover and rise until doubled.
3. Cook filling ingredients in a small pan until thick and spreadable; cool.
4. Roll dough into small ovals, spread filling, roll up, brush lightly with milk, coat in breadcrumbs, rise 25 minutes and bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes.

Short Description: A soft, buttery sweet roll topped with butter, sugar, and cheese.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours 10 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups bread flour
- 1 tsp instant yeast
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 egg
- 1/3 cup warm milk
- 2 tbsp softened butter
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Topping: 1 tbsp softened butter
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp grated cheddar cheese
Steps:
1. Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt; add egg, milk and butter and knead until elastic.
2. Cover and rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
3. Divide into 4 pieces, roll each into a thin strip, coil and place in greased molds; rise 30 minutes.
4. Bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes; cool slightly, then spread with butter and top with sugar and cheese.

Short Description: Soft, muffin-like cakes with a sweet, buttery flavor, a Ilocano favorite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1 egg
- 2 tbsp milk
- 2 tbsp melted butter
- 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 1/4 tsp vanilla
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 180°C and grease small muffin molds.
2. Whisk egg and sugar until combined, then stir in milk, butter and vanilla.
3. Fold in flour and baking powder just until smooth.
4. Fill molds two-thirds full and bake 12–16 minutes until golden and springy.

Short Description: A flaky Chinese-Filipino hopia pastry; this entry uses the savory-sweet Hopiang Baboy-style filling of candied winter melon and pork fat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 45 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Resting Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: About 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
Filling:
- 1/3 cup candied winter melon (kundol candy), finely chopped
- 1 tbsp finely diced cooked pork fat or bacon
- 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
- 1 tsp finely chopped spring onion (optional)

Water dough:
- 3/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp sugar
- Pinch of salt
- 1/4 cup water, plus a little if needed
- 1 tbsp neutral oil

Oil dough:
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 3 tbsp shortening or lard

Egg wash:
- 1 egg yolk mixed with 1 tsp water
Steps:
1. Mix the water-dough flour, sugar, salt, water, and oil into a smooth dough. Knead briefly, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
2. Mix the oil-dough flour and shortening or lard into a soft paste.
3. Combine the candied winter melon, diced pork fat, sesame seeds, and optional spring onion. Divide into four small portions.
4. Divide both doughs into four portions. Flatten one water-dough portion, enclose one oil-dough portion, then roll into an oval and fold into thirds. Turn, roll, and fold once more to create flaky layers.
5. Flatten each layered dough portion, add one filling portion, seal, and shape into a round. Place seam-side down on a lined tray.
6. Brush with egg wash and bake at 175°C for about 20-25 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool before serving so the filling sets.

Short Description: Flaky hopia pastry filled with thick purple-yam jam (ube halaya), baked until the layers are lightly golden.
Flavor profiles: Sweet, earthy ube, buttery and flaky
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 40 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Resting Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: About 1 hour 25 minutes
Allergens: Wheat, dairy if ube filling contains milk
Ingredients:
Filling:
- 1/2 cup thick ube halaya, divided into four portions

Water dough:
- 3/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp sugar
- Pinch of salt
- 1/4 cup water, plus a little if needed
- 1 tbsp neutral oil

Oil dough:
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 3 tbsp shortening or lard

Egg wash:
- 1 egg yolk mixed with 1 tsp water
Steps:
1. Mix the water-dough flour, sugar, salt, water, and oil into a smooth dough. Knead briefly, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
2. Mix the oil-dough flour and shortening or lard into a soft paste.
3. Divide the ube halaya into four small portions. If the jam is loose, chill it briefly so it is easier to wrap.
4. Divide both doughs into four portions. Flatten one water-dough portion, enclose one oil-dough portion, roll into an oval, fold into thirds, then roll and fold once more to create layers.
5. Flatten each layered portion, wrap around one ube filling portion, and seal the edges. Shape into rounds and place seam-side down on a lined tray.
6. Brush with egg wash and bake at 175°C for 20-25 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool before serving.

Short Description: Flaky hopia filled with sweet mung-bean paste (mongo), cooked down until thick so the filling does not leak during baking.
Flavor profiles: Sweet, nutty mung bean, flaky pastry
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 45 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Resting Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: About 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
Mung-bean filling:
- 1/3 cup dried mung beans, rinsed
- 1/4 cup sugar, or to taste
- Pinch of salt
- 1 tsp neutral oil
- 1-2 tbsp water, if needed

Water dough:
- 3/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp sugar
- Pinch of salt
- 1/4 cup water, plus a little if needed
- 1 tbsp neutral oil

Oil dough:
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 3 tbsp shortening or lard

Egg wash:
- 1 egg yolk mixed with 1 tsp water
Steps:
1. Simmer the mung beans in water until completely soft, about 25-35 minutes. Drain excess water, then mash the beans.
2. Return the mashed beans to a small pan with sugar, salt, and oil. Cook over low heat, stirring, until the mixture is thick and paste-like. Cool completely; a loose filling can split the pastry.
3. Mix the water-dough flour, sugar, salt, water, and oil into a smooth dough. Knead briefly, cover, and rest for 20 minutes.
4. Mix the oil-dough flour and shortening or lard into a soft paste. Divide both doughs and the cooled mung-bean filling into four portions.
5. Flatten a water-dough portion, enclose an oil-dough portion, roll into an oval, fold into thirds, then roll and fold again to create flaky layers.
6. Flatten, fill with mung-bean paste, seal, and shape into rounds. Place seam-side down on a lined tray.
7. Brush with egg wash and bake at 175°C for 20-25 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool before serving.

Short Description: Sticky, sweet glutinous rice cake, steamed and pan-fried until golden.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 40 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Allergens: Egg if dipped; possible soy depending on product
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice flour
- 1/2 cup water
- 1/3 cup brown sugar
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- Banana leaf or greased heatproof dish
Steps:
1. Whisk glutinous rice flour, water and brown sugar until smooth.
2. Pour into a greased heatproof dish lined with banana leaf.
3. Steam 30–35 minutes until firm and translucent; cool completely before slicing.
4. To serve, pan-fry slices until golden, optionally dipping in beaten egg first.

Short Description: Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves with savory fillings.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup glutinous rice, soaked 1 hour
- 2 chicken thigh pieces, diced
- 2 shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp oyster sauce
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/4 tsp ground pepper
- 1 salted egg yolk, quartered (optional)
- Banana leaves, softened
Steps:
1. Drain rice; sauté garlic and chicken until chicken is mostly cooked.
2. Add mushroom, soy sauce, oyster sauce and pepper; cook until the filling is nearly dry.
3. Spoon rice and filling into banana leaves, adding a small piece of salted egg yolk if desired; fold into tight parcels.
4. Steam 45–55 minutes until the rice is fully tender and the chicken is cooked through.

Short Description: A rich, thick Filipino hot chocolate made from tablea cacao tablets.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 tablea cacao discs (about 30 g total)
- 1 cup water or milk
- 1–2 tsp sugar, to taste
- Pinch of salt (optional)
Steps:
1. Heat water or milk in a small saucepan until steaming.
2. Add tablea and whisk or stir until fully melted and frothy.
3. Simmer gently for 2–3 minutes, stirring so it does not catch.
4. Sweeten to taste and serve hot.

Short Description: Refreshing young coconut water with tender strips of coconut meat.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups young coconut water
- 1/2 cup tender young coconut meat
- 1 tsp sugar or condensed milk (optional)
- Ice cubes
Steps:
1. Open a fresh young coconut safely and collect its water.
2. Scoop out tender coconut meat and slice it into thin strips.
3. Combine coconut water and meat in two glasses; sweeten only if desired.
4. Add ice and serve immediately.

Short Description: A refreshing, tangy-sweet drink made from fresh calamansi juice.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Overall Time: 10 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 8–10 calamansi
- 2 cups cold water
- 2–3 tbsp sugar or honey
- Ice cubes
Steps:
1. Cut calamansi and squeeze the juice into a measuring cup, avoiding seeds.
2. Stir sugar into a little warm water until dissolved.
3. Combine calamansi juice, sweetened water and cold water; taste and adjust sweetness.
4. Serve over ice.

Short Description: Ilocos empanada in the Vigan style, using a paler rice-flour crust, Vigan longganisa, egg, and a cabbage-based filling.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 25 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice flour
- 1/4 cup glutinous rice flour
- About 1/3 cup warm water, added gradually
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1 small Vigan longganisa, casing removed and crumbled
- 1/2 cup finely shredded cabbage, squeezed dry
- 2 eggs
- Oil for deep-frying
- Spiced vinegar, for serving
Steps:
1. Mix the rice flour, glutinous rice flour, and salt. Add warm water gradually and knead to a smooth, pliable dough. Do not add annatto if making the paler Vigan-style crust.
2. Cook the crumbled Vigan longganisa in a pan until fully cooked. Remove and drain excess fat; briefly soften the cabbage in the pan, then cool.
3. Divide the dough into two portions. Flatten each very thinly between lightly oiled plastic sheets or parchment.
4. Place cabbage and longganisa on one half of each round, then crack one egg onto each filling. Fold the dough over and seal firmly, keeping the egg contained.
5. Deep-fry one at a time in medium-hot oil until the crust is crisp and cooked through. Turn carefully so the crust does not tear.
6. Drain and serve immediately with spiced vinegar. Fry soon after filling so moisture from the vegetables does not soften the crust.

Short Description: Ilocos Norte (Batac) empanada with orange annatto rice-flour crust, Laoag/Ilocos Norte longganisa, grated green papaya, togue, and egg.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 25 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice flour
- 1/4 cup glutinous rice flour
- About 1/3 cup warm water, added gradually
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp annatto powder dissolved in 1 tbsp warm water
- 1 small Ilocos Norte or Laoag longganisa, casing removed and crumbled
- 1/2 cup grated green papaya, squeezed dry
- 1/4 cup mung bean sprouts (togue)
- 2 eggs
- Oil for deep-frying
- Spiced vinegar, for serving
Steps:
1. Mix the rice flour, glutinous rice flour, and salt. Add the annatto water and enough warm water to make a smooth, pliable orange dough.
2. Cook the crumbled Ilocos Norte longganisa until fully cooked. Squeeze moisture from the grated papaya and combine it with the togue.
3. Divide the dough into two portions and flatten each very thinly between lightly oiled plastic sheets or parchment.
4. Place papaya, togue, and longganisa on one half of each round. Crack one egg onto each filling, fold the dough over, and seal the edges firmly.
5. Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until the orange crust is crisp and cooked through, turning carefully. Avoid very high heat so the crust does not brown before the dough cooks.
6. Drain and serve hot with spiced vinegar. Fry soon after filling for the crispest crust.

Short Description: A smoky Ilocano eggplant dish scrambled with eggs and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 medium eggplants
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 small tomato, diced
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Char eggplants over a flame or under a broiler until the skin is blackened and the flesh is soft.
2. Cool, peel and chop or mash the flesh.
3. Sauté garlic, onion and tomato in oil until softened; add eggplant and season.
4. Pour in beaten eggs and stir gently until just set; serve hot.

Short Description: Tender pork cheek and ear dressed with onions, ginger, chili, and calamansi for a tangy bite.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 20 minutes
Allergens: Possible pork brain if included in traditional variation
Ingredients:
- 3–4 pieces pork cheek or pork ear, about 300 g total
- 1/2 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 1 thumb ginger, minced
- 1 green chili, sliced
- 1 tbsp calamansi juice
- 1 tbsp cane vinegar
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Simmer pork cheek or ear in water until tender, about 45–60 minutes; drain and cool.
2. Slice the pork and grill or sear in a hot pan until browned and smoky.
3. Mix onion, ginger, chili, calamansi juice, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper in a bowl.
4. Toss the grilled pork with the dressing and serve warm; some regional versions add cooked pig brain for a creamy texture.

Short Description: A warm beef brisket and tripe soup in a ginger-vinegar broth.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 250 g beef brisket or beef tripe, cleaned
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 small onion, quartered
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 bay leaf
- 4 cups water
- 2 tbsp cane vinegar or calamansi juice, to taste
- 1/2 tsp whole peppercorns
- Salt to taste
- Chopped green onion, optional
Steps:
1. Rinse the beef or tripe thoroughly; boil briefly, discard the first water and rinse again.
2. Simmer with fresh water, ginger, onion, garlic, bay leaf and peppercorns until tender.
3. Slice the cooked meat and return it to the broth.
4. Season with salt and vinegar or calamansi to taste; simmer 2–3 minutes and serve hot.

Short Description: A rustic stew of snails, beef, bamboo shoots, and young jackfruit with a rich, savory flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup cleaned edible snails or shellfish
- 150 g carabao skin or beef, sliced thinly
- 1/2 cup young bamboo shoots, sliced
- 1/2 cup young jackfruit or squash
- 1/2 cup mushrooms
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fish paste (bagoong)
- 1/4 cup chopped chili, adjust to taste
- 2 cups water
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Clean snails or shellfish thoroughly; blanch meat and drain.
2. Heat oil in a heavy pot and sauté garlic with fish paste until fragrant.
3. Add meat and water; simmer until tender, then add bamboo shoots and jackfruit or squash.
4. Add snails, mushrooms and chili; simmer until all components are cooked through and season carefully with fish paste.

Short Description: Salty cured pork (etag) simmered with tomatoes and onions, a Cordillera specialty.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 50 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 150–200 g commercially prepared etag, thinly sliced
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup water
- 1 small chili (optional)
Steps:
1. Use commercially prepared, food-safe etag; do not attempt uncontrolled home curing or aging.
2. Simmer the etag in water until softened and sufficiently heated through; discard excess salty water if needed.
3. Sauté garlic, onion and tomato in a separate pan until soft.
4. Add the heated etag and a splash of cooking liquid; simmer 5–10 minutes and serve as a small, salty viand with rice.

Short Description: Thin beef slices stir-fried with onions and cabbage until juicy and savory.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 250 g beef sirloin, thinly sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 cup cabbage, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce (optional)
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Pat beef dry and season lightly with pepper and optional soy sauce.
2. Heat oil in a very hot pan and sear beef in batches until browned; avoid overcrowding.
3. Add garlic and onion and stir-fry until fragrant.
4. Add cabbage and cook just until wilted; season to taste and serve immediately.

Short Description: A Batangas specialty of marinated beef strips, pan-fried until sweet and savory.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 5 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g pork shoulder or beef, thinly sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp cane vinegar
- 1 tbsp soy sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp brown sugar
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Mix garlic, vinegar, optional soy sauce, sugar and pepper; coat the thinly sliced meat.
2. Marinate for 20–30 minutes in the refrigerator.
3. Pan-fry the meat in oil over medium heat until browned and fully cooked, adding a splash of water if it dries too quickly.
4. Serve with garlic rice, sliced tomato or vinegar dip.

Short Description: A soft, fresh white cheese made from carabao milk, mild and creamy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Draining Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: At least 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 cups pasteurized whole milk
- 2 tbsp cane vinegar or calamansi juice
- 1/4 tsp salt
- Clean cheesecloth
Steps:
1. Warm milk gently in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
2. Remove from heat and stir in vinegar or calamansi juice until curds separate from whey.
3. Let stand 5 minutes, then strain through clean cheesecloth.
4. Mix curds with salt, press lightly into a small container and chill; use within a few days.

Short Description: Soft, buttery ladyfinger cookies, lightly sweet and crisp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 eggs, separated
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/3 cup cake flour
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1/4 tsp vanilla
- Powdered sugar for dusting
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 170°C and line a baking tray with parchment.
2. Beat egg yolks with vanilla; in a separate bowl beat whites, adding sugar gradually, until stiff peaks form.
3. Fold yolks into whites, then sift in flour and cornstarch and fold gently.
4. Pipe finger shapes onto the tray, dust with powdered sugar and bake 12–15 minutes until pale golden and dry.

Short Description: Two soft sponge cakes sandwiched with a creamy filling.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 35 minutes
Overall Time: 45 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 eggs, separated
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1/4 cup cake flour
- 1 tbsp melted butter
- 1 tbsp milk
- Filling: 1/2 cup milk
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tsp butter
Steps:
1. Heat oven to 170°C and line a small shallow pan with parchment.
2. Beat yolks with half the sugar and mix in flour, melted butter and milk; fold in whites beaten with the remaining sugar.
3. Bake 10–12 minutes until springy and cool; cut into 4 small rectangles.
4. Whisk filling ingredients except butter in a saucepan, cook until thick, stir in butter and cool; sandwich cake layers with custard.

Short Description: A simple, crunchy muscovado sugar candy with a deep caramel flavor.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 20 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup muscovado or panutsa sugar
- 1 tbsp water
- 1 tsp calamansi juice (optional)
- Banana leaf or lightly greased parchment
Steps:
1. Place sugar and water in a small heavy saucepan.
2. Heat gently until the sugar dissolves, then simmer until thick and bubbling; avoid stirring once boiling.
3. Test a drop in cold water: it should harden quickly; add calamansi if using.
4. Pour small rounds onto banana leaf or parchment and cool completely until hard.

Short Description: A soft, creamy rice-flour dish with shredded chicken, coconut milk, and a hint of peanut.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice flour
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1/2 small onion, minced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp peanut butter
- 1/2 cup cooked shredded chicken
- 1 hard-boiled egg, sliced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
- Banana leaves, softened
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Sauté garlic and onion in oil until fragrant; stir in rice flour, coconut milk and broth gradually to form a thick paste.
2. Season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring, until smooth and very thick.
3. Spread mixture onto softened banana leaves; add chicken, a little peanut butter and egg slices.
4. Fold into parcels and steam 30–40 minutes until firm and heated through.

Short Description: A savory pork and blood stew soured with vinegar, similar to dinuguan.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Ingredients:
- 250 g pork shoulder or pork mask, diced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 small onion, chopped
- 1 tbsp cane vinegar
- 1 tbsp fish sauce
- 1/2 cup water or pork stock
- 1/4 cup fresh pork blood from a food-safe source
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 green chili (optional)
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. If using pork mask or ears, parboil until tender, drain and dice; otherwise dice shoulder.
2. Heat oil and brown pork; add garlic, onion and bay leaf and cook until fragrant.
3. Add vinegar and let it simmer briefly without stirring, then add stock and simmer until pork is tender.
4. Stir in fish sauce, pepper and chili; slowly add pork blood and simmer until fully cooked and the sauce is smooth.

Short Description: A savory dish of marinated carabao meat, pan-fried until tender.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Marinating Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: At least 1 hour 5 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 250 g carabao meat or lean beef, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tbsp cane vinegar
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp cooking oil
Steps:
1. Mix meat with brown sugar, salt, vinegar and garlic; cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes for this quick home version.
2. Add the meat and marinade to a skillet with a splash of water and simmer until the meat is nearly tender.
3. Allow the liquid to evaporate, then add oil and fry until browned and cooked through.
4. Serve with garlic rice and atchara; this quick version is not shelf-stable cured meat.

Short Description: Tender beef tongue braised in a savory sauce with onions and tomatoes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
Overall Time: 2 hours
Ingredients:
- 1 small beef tongue, about 300–400 g
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp vinegar
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 cup water or beef stock
- 1 tsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Black pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Simmer beef tongue in water until the outer skin loosens and the meat is beginning to tenderize; peel and slice.
2. Heat oil and sauté garlic, onion and tomato until soft.
3. Add tongue slices, soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaf, sugar and stock; bring to a simmer.
4. Cover and braise gently until tender and the sauce reduces, adding water if necessary.

Short Description: A Visayan fish stew simmered in coconut milk with fermented black beans (tausi).
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces firm fish steaks or small fish, cleaned
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup coconut milk
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tbsp tausi (fermented black beans), rinsed
- 1/2 green mango or 2 bilimbi, sliced
- 1 green chili
- 1 tsp cooking oil
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Heat oil and sauté garlic, onion and tomato until fragrant.
2. Add tausi, coconut milk and water; bring to a gentle simmer.
3. Nestle in the fish and add green mango or bilimbi and chili.
4. Cover and simmer 12–18 minutes until the fish is cooked and the broth tastes sour and savory; avoid stirring roughly.

Short Description: Rice cooked in woven coconut leaves, chewy and fragrant.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 1 cup uncooked white rice
- Water for rinsing and cooking
- 4–6 small woven puso leaf pouches, food-safe
Steps:
1. Rinse rice until the water is mostly clear and drain.
2. Fill each clean woven pouch loosely about halfway with rice so it has room to expand.
3. Arrange pouches in a large pot, cover fully with water and bring to a boil.
4. Simmer 45–60 minutes until rice is cooked through; drain and cool slightly before serving.

Short Description: A Cebuano spring roll of five-spice vegetables, fried until golden and crisp.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 40 minutes
Allergens: Wheat, soy if soy sauce used
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup shredded singkamas or jicama
- 1/4 cup shredded carrot
- 1/4 cup shredded cabbage
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp chopped spring onion
- 1/4 tsp Chinese five-spice powder
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 6 small lumpia wrappers
- Oil for frying
Steps:
1. Squeeze excess liquid from singkamas and vegetables; combine with garlic, spring onion, five-spice powder and soy sauce.
2. Place a spoonful of filling on each wrapper and roll tightly, sealing with water.
3. Heat oil over medium heat and fry rolls in batches until crisp and golden.
4. Drain on a rack or paper towels and serve hot with spiced vinegar.

Short Description: A Visayan fish dish cooked in vinegar, ginger, and chilies.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 pieces fish steaks or small cleaned fish
- 1/3 cup cane vinegar
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 small eggplant, sliced
- 1/4 bitter melon, sliced (optional)
- 3 whole peppercorns
- 1 green chili
- Salt to taste
Steps:
1. Arrange onion, ginger, peppercorns and fish in a shallow pot.
2. Pour vinegar and water over the fish; add salt and bring to a boil without stirring.
3. Lower heat, cover and simmer about 15 minutes.
4. Add eggplant, optional bitter melon and chili; cook until the vegetables are tender and serve with rice.

Short Description: Chicken steamed in banana leaves with ginger, lemongrass, and spices.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 55 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 chicken pieces, bone-in
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1/2 small onion, sliced
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, crushed
- 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised
- 1 cup chicken broth or water
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Banana leaves, softened
Steps:
1. Place chicken, tomato, onion, ginger, garlic, lemongrass, broth, salt and pepper in the center of softened banana leaves.
2. Wrap into a secure packet and tie with kitchen string.
3. Steam or gently simmer the packet in a covered pot for 40–45 minutes until chicken is fully cooked.
4. Carefully open the packet and serve the chicken with its broth.

Short Description: A Visayan pork soup with ginger, lemongrass, taro, and vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Overall Time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Allergens: None of the listed major allergens
Ingredients:
- 3–4 pieces pork ribs or pork shoulder chunks
- 1 thumb ginger, sliced
- 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised
- 1 small onion, quartered
- 1 small gabi, cubed
- 1/2 cup string beans, cut
- 1/2 red bell pepper, sliced
- 4 cups water
- Salt and pepper to taste
Steps:
1. Put pork, ginger, lemongrass, onion and water in a pot; bring to a boil and skim foam.
2. Lower heat and simmer until pork is nearly tender, about 35–45 minutes.
3. Add gabi and cook until soft; add string beans and bell pepper.
4. Simmer until vegetables are tender, season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

Short Description: A sweet sticky snack made from millet and coconut milk, steamed in banana leaves.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup kabog millet or hulled millet
- 3/4 cup coconut milk
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/8 tsp salt
- Banana leaves, softened
- Hot chocolate or ripe mango, to serve
Steps:
1. Pick over millet, rinse well and drain.
2. Bring coconut milk, sugar and salt to a gentle boil; add millet gradually while stirring.
3. Cook on low heat until the grains begin to soften and absorb most liquid, about 15–20 minutes.
4. Spoon onto banana leaves, wrap tightly and steam 35–45 minutes until fully tender.

Short Description: A crispy, lightly sweet fried rice-flour snack.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 30 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Allergens: Egg if included in a family variation
Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rice flour
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1/2 cup water, as needed
- Pinch of salt
- Oil for deep-frying
Steps:
1. Mix rice flour, sugar, salt and enough water to make a thin, pourable batter.
2. Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat; test a small drop to ensure it sizzles.
3. Pour batter through a small-holed ladle or squeeze bottle in thin circular streams over the oil.
4. Fry until crisp and pale golden, drain carefully and cool before serving.

Short Description: Crispy, buttery ring-shaped cookies, sweet and crumbly.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 10–12 minutes
Chilling Time: 0 minutes (optional, if dough is too soft)
Overall Time: 30–32 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup butter
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 2 egg yolks
- 1 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/4 cup milk (60 ml)
- 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
Steps:
1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease a baking tray or line it with baking paper.
2. Cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
3. Add the egg yolks and vanilla extract. Beat until well combined.
4. Sift in the flour and baking powder. Gradually add the milk until a soft dough forms.
5. Roll the dough to about 1/4 inch thick.
6. Cut the dough into flower-shaped rings with a small hole in the center.
7. Arrange the cookies on the prepared baking tray.
8. Bake for 10–12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden.
9. Let the rosquillos cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container.

Short Description: Crunchy, caramelized banana and sweet potato fritters, sweet and crunchy.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 25 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Overall Time: 50 minutes
Ingredients:
- 2–3 firm saba bananas, preferably unripe
- Oil for deep-frying
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 tablespoon water (15 ml)
- 1 teaspoon butter, optional
- 2 teaspoons sesame seeds (linga)
- A small pinch of salt
Steps:
1. Peel the saba bananas and slice them lengthwise into thin, even strips.
2. Pat the banana strips dry thoroughly.
3. Heat the oil in a pan and fry the banana strips until crisp and lightly golden. Remove and drain on a rack.
4. In a clean pan, combine the brown sugar, water, butter if using, and salt.
5. Cook over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes bubbling and syrupy.
6. Add the fried banana strips and quickly toss them in the caramel until evenly coated.
7. Sprinkle the sesame seeds over the bananas while the caramel is still sticky.
8. Transfer the strips to an oiled tray or parchment paper, separating them as much as possible.
9. Allow them to cool completely until crisp before serving.

Short Description: A sweet, sticky Leyte delicacy made from taro, coconut milk, and sugar, steamed in coconut shells.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 25 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour 40 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kg gabi or talyan (taro)
- 1 small pack coconut milk (200 ml)
- 1/4 cup condensed milk
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 egg yolk
- 1 tablespoon butter, melted
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- Banana leaves, softened over a flame
- 2 small heatproof bowls or clean coconut shell halves
Steps:
1. Peel and steam or boil the gabi until very tender. Mash it while still warm until smooth.
2. In a heavy pan, combine the coconut milk, condensed milk, brown sugar, butter, and salt. Warm over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
3. Add the mashed gabi and cook slowly, stirring often, until the mixture becomes thick and heavy but remains spreadable.
4. Remove the pan from the heat and let the mixture cool for a few minutes.
5. Add the egg yolk and mix thoroughly.
6. Line the bowls or coconut shell halves with softened banana leaves and spoon in the mixture.
7. Cover with more banana leaves or foil, then steam for 40–50 minutes or until set.
8. Allow to cool until warm before serving.

Short Description: A sweet, chewy treat of pinipig, young coconut, and brown sugar wrapped in banana leaves.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 10 minutes
Overall Time: 25 minutes
Allergens: None of the major common allergens listed in the recipe
Ingredients:
- 1 cup pinipig
- 1/2 cup grated young coconut
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1/8 teaspoon salt
- 1–2 tablespoons coconut milk (15–30 ml), as needed
- Banana leaves or wax paper for wrapping
Steps:
1. Toast the pinipig in a pan over medium-low heat until fragrant. Let it cool.
2. Pound the toasted pinipig using a mortar and pestle until it becomes a coarse meal. Do not grind it into fine flour.
3. Combine the pounded pinipig, grated young coconut, brown sugar, and salt in a bowl.
4. Add the coconut milk a little at a time, mixing and kneading gently until the mixture holds together when pressed.
5. Taste and adjust the sweetness if needed.
6. Shape the mixture into small compact logs or ovals.
7. Wrap each piece in banana leaf or wax paper.
8. Let the pieces rest for 15 minutes before serving.

Short Description: A fruity, creamy dessert of layered fruit, gelatin, and cream in a tall glass.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Chilling Time: 2 hours, or until the jelly sets
Overall Time: About 2 hours 10 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1 cup watermelon, diced
- 1/2 cup ripe papaya, diced
- 1/2 cup melon, diced
- 1/2 cup pineapple, diced
- 1 small pack strawberry-flavored jelly powder
- 1/2 cup all-purpose cream, chilled
- 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract, optional
- 2 scoops strawberry ice cream
Steps:
1. Prepare the strawberry jelly according to the package instructions. Refrigerate until completely set, then cut into small cubes.
2. Chill the all-purpose cream. Mix in the vanilla extract if using.
3. Cut the watermelon, papaya, melon, and pineapple into bite-sized pieces.
4. Divide the fruit among two tall glasses.
5. Add the strawberry jelly cubes on top of the fruit.
6. Pour the chilled cream over the fruit and jelly.
7. Top each glass with a scoop of strawberry ice cream.
8. Serve immediately.

Short Description: A fresh, tangy salad of pomelo and shrimp in a light dressing.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Chilling Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 35 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kg hipon, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 shrimp broth cube
- 1 cup water (240 ml)
- 1 small cucumber, seeded and cut into strips
- 1 tomato, cut into wedges
- 1/2 small suha (pomelo), peeled and separated into segments
- 1–2 cups lettuce or other available salad greens
- 1 egg, hard-boiled and cut into wedges
- 1 small handful fried wonton strips or croutons, optional

DRESSING
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 2 teaspoons vinegar
- 1 teaspoon minced garlic
- 1 teaspoon mustard
- 1 tablespoon calamansi juice
- 1 teaspoon chili sauce, optional
- 1 teaspoon liquid seasoning, optional
- 1 tablespoon honey
- A small pinch of seasoning granules, optional
Steps:
1. Bring the water and shrimp broth cube to a boil in a pot.
2. Add the peeled hipon and cook until pink and opaque, about 2–3 minutes. Drain and set aside to cool.
3. Remove the thick peel and bitter membranes from the suha. Separate the fruit into bite-sized segments.
4. Combine the cucumber, tomato, suha, salad greens, and cooked hipon in a bowl.
5. In a separate bowl, combine the cooking oil, vinegar, garlic, mustard, calamansi juice, chili sauce, liquid seasoning, honey, and seasoning granules. Mix well.
6. Refrigerate the salad for 15 minutes.
7. Toss the salad with the dressing just before serving.
8. Top with the hard-boiled egg wedges and fried wonton strips or croutons, if using.

Short Description: A spicy, tangy Ilocano vinegar infused with garlic, chilies, and ginger.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Infusing Time: At least 3 days
Overall Time: At least 3 days 15 minutes
Allergens: None of the major common allergens listed in the recipe
Ingredients:
- 2 cups cane vinegar or coconut vinegar (480 ml)
- 1/2 cup siling labuyo or small red chilies
- 3 tablespoons ginger, sliced
- 1 head garlic, peeled
- 3 teaspoons whole peppercorns
- 1 medium onion, sliced
Steps:
1. Combine the peppercorns, ginger, garlic, onion, and chilies in a clean, dry glass bottle or jar.
2. Pour in the vinegar until the ingredients are covered.
3. Close the container tightly and shake gently to distribute the ingredients.
4. Store in a cool, safe place for at least 3 days to allow the flavors to develop. The longer it infuses, the spicier the vinegar becomes.
5. Serve as a dipping sauce for fried and grilled foods.

Short Description: A tangy dipping sauce of soy sauce and calamansi, perfect with grilled dishes.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 0 minutes
Infusing Time: 10 minutes (optional)
Overall Time: 5–15 minutes
Allergens: Soy, Wheat (depending on the soy sauce)
Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 3 tablespoons calamansi juice
- 1 siling labuyo, chopped
- 1/4 cup red onion, finely chopped
- 1 tablespoon garlic, minced
Steps:
1. Finely chop the red onion and siling labuyo, then place them in a small bowl.
2. Add the minced garlic, soy sauce, and calamansi juice.
3. Stir until everything is well combined.
4. Let the sauce sit for 10 minutes if you want the flavors to blend.
5. Serve with grilled meat, fried fish, siomai, or other dishes.

Short Description: A sweet, savory sauce made from liver and breadcrumbs, the classic partner of lechon.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 20 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kg pork liver
- 1/2 cup white vinegar (120 ml)
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium onion, chopped
- 1 cup water (240 ml)
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 1 teaspoon onion powder
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- Salt and ground black pepper, to taste
Steps:
1. Season the pork liver with salt and ground black pepper. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
2. Grill or cook the liver in a pan until completely cooked. Let it cool, then slice it into small pieces.
3. Heat the cooking oil in a pan or wok over medium heat.
4. Add the garlic and onion. Sauté until the onion softens.
5. Add the cooked liver and sauté for about 1 minute.
6. Pour in the vinegar and bring the mixture to a boil.
7. Add the brown sugar and water. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then bring the mixture to a boil again.
8. Add the breadcrumbs and simmer for about 2 minutes, stirring well.
9. Transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until smooth. Handle the hot mixture carefully and allow steam to escape safely.
10. Return the blended sauce to the pan and cook until it begins to boil again.
11. Season with salt, ground black pepper, and onion powder.
12. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve with lechon, lechon kawali, or other roasted meat.

Short Description: Juicy, savory Filipino meatballs, fried or simmered until golden.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Overall Time: 30 minutes
Ingredients:
- 1/4 kg ground pork
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- Cooking oil, for frying
Steps:
1. Combine the ground pork, onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, soy sauce, and ground black pepper in a bowl.
2. Mix until all the ingredients are evenly distributed.
3. Shape the mixture into small meatballs.
4. Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
5. Fry the meatballs in batches, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
6. Drain on a plate lined with paper towels and serve.

Short Description: Crispy fried pork belly in a rich, creamy peanut sauce with vegetables.
Cooking Time:
Preparation Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 45 minutes
Overall Time: 1 hour
Ingredients:
- 1/2 kg pork belly
- 1 sachet (8 g) MAGGI Magic Sarap
- 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
- Cooking oil, for frying
- 1 medium eggplant, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 small onion, minced
- 2 tablespoons ground rice
- 2 tablespoons ground peanuts
- 1 teaspoon atsuete seeds mixed with 2 tablespoons hot water, then strained
- 1 cup water (240 ml)
- 1/2 bunch sitaw, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/2 bunch pechay, roots removed and leaves rinsed
- Bagoong alamang, for serving
Steps:
1. Season the pork belly with half of the MAGGI Magic Sarap and the ground black pepper.
2. Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Fry the pork until golden brown and cooked through. Transfer to a rack to drain excess oil.
3. Fry the eggplant in the same oil until golden brown. Remove and drain.
4. Leave about 2 tablespoons of oil in the pan. Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
5. Add the ground rice and stir.
6. Pour in the water and bring to a simmer.
7. Gradually add the strained atsuete water until the sauce reaches your preferred color.
